Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Saṃyuttanikāyo

The Connected Discourses

Nidānavaggo

The Book of Causation

1. Nidānasaṃyuttaṃ

1. The Connected Discourses on Causation

1. Buddhavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Buddha

1. Paṭiccasamuppādasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Dependent Origination

1. Evaṃ [T 2.0001][M 1.0243][P 2.0001][V 1.0001] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “paṭiccasamuppādaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks.” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Monks, I will teach you dependent origination. Listen to it and apply your minds well; I will speak.” “So be it, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamo [V 1.0002] ca, bhikkhave, paṭiccasamuppādo? Avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ; viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ; nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ; saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso; phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā; taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo; bhavapaccayā jāti[T 2.0002]; jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, paṭiccasamuppādo.

“And what, monks, is dependent origination? With ignorance as a condition, monks, formations come to be; with formations as a condition, consciousness comes to be; with consciousness as a condition, name-and-form comes to be; with name-and-form as a condition, the six sense bases come to be; with the six sense bases as a condition, contact comes to be; with contact as a condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as a condition, craving comes to be; with craving as a condition, clinging comes to be; with clinging as a condition, existence comes to be; with existence as a condition, birth comes to be; with birth as a condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Such is the arising of this entire mass of suffering. This, monks, is called dependent origination.”

“Avijjāya [M 1.0244] tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā [P 2.0002] viññāṇanirodho; viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho; nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho; saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho; phassanirodhā vedanānirodho; vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho; taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho; upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho; bhavanirodhā jātinirodho; jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Through the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; through the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness; through the cessation of consciousness, there is the cessation of name-and-form; through the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of the six sense bases; through the cessation of the six sense bases, there is the cessation of contact; through the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling; through the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving; through the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging; through the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of existence; through the cessation of existence, there is the cessation of birth; through the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.” This is what the Blessed One said. Delighted, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One’s statement.

2. Vibhaṅgasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Analysis

2. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “paṭiccasamuppādaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi vibhajissāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

2. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Monks, I will teach you dependent origination and I will analyze it. Listen to that, attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, paṭiccasamuppādo? Avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ; viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ; nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ; saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso; phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā; taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo; bhavapaccayā jāti[T 2.0003]; jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

“And what, monks, is dependent origination? With ignorance as a condition, monks, formations arise; with formations as a condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as a condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as a condition, the sixfold sense base arises; with the sixfold sense base as a condition, contact arises; with contact as a condition, feeling arises; with feeling as a condition, craving arises; with craving as a condition, clinging arises; with clinging as a condition, existence arises; with existence as a condition, birth arises; with birth as a condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko; ayaṃ vuccati [V 1.0003] jarā. Yā tesaṃ [P 2.0003] tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo ( ) (jīvitindriyassa upacchedo) (syā. kaṃ.) evamuparipi, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana na dissati, idaṃ vuccati maraṇaṃ. Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ.

“And what, monks, is aging-and-death? Whatever, for those various beings in this or that order of beings, is aging, decrepitude, brokenness of teeth, grayness of hair, wrinkledness of skin, the decline of life, the decay of the sense faculties—this is called aging. Whatever, for those various beings from this or that order of beings, is the passing away, the act of passing away, the breaking up, the disappearance, death, dying, the completion of time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the casting off of the corpse—this is called death. Thus, this aging and this death: this, monks, is called aging-and-death.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti nibbatti abhinibbatti khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, jāti.

“And what, monks, is birth? Whatever, for those various beings in this or that order of beings, is birth, coming into being, descent, production, reproduction, the manifestation of the aggregates, the acquisition of the sense bases: this, monks, is called birth.”

“Katamo [M 1.0245] ca, bhikkhave, bhavo? Tayo me, bhikkhave, bhavā – kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhavo.

“And what, monks, is existence? There are these three kinds of existence, monks: sensual existence, form existence, and formless existence. This, monks, is called existence.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, upādānaṃ? Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, upādānāni – kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, upādānaṃ.

“And what, monks, is clinging? There are these four kinds of clinging, monks: clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rites and observances, and clinging to the doctrine of self. This, monks, is called clinging.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, taṇhā? Chayime, bhikkhave, taṇhākāyā – rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, taṇhā.

“And what, monks, is craving? There are these six classes of craving, monks: craving for forms, craving for sounds, craving for odors, craving for tastes, craving for tangible objects, and craving for mental objects. This, monks, is called craving.”

“Katamā [T 2.0004] ca, bhikkhave, vedanā? Chayime, bhikkhave, vedanākāyā – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, vedanā.

“And what, monks, is feeling? There are these six classes of feeling, monks: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This, monks, is called feeling.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, phasso? Chayime, bhikkhave, phassakāyā – cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manosamphasso. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, phasso.

“And what, monks, is contact? There are these six classes of contact, monks: eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. This, monks, is called contact.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, saḷāyatanaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saḷāyatanaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the sixfold sense base? The eye-base, the ear-base, the nose-base, the tongue-base, the body-base, and the mind-base. This, monks, is called the sixfold sense base.”

“Katamañca[V 1.0004], bhikkhave, nāmarūpaṃ? Vedanā, saññā, cetanā, phasso, manasikāro – idaṃ vuccati nāmaṃ. Cattāro ca [P 2.0004] mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, nāmarūpaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is name-and-form? Feeling, perception, volition, contact, and attention—this is called name. The four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called form. Thus, this name and this form: this, bhikkhus, is called name-and-form.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ? Chayime, bhikkhave, viññāṇakāyā – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is consciousness? There are these six classes of consciousness, bhikkhus: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. This, bhikkhus, is called consciousness.”

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā? Tayome, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā – kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā.

“And what, bhikkhus, are formations? There are these three formations, bhikkhus: the bodily formation, the verbal formation, and the mental formation. These, bhikkhus, are called formations.”

“Katamā [T 2.0005] ca, bhikkhave, avijjā? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, avijjā.

“And what, bhikkhus, is ignorance? Whatever ignorance there is, bhikkhus, concerning suffering, concerning the origin of suffering, concerning the cessation of suffering, concerning the path of practice leading to the cessation of suffering: this, bhikkhus, is called ignorance.”

“Iti [M 1.0246] kho, bhikkhave, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, formations arise; with formations as condition, consciousness arises... thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. But from the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, comes the cessation of formations; from the cessation of formations, the cessation of consciousness... thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

3. Paṭipadāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Practice

3. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “micchāpaṭipadañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi sammāpaṭipadañca. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

3. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice. Listen to it and apply your minds well; I will speak.” “So be it, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā? Avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā [V 1.0005] viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the wrong practice? With ignorance as condition, bhikkhus, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness comes to be... Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. This, bhikkhus, is called the wrong practice.

“Katamā [P 2.0005] ca, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā? Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the right practice? From the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, comes the cessation of formations; from the cessation of formations, comes the cessation of consciousness... Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. This, bhikkhus, is called the right practice.”

4. Vipassīsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Vipassī

4. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “vipassissa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa [T 2.0006] pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘kicchaṃ vatāyaṃ loko āpanno jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca. Atha ca panimassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṃ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa. Kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’”ti?

4. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, before his enlightenment, while he was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into hardship! It is born, it ages, it dies, it passes away, and it is reborn. And yet, it does not know the escape from this suffering, that is, from aging and death. When, indeed, will an escape from this suffering, from aging and death, be discerned?’”

“Atha kho bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā jarāmaraṇa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa’”nti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does aging and death come to be? What is the condition for aging and death?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When birth exists, aging and death come to be; with birth as a condition, there is aging and death.’”

“Atha [M 1.0247] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jāti hoti, kiṃpaccayā jātī’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘bhave kho sati jāti hoti, bhavapaccayā jātī’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does birth come to be? What is the condition for birth?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When becoming exists, birth comes to be; with becoming as a condition, there is birth.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati bhavo hoti, kiṃpaccayā bhavo’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā [V 1.0006] ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘upādāne kho sati bhavo hoti, upādānapaccayā bhavo’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does becoming come to be? What is the condition for becoming?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When clinging exists, becoming comes to be; with clinging as a condition, there is becoming.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati upādānaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā upādāna’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā [P 2.0006] ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘taṇhāya kho sati upādānaṃ [T 2.0007] hoti, taṇhāpaccayā upādāna’”nti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does clinging come to be? What is the condition for clinging?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When craving exists, clinging comes to be; with craving as a condition, there is clinging.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati taṇhā hoti, kiṃpaccayā taṇhā’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘vedanāya kho sati taṇhā hoti, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does craving come to be? What is the condition for craving?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When feeling exists, craving comes to be; with feeling as a condition, there is craving.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati vedanā hoti, kiṃpaccayā vedanā’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘phasse kho sati vedanā hoti, phassapaccayā vedanā’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does feeling come to be? What is the condition for feeling?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When contact exists, feeling comes to be; with contact as a condition, there is feeling.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati phasso hoti, kiṃpaccayā phasso’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saḷāyatane kho sati phasso hoti, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does contact come to be? What is the condition for contact?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When the six sense bases exist, contact comes to be; with the six sense bases as a condition, there is contact.’”

“Atha [M 1.0248] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati saḷāyatanaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā saḷāyatana’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho sati saḷāyatanaṃ hoti, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatana’”nti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists do the six sense bases come to be? What is the condition for the six sense bases?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When name-and-form exists, the six sense bases come to be; name-and-form is the condition for the six sense bases.’

“Atha [V 1.0007] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati nāmarūpaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā nāmarūpa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘viññāṇe kho sati nāmarūpaṃ hoti[T 2.0008], viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa’”nti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does name-and-form come to be? What is the condition for name-and-form?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When consciousness exists, name-and-form comes to be; consciousness is the condition for name-and-form.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati viññāṇaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā viññāṇa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saṅkhāresu kho sati viññāṇaṃ hoti, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa’”nti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists does consciousness come to be? What is the condition for consciousness?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When formations exist, consciousness comes to be; formations are the condition for consciousness.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi [P 2.0007] – ‘kimhi nu kho sati saṅkhārā honti, kiṃpaccayā saṅkhārā’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘avijjāya kho sati saṅkhārā honti, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists do formations come to be? What is the condition for formations?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When ignorance exists, formations come to be; ignorance is the condition for formations.’

“Iti hidaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. ‘Samudayo, samudayo’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

Thus, with ignorance as condition, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness… and so on… Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering. ‘Origin, Origin’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī the eye, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose clear knowing, there arose light.

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘jātiyā kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does aging and death not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of aging and death occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When birth does not exist, aging and death do not occur; with the cessation of birth, there is the cessation of aging and death.’

“Atha [M 1.0249] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati jāti na hoti[T 2.0009], kissa nirodhā jātinirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa [V 1.0008] yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘bhave kho asati jāti na hoti, bhavanirodhā jātinirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does birth not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of birth occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When becoming does not exist, birth does not occur; with the cessation of becoming, there is the cessation of birth.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati bhavo na hoti, kissa nirodhā bhavanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘upādāne kho asati bhavo na hoti, upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does becoming not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of becoming occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When clinging does not exist, becoming does not occur; with the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of becoming.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati upādānaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā upādānanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘taṇhāya kho asati upādānaṃ na hoti, taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does clinging not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of clinging occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When craving does not exist, clinging does not occur; with the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging.’

“Atha [P 2.0008] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati taṇhā na hoti, kissa nirodhā taṇhānirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘vedanāya kho asati taṇhā na hoti, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does craving not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of craving occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When feeling does not exist, craving does not occur; with the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati vedanā na hoti, kissa nirodhā vedanānirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘phasse kho asati vedanā na hoti, phassanirodhā [T 2.0010] vedanānirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does feeling not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of feeling occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When contact does not exist, feeling does not occur; with the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati phasso na hoti, kissa nirodhā phassanirodho’ti? Atha kho bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu [M 1.0250] paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saḷāyatane kho asati phasso na hoti, saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does contact not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of contact occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When the six sense bases do not exist, contact does not occur; with the cessation of the six sense bases, there is the cessation of contact.’

“Atha [V 1.0009] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati saḷāyatanaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho asati saḷāyatanaṃ na hoti, nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, do the six sense bases not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of the six sense bases occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When name-and-form does not exist, the six sense bases do not occur; with the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of the six sense bases.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati nāmarūpaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘viññāṇe kho asati nāmarūpaṃ na hoti, viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’”ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does name-and-form not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of name-and-form occur?’ Then, bhikkhus, through wise attention, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī a breakthrough of wisdom: ‘When consciousness does not exist, name-and-form does not occur; with the cessation of consciousness, there is the cessation of name-and-form.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati viññāṇaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā viññāṇanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saṅkhāresu kho asati viññāṇaṃ na hoti, saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho’”ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does consciousness not come to be? With the cessation of what does the cessation of consciousness occur?’ Then, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough of wisdom for the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When formations do not exist, consciousness does not come to be; with the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness.’

“Atha [P 2.0009] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, kissa nirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti[T 2.0011]? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘avijjāya kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’”ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, do formations not come to be? With the cessation of what does the cessation of formations occur?’ Then, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough of wisdom for the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When ignorance does not exist, formations do not come to be; with the cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of formations.’

“Iti hidaṃ avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotīti. ‘Nirodho, nirodho’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi”. Catutthaṃ.

Thus, with the cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; with the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness… and so on… Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. ‘Cessation, cessation!’—thus, monks, in regard to things unheard before, there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassī the eye, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. The fourth.

(Sattannampi buddhānaṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbo).

(This should be elaborated in the same way for all seven Buddhas.)

5. Sikhīsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Sikhī

5. Sikhissa[M 1.0251][V 1.0010], bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa…pe….

5. Monks, for Sikhī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One… and so on.

6. Vessabhūsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Vessabhū

6. Vessabhussa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa…pe….

6. Monks, for Vessabhū, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One… and so on.

7. Kakusandhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Kakusandha

7. Kakusandhassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa…pe….

7. Monks, for Kakusandha, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One… and so on.

8. Koṇāgamanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Koṇāgamana

8. Koṇāgamanassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa…pe….

8. Monks, for Koṇāgamana, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One… and so on.

9. Kassapasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Kassapa

9. Kassapassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa…pe….

9. Monks, for Kassapa, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One… and so on.

10. Gotamasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Gotama

10. “Pubbeva [P 2.0010] me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘kicchaṃ vatāyaṃ loko āpanno jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca. Atha ca panimassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṃ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa. Kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’”ti?

10. Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into hardship—it is born, it ages, it dies, it passes away, and it is reborn. And yet, it does not know the escape from this suffering, that is, from aging and death. When, indeed, will an escape from this suffering, from aging and death, be discerned?’

“Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā [V 1.0011] jarāmaraṇa’nti[T 2.0012]? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa’”nti.

To me, monks, this thought occurred: ‘When what exists does aging and death come to be? With what as condition is there aging and death?’ To me, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When birth exists, aging and death come to be. With birth as a condition, there is aging and death.’

“Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jāti hoti…pe… bhavo… upādānaṃ… taṇhā… vedanā… phasso… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhārā honti, kiṃpaccayā saṅkhārā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave[M 1.0252], yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘avijjāya kho sati saṅkhārā honti, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’”ti.

To me, monks, this thought occurred: ‘When what exists does birth come to be… does existence… does clinging… does craving… does feeling… does contact… do the six sense bases… does name-and-form… does consciousness… do formations come to be? With what as a condition are there formations?’ To me, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When ignorance exists, formations come to be. With ignorance as a condition, there are formations.’

“Iti hidaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. ‘Samudayo, samudayo’ti kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

Thus, with ignorance as a condition, formations come to be; with formations as a condition, consciousness comes to be… and so on… In this way, there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. ‘Origin, origin!’—thus, monks, regarding things unheard of before, the eye arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose.

“Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘jātiyā kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’”ti.

To me, monks, this thought occurred: ‘When what does not exist does aging and death not come to be? With the cessation of what is there the cessation of aging and death?’ To me, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When birth does not exist, aging and death does not come to be. With the cessation of birth, there is the cessation of aging and death.’

“Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho [P 2.0011] asati jāti na hoti…pe… bhavo… upādānaṃ… taṇhā… vedanā… phasso… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhārā na honti, kissa nirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu [T 2.0013] paññāya abhisamayo – ‘avijjāya kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’”ti.

To me, monks, this thought occurred: ‘When what does not exist does birth not come to be… does existence… does clinging… does craving… does feeling… does contact… do the six sense bases… do name-and-form… do consciousness… do formations not come to be? With the cessation of what is there the cessation of formations?’ To me, monks, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When ignorance does not exist, formations do not come to be. With the cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of formations.’

“Iti hidaṃ avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti. ‘Nirodho, nirodho’ti [V 1.0012] kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādī”ti. Dasamo.

Thus, with the cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; with the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness… and so on… In this way, there is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. ‘Cessation, cessation!’—thus, monks, regarding things unheard of before, the eye arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose. Tenth.

Buddhavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on the Buddhas.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Desanā vibhaṅgapaṭipadā ca,

Vipassī sikhī ca vessabhū;

Kakusandho koṇāgamano kassapo,

Mahāsakyamuni ca gotamoti.

Teaching, Analysis, and Practice; Vipassī, Sikhī, and Vessabhū; Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, and Kassapa; and the Great Sage of the Sakyans, Gotama.

2. Āhāravaggo

2. The Chapter on Nutriment

1. Āhārasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Nutriment

11. Evaṃ [T 2.0014][M 1.0253] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme…pe… etadavoca – “cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāya. Katame cattāro? Kabaḷīkāro kabaḷiṃkāro (sī. pī.), kavaḷīkāro (syā. kaṃ.) āhāro – oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṃ catutthaṃ. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāya”.

11. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Monks, there are these four nutriments for the maintenance of beings that have come to be and for the support of those seeking a new existence. What four? The nutriment of physical food, whether coarse or subtle; contact as the second; mental volition as the third; and consciousness as the fourth. These, monks, are the four nutriments for the maintenance of beings that have come to be and for the support of those seeking a new existence.’

“Ime, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā [P 2.0012] kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Ime cattāro āhārā taṇhānidānā taṇhāsamudayā taṇhājātikā taṇhāpabhavā. Taṇhā cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Taṇhā vedanānidānā vedanāsamudayā vedanājātikā [V 1.0013] vedanāpabhavā. Vedanā cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Vedanā phassanidānā phassasamudayā phassajātikā phassapabhavā. Phasso cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo? Phasso saḷāyatananidāno saḷāyatanasamudayo saḷāyatanajātiko saḷāyatanapabhavo. Saḷāyatanañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānaṃ [T 2.0015] kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpanidānaṃ nāmarūpasamudayaṃ nāmarūpajātikaṃ nāmarūpapabhavaṃ. Nāmarūpañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇanidānaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ viññāṇajātikaṃ viññāṇapabhavaṃ. Viññāṇañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Viññāṇaṃ saṅkhāranidānaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ saṅkhārajātikaṃ saṅkhārapabhavaṃ. Saṅkhārā cime, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Saṅkhārā avijjānidānā avijjāsamudayā avijjājātikā avijjāpabhavā.

“Bhikkhus, these four nutriments: what is their source, what is their origin, what is their birth, what is their provenance? These four nutriments have craving as their source, craving as their origin, craving as their birth, and craving as their provenance. And this craving, bhikkhus: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance? Craving has feeling as its source, feeling as its origin, feeling as its birth, and feeling as its provenance. And this feeling, bhikkhus: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance? Feeling has contact as its source, contact as its origin, contact as its birth, and contact as its provenance. And this contact, bhikkhus: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance? Contact has the six sense bases as its source, the six sense bases as its origin, the six sense bases as its birth, and the six sense bases as its provenance. And these six sense bases, bhikkhus: what is their source, what is their origin, what is their birth, what is their provenance? The six sense bases have name-and-form as their source, name-and-form as their origin, name-and-form as their birth, and name-and-form as their provenance. And this name-and-form, bhikkhus: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance? Name-and-form has consciousness as its source, consciousness as its origin, consciousness as its birth, and consciousness as its provenance. And this consciousness, bhikkhus: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance? Consciousness has formations as its source, formations as its origin, formations as its birth, and formations as its provenance. And these formations, bhikkhus: what is their source, what is their origin, what is their birth, what is their provenance? Formations have ignorance as their source, ignorance as their origin, ignorance as their birth, and ignorance as their provenance.”

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho [M 1.0254] …pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as a condition, formations come to be; with formations as a condition, consciousness comes to be… Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance comes the cessation of formations; with the cessation of formations, the cessation of consciousness… Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.” First.

2. Moḷiyaphaggunasuttaṃ

2. The Moḷiyaphagguna Sutta

12. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “cattārome[P 2.0013], bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāya. Katame cattāro? Kabaḷīkāro āhāro – oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṃ catutthaṃ. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāyā”ti.

12. Dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, there are these four nutriments for the maintenance of beings that have come to be and for the support of those seeking to be. What are the four? The nutriment of physical food, coarse or fine; contact is the second; mental volition is the third; and consciousness is the fourth. These, bhikkhus, are the four nutriments for the maintenance of beings that have come to be and for the support of those seeking to be.”

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, viññāṇāhāraṃ āhāretī”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca – “‘āhāretī’ti ahaṃ na vadāmi. ‘Āhāretī’ti cāhaṃ [T 2.0016] vadeyyaṃ, tatrassa kallo pañho – ‘ko nu kho, bhante, āhāretī’ti[V 1.0014]? Evaṃ cāhaṃ na vadāmi. Evaṃ maṃ avadantaṃ yo evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kissa nu kho, bhante, viññāṇāhāro’ti, esa kallo pañho. Tatra kallaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ – ‘viññāṇāhāro āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā paccayo, tasmiṃ bhūte sati saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso’”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Moḷiyaphagguna said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, who consumes the nutriment of consciousness?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “I do not say, ‘one consumes.’ If I were to say, ‘one consumes,’ then the question, ‘Venerable sir, who consumes?’ would be proper. But I do not say so. Since I do not say so, one who would ask me, ‘Venerable sir, for what is the nutriment of consciousness a condition?’ would be asking a proper question. In that case, the proper explanation is: ‘The nutriment of consciousness is a condition for future rebirth. When that exists, the six sense bases come to be; with the six sense bases as a condition, contact comes to be.’”

“Ko nu kho, bhante, phusatī”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca – “‘phusatī’ti ahaṃ na vadāmi. ‘Phusatī’ti cāhaṃ vadeyyaṃ, tatrassa kallo pañho – ‘ko nu kho, bhante, phusatī’ti? Evaṃ cāhaṃ na vadāmi. Evaṃ maṃ avadantaṃ yo evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃpaccayā nu kho, bhante, phasso’ti, esa kallo pañho. Tatra kallaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ – ‘saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā’”ti.

“Venerable sir, who has contact?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “I do not say, ‘one has contact.’ If I were to say, ‘one has contact,’ then the question, ‘Venerable sir, who has contact?’ would be proper. But I do not say so. Since I do not say so, one who would ask me, ‘Venerable sir, with what as a condition is there contact?’ would be asking a proper question. In that case, the proper explanation is: ‘With the six sense bases as a condition, contact comes to be; with contact as a condition, feeling comes to be.’”

“Ko nu kho, bhante, vedayatī”ti vediyatīti (sī. pī. ka.)? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca – “‘vedayatī’ti ahaṃ na vadāmi. ‘Vedayatī’ti cāhaṃ vadeyyaṃ, tatrassa kallo pañho – ‘ko nu kho, bhante, vedayatī’ti? Evaṃ cāhaṃ na vadāmi. Evaṃ maṃ avadantaṃ yo evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃpaccayā nu kho, bhante, vedanā’ti, esa kallo pañho. Tatra kallaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ – ‘phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’”ti.

“Venerable sir, who feels?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “I do not say, ‘one feels.’ If I were to say, ‘one feels,’ then the question, ‘Venerable sir, who feels?’ would be proper. But I do not say so. Since I do not say so, one who would ask me, ‘Venerable sir, with what as a condition is there feeling?’ would be asking a proper question. In that case, the proper explanation is: ‘With contact as a condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as a condition, craving comes to be.’”

“Ko [M 1.0255] nu kho, bhante, tasatī”ti taṇhīyatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ.)? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca – “‘tasatī’ti ahaṃ na vadāmi[P 2.0014]. ‘Tasatī’ti cāhaṃ [T 2.0017] vadeyyaṃ, tatrassa kallo pañho – ‘ko nu kho, bhante, tasatī’ti? Evaṃ cāhaṃ na vadāmi. Evaṃ maṃ avadantaṃ yo evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃpaccayā nu kho, bhante, taṇhā’ti, esa kallo pañho. Tatra kallaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ – ‘vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādāna’”nti.

“Venerable sir, who craves?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “I do not say, ‘one craves.’ If I were to say, ‘one craves,’ then the question, ‘Venerable sir, who craves?’ would be proper. But I do not say so. Since I do not say so, one who would ask me, ‘Venerable sir, with what as a condition is there craving?’ would be asking a proper question. In that case, the proper explanation is: ‘With feeling as a condition, craving comes to be; with craving as a condition, clinging comes to be.’”

“Ko nu kho, bhante, upādiyatī”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca – “‘upādiyatī’ti ahaṃ na vadāmi. ‘Upādiyatī’ti cāhaṃ vadeyyaṃ, tatrassa kallo pañho – ‘ko nu kho, bhante, upādiyatī’ti? Evaṃ cāhaṃ na vadāmi. Evaṃ maṃ avadantaṃ yo evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃpaccayā nu kho, bhante, upādāna’nti, esa kallo pañho. Tatra kallaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ [V 1.0015] – ‘taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo’ti…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

“Venerable sir, who clings?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “I do not say, ‘one clings.’ If I were to say, ‘one clings,’ then the question, ‘Venerable sir, who clings?’ would be proper. But I do not say so. Since I do not say so, one who would ask me, ‘Venerable sir, with what as a condition is there clinging?’ would be asking a proper question. In that case, the proper explanation is: ‘With craving as a condition, clinging comes to be; with clinging as a condition, existence comes to be.’ … Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

“Channaṃ tveva, phagguna, phassāyatanānaṃ asesavirāganirodhā phassanirodho; phassanirodhā vedanānirodho; vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho; taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho; upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho; bhavanirodhā jātinirodho; jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Phagguna, from the remainderless fading away and cessation of just the six bases for contact, there is the cessation of contact. From the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling. From the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving. From the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging. From the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of existence. From the cessation of existence, there is the cessation of birth. From the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. Second.

3. Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

13. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā [T 2.0018] vā jarāmaraṇaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; jātiṃ…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti[P 2.0015], na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā; na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ [M 1.0256] brāhmaññatthaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) moggallānabyākaraṇaṃ oloketabbaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

13. At Sāvatthī. … “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand aging and death, do not understand the origin of aging and death, do not understand the cessation of aging and death, do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of aging and death; who do not understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name and form… consciousness… who do not understand formations, do not understand the origin of formations, do not understand the cessation of formations, do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of formations—they are not, to me, bhikkhus, ascetics or brahmins considered ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. Nor do those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti; jātiṃ…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā; te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“But, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand aging and death, understand the origin of aging and death, understand the cessation of aging and death, understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of aging and death; who understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name and form… consciousness… who understand formations, understand the origin of formations, understand the cessation of formations, understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of formations—indeed, to me, bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins are considered ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” Third.

4. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

14. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0019][V 1.0016] viharati…pe… “ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime dhamme nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhaṃ nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti, katame dhamme nappajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ nappajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhaṃ nappajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti”?

14. At Sāvatthī. … “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand these phenomena, do not understand the origin of these phenomena, do not understand the cessation of these phenomena, do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena—what phenomena do they not understand? What is the origin of these phenomena that they do not understand? What is the cessation of these phenomena that they do not understand? What is the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena that they do not understand?”

“Jarāmaraṇaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; jātiṃ…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti. Ime dhamme nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ [P 2.0016] nirodhaṃ nappajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti. Na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

“They do not understand aging and death, they do not understand the origin of aging and death, they do not understand the cessation of aging and death, they do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of aging and death; they do not understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name and form… consciousness… they do not understand formations, they do not understand the origin of formations, they do not understand the cessation of formations, they do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of formations. They do not understand these phenomena, they do not understand the origin of these phenomena, they do not understand the cessation of these phenomena, they do not understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena. They are not, to me, bhikkhus, ascetics or brahmins considered ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. Nor do those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.”

“Ye [M 1.0257] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime dhamme pajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ pajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ [T 2.0020] nirodhaṃ pajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, katame dhamme pajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ pajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhaṃ pajānanti, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti?

“But, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand these phenomena, understand the origin of these phenomena, understand the cessation of these phenomena, understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena—what phenomena do they understand? What is the origin of these phenomena that they understand? What is the cessation of these phenomena that they understand? What is the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena that they understand?”

“Jarāmaraṇaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti; jātiṃ…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti. Ime dhamme pajānanti[V 1.0017], imesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayaṃ pajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhaṃ pajānanti, imesaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti. Te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā, brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā. Te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“They understand aging and death, they understand the origin of aging and death, they understand the cessation of aging and death, they understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of aging and death; they understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name and form… consciousness… they understand formations, they understand the origin of formations, they understand the cessation of formations, they understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of formations. They understand these phenomena, they understand the origin of these phenomena, they understand the cessation of these phenomena, they understand the path of practice leading to the cessation of these phenomena. Indeed, to me, bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins are considered ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” Fourth.

5. Kaccānagottasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse to Kaccānagotta

15. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha [P 2.0017] kho āyasmā kaccānagotto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā kaccānagotto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘sammādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhī’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sammādiṭṭhi hotī”ti?

15. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Kaccānagotta approached the Blessed One, and after approaching and paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Kaccānagotta said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said, “right view, right view.” To what extent, venerable sir, is there right view?'

“Dvayanissito [T 2.0021] khvāyaṃ, kaccāna, loko yebhuyyena – atthitañceva natthitañca. Lokasamudayaṃ kho, kaccāna, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato yā loke natthitā sā na hoti. Lokanirodhaṃ kho, kaccāna, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato yā loke atthitā sā na hoti. Upayupādānābhinivesavinibandho upāyupādānābhinivesavinibandho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) khvāyaṃ, kaccāna, loko yebhuyyena. Tañcāyaṃ upayupādānaṃ cetaso adhiṭṭhānaṃ abhinivesānusayaṃ na upeti na upādiyati nādhiṭṭhāti – ‘attā me’ti. ‘Dukkhameva uppajjamānaṃ [M 1.0258] uppajjati, dukkhaṃ nirujjhamānaṃ nirujjhatī’ti na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati aparapaccayā ñāṇamevassa ettha hoti. Ettāvatā kho, kaccāna, sammādiṭṭhi hoti.

“Kaccāna, this world for the most part relies on a duality: on existence and on non-existence. For one who sees the arising of the world as it actually is with right wisdom, that which is non-existence in the world does not exist for them. For one who sees the cessation of the world as it actually is with right wisdom, that which is existence in the world does not exist for them. Kaccāna, this world for the most part is bound by approach, clinging, and adherence. But this noble disciple does not approach, does not cling to, and does not resolve on that approach and clinging, that mental determination, adherence, and underlying tendency, with the thought: ‘My self.’ They do not doubt or become perplexed that ‘It is only suffering that arises when arising; it is suffering that ceases when ceasing.’ Knowledge about this arises for them independent of another. To this extent, Kaccāna, there is right view.

“‘Sabbaṃ atthī’ti kho, kaccāna, ayameko anto. ‘Sabbaṃ natthī’ti ayaṃ dutiyo anto. Ete te, kaccāna, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī’”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“‘Everything exists,’ Kaccāna, is one extreme. ‘Everything does not exist,’ is a second extreme. Without approaching either of these two extremes, Kaccāna, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With ignorance as a condition, formations come to be; with formations as a condition, consciousness comes to be… Thus is the arising of this whole mass of suffering. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; with the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness… Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’”

6. Dhammakathikasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Dhamma-Teacher

16. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0018][P 2.0018] …pe… atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘dhammakathiko [T 2.0022] dhammakathiko’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhammakathiko hotī”ti?

16. At Sāvatthī... Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, and after approaching and paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said, “a Dhamma-teacher, a Dhamma-teacher.” To what extent, venerable sir, is one a Dhamma-teacher?'

“Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṃ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāya. Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāya. Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāya.

“Bhikkhu, if one teaches the Dhamma for disenchantment with, for dispassion towards, and for the cessation of aging and death, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu who is a Dhamma-teacher.' Bhikkhu, if one is practicing for disenchantment with, for dispassion towards, and for the cessation of aging and death, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu practicing in accordance with the Dhamma.' Bhikkhu, if, through disenchantment with, dispassion towards, and cessation of aging and death, one is liberated without clinging, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu who has attained Nibbāna in this very life.'

“Jātiyā ce bhikkhu…pe… bhavassa ce bhikkhu… upādānassa ce bhikkhu… taṇhāya ce bhikkhu… vedanāya ce bhikkhu… phassassa ce bhikkhu… saḷāyatanassa ce bhikkhu… nāmarūpassa ce bhikkhu… viññāṇassa ce bhikkhu… saṅkhārānaṃ ce bhikkhu… avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṃ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāya. Avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāya. Avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāyā”ti.

“Bhikkhu, if one teaches the Dhamma for disenchantment with, for dispassion towards, and for the cessation of birth... of existence... of clinging... of craving... of feeling... of contact... of the six sense bases... of name-and-form... of consciousness... of formations... of ignorance, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu who is a Dhamma-teacher.' Bhikkhu, if one is practicing for disenchantment with, for dispassion towards, and for the cessation of ignorance, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu practicing in accordance with the Dhamma.' Bhikkhu, if, through disenchantment with, dispassion towards, and cessation of ignorance, one is liberated without clinging, it is fitting to call them a 'bhikkhu who has attained Nibbāna in this very life.'”

7. Acelakassapasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse to Kassapa the Naked Ascetic

17. Evaṃ [M 1.0259] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha [P 2.0019] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā [V 1.0019] kho acelo kassapo [T 2.0023] bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho acelo kassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “puccheyyāma mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ kañcideva kiñcideva (ka.) desaṃ, sace no bhavaṃ gotamo okāsaṃ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti.

17. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Rājagaha for alms. The naked ascetic Kassapa saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the naked ascetic Kassapa said this to the Blessed One: “We would ask the Venerable Gotama about a certain matter, if the Venerable Gotama would grant us the opportunity for an explanation of the question.”

“Akālo kho tāva, kassapa, pañhassa; antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhamhā”ti. Dutiyampi kho acelo kassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca “puccheyyāma mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ kañcideva desaṃ, sace no bhavaṃ gotamo okāsaṃ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti. “Akālo kho tāva, kassapa, pañhassa; antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhamhā”ti. Tatiyampi kho acelo kassapo…pe… antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhamhāti. Evaṃ vutte, acelo kassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “na kho pana mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ bahudeva pucchitukāmā”ti. “Puccha, kassapa, yadākaṅkhasī”ti.

“For now, Kassapa, is not the time for a question; we have entered among the houses.” For a second time, the naked ascetic Kassapa said this to the Blessed One: “We would ask the Venerable Gotama about a certain matter, if the Venerable Gotama would grant us the opportunity for an explanation of the question.” “For now, Kassapa, is not the time for a question; we have entered among the houses.” For a third time, the naked ascetic Kassapa… we have entered among the houses. When this was said, the naked ascetic Kassapa said this to the Blessed One: “Indeed, we do not wish to ask the Venerable Gotama very much.” “Ask, Kassapa, what you wish.”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘sayaṃkataṃ dukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, paraṃkataṃ dukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca dukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ [P 2.0020] pana bho gotama, asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ dukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ nu [T 2.0024] kho, bho gotama, natthi dukkha’nti? ‘Na kho, kassapa, natthi dukkhaṃ. Atthi kho, kassapa, dukkha’nti. ‘Tena hi bhavaṃ gotamo dukkhaṃ na jānāti, na passatī’ti. ‘Na khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkhaṃ na jānāmi, na passāmi. Jānāmi khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkhaṃ; passāmi khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkha’”nti.

“Venerable Gotama, is suffering self-made?” “Do not say so, Kassapa,” said the Blessed One. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering made by another?” “Do not say so, Kassapa,” said the Blessed One. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering both self-made and made by another?” “Do not say so, Kassapa,” said the Blessed One. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering not made by self, not made by another, and arisen without cause?” “Do not say so, Kassapa,” said the Blessed One. “Then, Venerable Gotama, does suffering not exist?” “It is not so, Kassapa, that suffering does not exist. Suffering does indeed exist, Kassapa.” “In that case, the Venerable Gotama does not know suffering, does not see suffering.” “It is not so, Kassapa, that I do not know suffering, nor that I do not see it. I indeed know suffering, Kassapa; I indeed see suffering, Kassapa.”

“Ki nu kho, bho gotama, ‘sayaṃkataṃ dukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, paraṃkataṃ dukkha’nti iti [M 1.0260] puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca dukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ dukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, kassapā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi dukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho, kassapa, natthi dukkhaṃ[V 1.0020], atthi kho, kassapa, dukkha’nti vadesi. ‘Tena hi bhavaṃ gotamo dukkhaṃ na jānāti na passatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkhaṃ na jānāmi na passāmi. Jānāmi khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkhaṃ; passāmi khvāhaṃ, kassapa, dukkha’nti vadesi. Ācikkhatu ca ayaṃ cakāro sī. potthake natthi me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhaṃ. Desetu ca ayaṃ cakāro sī. potthake natthi me, bhante, bhagavā dukkha”nti.

“Venerable Gotama, when asked, ‘Is suffering self-made?’ you say, ‘Do not say so, Kassapa.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering made by another?’ you say, ‘Do not say so, Kassapa.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering both self-made and made by another?’ you say, ‘Do not say so, Kassapa.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, is suffering not made by self, not made by another, and arisen without cause?’ you say, ‘Do not say so, Kassapa.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, does suffering not exist?’ you say, ‘It is not so, Kassapa, that suffering does not exist. Suffering does indeed exist, Kassapa.’ When asked, ‘In that case, the Venerable Gotama does not know suffering, does not see suffering,’ you say, ‘It is not so, Kassapa, that I do not know suffering, nor that I do not see it. I indeed know suffering, Kassapa; I indeed see suffering, Kassapa.’ Venerable sir, may the Blessed One declare suffering to me. May the Blessed One teach suffering to me.”

“‘So karoti so paṭisaṃvedayatī’ti paṭisaṃvediyatīti (sī. pī. ka.) kho, kassapa, ādito sato ‘sayaṃkataṃ dukkha’nti iti vadaṃ sassataṃ etaṃ pareti. ‘Añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedayatī’ti kho, kassapa, vedanābhitunnassa sato ‘paraṃkataṃ dukkha’nti [T 2.0025] iti vadaṃ ucchedaṃ etaṃ pareti. Ete te, kassapa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā [P 2.0021] saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī’”ti.

“Kassapa, one who says, ‘The one who acts is the one who experiences,’ holding from the outset that ‘suffering is self-made,’ falls into this eternalism. Kassapa, one who says, ‘One acts, another experiences,’ being afflicted by feeling and holding that ‘suffering is made by another,’ falls into this annihilationism. Without approaching either of these two extremes, Kassapa, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle way: ‘With ignorance as a condition, formations come to be; with formations as a condition, consciousness… and so on. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. But with the complete fading away and cessation of ignorance, formations cease; with the cessation of formations, consciousness ceases… and so on. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’”

Evaṃ vutte, acelo kassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya…pe… cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

When this was said, the naked ascetic Kassapa said this to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, venerable sir! Magnificent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned… and so on… or hold up an oil lamp so that those with eyes might see forms; in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. I, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May I, venerable sir, receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence; may I receive the full ordination.”

“Yo kho, kassapa, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena accayena parivuṭṭhaparivāsaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) (parivutthaparivāsaṃ) āraddhacittā bhikkhū bhikkhū ākaṅkhamānā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mayā puggalavemattatā viditā”ti.

“Kassapa, one who was formerly a follower of another sect and who desires the going forth and the full ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline lives on probation for four months. After the passing of four months, the bhikkhus, being of pleased minds, give the going forth and the full ordination for the state of a bhikkhu. However, the distinction among individuals is known by me.”

“Sace[M 1.0261], bhante, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena accayena parivuṭṭhaparivāsaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) (parivutthaparivāsaṃ) āraddhacittā bhikkhū bhikkhū ākaṅkhamānā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi[T 2.0026][V 1.0021], catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena accayena parivuṭṭhaparivāsaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) (parivutthaparivāsaṃ) āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā”ti.

“Venerable sir, if someone who was formerly a follower of another sect desires the going forth in this Dhamma and Discipline, and desires the higher ordination, they undergo probation for four months. After the passing of four months, the bhikkhus, being of pleased minds, may give the going forth and the higher ordination for the state of a bhikkhu. I will undergo probation for four years. After the passing of four years, may the bhikkhus, being of pleased minds, give me the going forth and the higher ordination for the state of a bhikkhu.”

Alattha kho acelo kassapo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā kassapo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya [P 2.0022] kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā kassapo arahataṃ ahosīti. Sattamaṃ.

The naked ascetic Kassapa received the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence; he received the higher ordination. And not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Kassapa, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, soon realized for himself with direct knowledge that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having made it manifest, he dwelled having attained it in this very life. He understood: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.” And the Venerable Kassapa became one of the arahants. The Seventh.

8. Timbarukasuttaṃ

8. The Timbaruka Sutta

18. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha kho timbaruko paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho timbaruko paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

18. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the wanderer Timbaruka approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Timbaruka said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkataṃ sukhadukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, paraṃkataṃ sukhadukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca sukhadukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkha’nti? ‘Mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti bhagavā avoca[T 2.0027]. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi sukhadukkha’nti? ‘Na kho, timbaruka, natthi sukhadukkhaṃ; atthi kho, timbaruka, sukhadukkha’nti. ‘Tena hi bhavaṃ gotamo sukhadukkhaṃ na jānāti, na passatī’ti? ‘Na khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṃ na jānāmi, na passāmi. Jānāmi khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṃ; passāmi khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkha’”nti.

“Venerable Gotama, is happiness and suffering self-made?” “Do not say so, Timbaruka,” the Blessed One said. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is happiness and suffering made by another?” “Do not say so, Timbaruka,” the Blessed One said. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is happiness and suffering both self-made and made by another?” “Do not say so, Timbaruka,” the Blessed One said. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is happiness and suffering not self-made, not other-made, and arisen without a cause?” “Do not say so, Timbaruka,” the Blessed One said. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is there no happiness and suffering?” “It is not, Timbaruka, that there is no happiness and suffering; there is indeed happiness and suffering, Timbaruka.” “In that case, does the Venerable Gotama not know or see happiness and suffering?” “It is not, Timbaruka, that I do not know or see happiness and suffering. I know happiness and suffering, Timbaruka; I see happiness and suffering, Timbaruka.”

“‘Kiṃ [M 1.0262] nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkataṃ sukhadukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ [P 2.0023] pana, bho gotama, paraṃkataṃ sukhadukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā [V 1.0022] hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca sukhadukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṃ, timbarukā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi sukhadukkha’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho, timbaruka, natthi sukhadukkhaṃ; atthi kho, timbaruka, sukhadukkha’nti vadesi. ‘Tena hi bhavaṃ gotamo sukhadukkhaṃ na jānāti, na passatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṃ na jānāmi, na passāmi. Jānāmi khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṃ; passāmi khvāhaṃ, timbaruka, sukhadukkha’nti vadesi. Ācikkhatu ca me bhavaṃ gotamo sukhadukkhaṃ. Desetu ca me bhavaṃ gotamo sukhadukkha”nti.
