Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu diṭṭhisampanno itipi, dassanasampanno itipi, āgato imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, passati imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, sekkhena ñāṇena samannāgato itipi, sekkhāya vijjāya samannāgato itipi, dhammasotaṃ samāpanno itipi, ariyo nibbedhikapañño itipi, amatadvāraṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati itipī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu thus understands aging-and-death, thus understands the origin of aging-and-death, thus understands the cessation of aging-and-death, thus understands the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death; thus understands birth... becoming... clinging... craving... feeling... contact... the sixfold sense base... name-and-form... consciousness... formations... the origin of formations... the cessation of formations... thus understands the path leading to the cessation of formations—this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is called one accomplished in view, one accomplished in vision, one who has come to this good Dhamma, one who sees this good Dhamma, one endowed with the trainee's knowledge, one endowed with the trainee's true knowledge, one who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrating wisdom, one who stands having reached the door to the Deathless.”

9. Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

29. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “tatra kho…pe… ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā [V 1.0041] vā jarāmaraṇaṃ na parijānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ na parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ na parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na parijānanti, jātiṃ na parijānanti…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre… saṅkhārasamudayaṃ… saṅkhāranirodhaṃ… saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na parijānanti. Na mete, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā. Na ca panete [M 1.0280] āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme [T 2.0054] sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti”.

29. At Sāvatthī... There... “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not fully comprehend aging and death, do not fully comprehend the origin of aging and death, do not fully comprehend the cessation of aging and death, do not fully comprehend the path leading to the cessation of aging and death; do not fully comprehend birth... becoming... clinging... craving... feeling... contact... the six sense bases... name-and-form... consciousness... formations... the origin of formations... the cessation of formations... the path leading to the cessation of formations—these, Bhikkhus, are not considered ascetics among ascetics, nor brahmins among brahmins. And these venerable ones do not, in this very life, having realized it for themselves through higher knowledge, dwell having attained the state of an ascetic or the state of a brahmin.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ parijānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ parijānanti, jātiṃ parijānanti…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre parijānanti[P 2.0046], saṅkhārasamudayaṃ parijānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ parijānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ parijānanti. Te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā. Te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins fully comprehend aging and death, fully comprehend the origin of aging and death, fully comprehend the cessation of aging and death, and fully comprehend the path leading to the cessation of aging and death; who fully comprehend birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name-and-form… consciousness… and formations; who fully comprehend the origin of formations, fully comprehend the cessation of formations, and fully comprehend the path leading to the cessation of formations—these ascetics and brahmins, Bhikkhus, are considered ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And these venerable ones, in this very life, having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, enter upon and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” The Ninth.

10. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

30. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “tatra kho…pe… ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti te vata jarāmaraṇaṃ samatikkamma ṭhassantīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Jātiṃ nappajānanti…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti te vata saṅkhāre samatikkamma ṭhassantīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati”.

30. At Sāvatthī… There… “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand aging and death, do not understand the origin of aging and death, do not understand the cessation of aging and death, and do not understand the path leading to the cessation of aging and death—that they will transcend aging and death is impossible. They do not understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name-and-form… consciousness… formations; they do not understand the origin of formations, do not understand the cessation of formations, and do not understand the path leading to the cessation of formations—that they will transcend formations is impossible.”

“Ye [T 2.0055][V 1.0042] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti te vata jarāmaraṇaṃ samatikkamma ṭhassantīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Jātiṃ pajānanti…pe… bhavaṃ… upādānaṃ… taṇhaṃ… vedanaṃ… phassaṃ… saḷāyatanaṃ… nāmarūpaṃ… viññāṇaṃ… saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti. Te vata saṅkhāre samatikkamma ṭhassantīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand aging and death, understand the origin of aging and death, understand the cessation of aging and death, and understand the path leading to the cessation of aging and death—that they will transcend aging and death is possible. They understand birth… existence… clinging… craving… feeling… contact… the six sense bases… name-and-form… consciousness… formations; they understand the origin of formations, understand the cessation of formations, and understand the path leading to the cessation of formations—that they will transcend formations is possible.” The Tenth.

Dasabalavaggo [P 2.0047] tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Ten Powers, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Dve [M 1.0281] dasabalā upanisā ca, aññatitthiyabhūmijo;

Upavāṇo paccayo bhikkhu, dve ca samaṇabrāhmaṇāti.

Two on the Ten Powers, Upanisā, Aññatitthiya, and Bhūmija; Upavāṇa, Paccaya, Bhikkhu, and two on Ascetics and Brahmins.

4. Kaḷārakhattiyavaggo

4. The Chapter on Kaḷāra the Khattiya

1. Bhūtasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on What Has Come to Be

31. Ekaṃ [T 2.0056] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “vuttamidaṃ, sāriputta, pārāyane pārāyaṇe (sī.) ajitapañhe –

31. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Sāriputta, this was said in the Pārāyana, in Ajita’s Questions—

“Ye ca saṅkhātadhammāse, ye ca sekkhā puthū idha;

Tesaṃ me nipako iriyaṃ, puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisā”ti.

‘Venerable sir, there are those here who have comprehended the Dhamma, and also the many trainees. Being asked by me about their conduct, you who are wise, please explain it to me.’

“Imassa nu kho, sāriputta, saṃkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti? Evaṃ [V 1.0043] vutte, āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi…pe… dutiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “vuttamidaṃ, sāriputta, pārāyane ajitapañhe –

“Now, Sāriputta, how should the meaning of this statement, spoken in brief, be understood in detail?” When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta remained silent. A second time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta… and a second time the Venerable Sāriputta remained silent. A third time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Sāriputta, this was said in the Pārāyana, in Ajita’s Questions—

“Ye ca saṅkhātadhammāse, ye ca sekkhā puthū idha;

Tesaṃ me nipako iriyaṃ, puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisā”ti.

‘Venerable sir, there are those here who have comprehended the Dhamma, and also the many trainees. Being asked by me about their conduct, you who are wise, please explain it to me.’

“Imassa [P 2.0048] nu kho, sāriputta, saṃkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti? Tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi.

“Now, Sāriputta, how should the meaning of this statement, spoken in brief, be understood in detail?” For a third time, the Venerable Sāriputta remained silent.

“Bhūtamidanti, sāriputta, passasī”ti? Bhūtamidanti, bhante, yathābhūtaṃ [T 2.0057] sammappaññāya passati. Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno [M 1.0282] hoti. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhante, sekkho hoti.

“Do you see, Sāriputta, ‘This has come to be’?” “Venerable sir, one sees ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what has come to be. One sees ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what has originated from nutriment. One sees ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what is subject to cessation. In this way, venerable sir, one is a trainee.”

“Kathañca, bhante, saṅkhātadhammo hoti? Bhūtamidanti, bhante, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā [P 2.0049] anupādā vimutto hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhante, saṅkhātadhammo hoti. Iti kho, bhante, yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ pārāyane ajitapañhe –

“And how, venerable sir, is one of comprehended Dhamma? Venerable sir, one sees ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what has come to be. One sees ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what has originated from nutriment. One sees ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what is subject to cessation. In this way, venerable sir, one is of comprehended Dhamma. Thus, venerable sir, it was stated in the Pārāyana, in Ajita’s Questions—

“Ye [T 2.0058][V 1.0044] ca saṅkhātadhammāse, ye ca sekkhā puthū idha;

Tesaṃ me nipako iriyaṃ, puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisā”ti.

‘Venerable sir, there are those here who have comprehended the Dhamma, and also the many trainees. Being asked by me about their conduct, you who are wise, please explain it to me.’

“Imassa khvāhaṃ, bhante, saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“Venerable sir, I understand the meaning of this statement, spoken in brief, in detail in this way.”

“Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, bhūtamidanti, sāriputta, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭippanno hoti. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Evaṃ kho, sāriputta, sekkho hoti.

“Good, good, Sāriputta! Sāriputta, one sees ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what has come to be. One sees ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what has originated from nutriment. One sees ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is, one practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, and for cessation regarding what is subject to cessation. In this way, Sāriputta, one is a trainee.

“Kathañca, sāriputta, saṅkhātadhammo hoti? Bhūtamidanti, sāriputta, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā [M 1.0283] bhūtassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti. Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Tadāhāranirodhā [T 2.0059] yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññā [P 2.0050] disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti. Evaṃ kho, sāriputta, saṅkhātadhammo hoti. Iti kho, sāriputta, yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ pārāyane ajitapañhe –

“And how, Sāriputta, is one of comprehended Dhamma? Sāriputta, one sees ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘This has come to be’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what has come to be. One sees ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘It has originated from nutriment’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what has originated from nutriment. One sees ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is. Having seen ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation’ with right wisdom as it really is, through disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation, one is liberated without clinging regarding what is subject to cessation. In this way, Sāriputta, one is of comprehended Dhamma. Thus, Sāriputta, it was stated in the Pārāyana, in Ajita’s Questions—

“Ye ca saṅkhātadhammāse, ye ca sekkhā puthū idha;

Tesaṃ me nipako iriyaṃ, puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisā”ti.

‘Venerable sir, there are those here who have comprehended the Dhamma, and also the many trainees. Being asked by me about their conduct, you who are wise, please explain it to me.’

“Imassa kho sāriputta saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Sāriputta, the meaning of this statement, spoken in brief, should indeed be understood in detail in this way.”

2. Kaḷārasuttaṃ

2. The Kaḷāra Sutta

32. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0045] viharati. Atha kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “moḷiyaphagguno, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattoti. Na hi nūna so āyasmā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye assāsamalatthāti. Tena hāyasmā sāriputto imasmiṃ dhammavinaye assāsaṃ patto”ti?

32. He was dwelling in Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. Having concluded the talk that was joyful and memorable, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: 'Friend Sāriputta, the bhikkhu Moḷiyaphagguna has renounced the training and reverted to the low life. Surely, that venerable one did not obtain solace in this Dhamma and Discipline. Then, has the Venerable Sāriputta attained solace in this Dhamma and Discipline?'

“Na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, kaṅkhāmī”ti. “Āyatiṃ, panāvuso”ti?

“Friend, I have no doubt.” “But in the future, friend?”

“Na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, vicikicchāmī”ti.

“Friend, I have no uncertainty.”

Atha kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi[T 2.0060]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ [P 2.0051] etadavoca – “āyasmatā, bhante, sāriputtena aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti.

Then the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya rose from his seat, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the Venerable Sāriputta has declared final knowledge thus: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state.’”

Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena sāriputtaṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso sāriputta, āmantetī’”ti[M 1.0284]. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “satthā taṃ, āvuso sāriputta, āmantetī”ti. “Evaṃ, āvuso”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira tayā, sāriputta, aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti? “Na kho, bhante, etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi attho attho ca (syā. kaṃ. ka.) vutto”ti. “Yena kenacipi, sāriputta, pariyāyena kulaputto aññaṃ byākaroti, atha kho byākataṃ byākatato daṭṭhabba”nti. “Nanu ahampi[V 1.0046], bhante, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘na kho, bhante, etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi attho vutto’”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain bhikkhu: “Come, bhikkhu, in my name call Sāriputta, saying: ‘The Teacher calls you, friend Sāriputta.’” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” that bhikkhu replied to the Blessed One. Having assented, he went to the Venerable Sāriputta and said: “The Teacher calls you, friend Sāriputta.” “Yes, friend,” the Venerable Sāriputta replied to that bhikkhu. Then he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Is it true, Sāriputta, as has been heard, that you have declared final knowledge thus: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state’?” “Venerable Sir, the meaning was not stated with these words and with these phrases.” “Sāriputta, in whatever way a clansman declares final knowledge, what is declared should be understood as declared.” “But did I not also say, Venerable Sir: ‘Venerable Sir, the meaning was not stated with these words and with these phrases’?”

“Sace taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ jānatā pana tayā, āvuso sāriputta, kathaṃ passatā aññā [T 2.0061] byākatā – khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti?

“Sāriputta, if they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, knowing how, seeing how, have you declared final knowledge thus: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state”?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?”

“Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ jānatā pana tayā, āvuso sāriputta, kathaṃ passatā aññā byākatā – khīṇā [P 2.0052] jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti; evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), puṭṭhāhaṃ (pī. ka.), bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘yaṃnidānā, āvuso, jāti, tassa nidānassa khayā khīṇasmiṃ khīṇāmhīti viditaṃ. Khīṇāmhīti viditvā – khīṇājāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“Venerable Sir, if they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, knowing how, seeing how, have you declared final knowledge thus: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state”?’—being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, whatever is the cause of birth, through the destruction of that cause it is known to me: “When that is destroyed, I am one for whom it is destroyed.” Knowing, “I am one for whom it is destroyed,” I know that: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state.”’ Being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sace pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘jāti panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho taṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘jāti panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘jāti kho, āvuso, bhavanidānā bhavasamudayā [M 1.0285] bhavajātikā bhavappabhavā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“But if they were to ask you, Sāriputta: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of birth, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?” “Venerable Sir, if they were to ask me: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of birth, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, birth has becoming as its basis, becoming as its origin, becoming as its source, and becoming as its provenance.’ Being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sace pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘bhavo panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘bhavo panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo’ti[T 2.0062]? Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘bhavo kho, āvuso, upādānanidāno upādānasamudayo upādānajātiko upādānappabhavo’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“If they were to ask you, Sāriputta: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of becoming, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?” “Venerable Sir, if they were to ask me: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of becoming, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, becoming has clinging as its basis, clinging as its origin, clinging as its source, and clinging as its provenance.’ Being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sace [V 1.0047] pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘upādānaṃ panāvuso…pe… sace pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – taṇhā panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace [P 2.0053] maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – taṇhā panāvuso sāriputta, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘taṇhā kho, āvuso, vedanānidānā vedanāsamudayā vedanājātikā vedanāpabhavā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“But if, Sāriputta, they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of craving, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?” “Venerable Sir, if they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, what is the basis of craving, what is its origin, what is its source, what is its provenance?’—being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, craving has feeling as its basis, feeling as its origin, feeling as its source, and feeling as its provenance.’ Being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sace [T 2.0063] pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ jānato pana te, āvuso sāriputta, kathaṃ passato yā vedanāsu nandī sā na upaṭṭhāsī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ jānato pana te, āvuso sāriputta, kathaṃ passato yā vedanāsu nandī sā na upaṭṭhāsī’ti evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘tisso kho imā, āvuso, vedanā. Katamā tisso? Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Imā kho, āvuso, tisso vedanā aniccā. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhanti viditaṃ viditā (ṭīkā), yā vedanāsu nandī sā na upaṭṭhāsī’ti. Evaṃ, puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“But if, Sāriputta, they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, knowing how, seeing how, does the delight in feelings not arise for you?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?” “Venerable Sir, if they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, knowing how, seeing how, does the delight in feelings not arise for you?’—being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Friends, these three feelings are impermanent. When it is known that whatever is impermanent is suffering, the delight in feelings does not arise.’ Being asked thus, Venerable Sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta. Ayampi kho, sāriputta, pariyāyo, etasseva atthassa saṃkhittena veyyākaraṇāya – ‘yaṃ kiñci vedayitaṃ taṃ dukkhasmi’”nti.

“Good, good, Sāriputta. This too, Sāriputta, is a way of explaining this same meaning in brief: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’”

“Sace [M 1.0286] pana taṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ vimokkhā pana tayā, āvuso sāriputta, aññā byākatā – khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, sāriputta, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti? “Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃ vimokkhā pana tayā, āvuso sāriputta, aññā byākatā [T 2.0064] – khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘ajjhattaṃ [P 2.0054] vimokkhā khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbupādānakkhayā tathā sato viharāmi yathā sataṃ viharantaṃ āsavā nānussavanti, attānañca nāvajānāmī’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhohaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyya”nti.

“But if, Sāriputta, they were to ask you thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, by what liberation have you declared final knowledge, saying: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state”?’—being asked thus, Sāriputta, how would you answer?” “Venerable sir, if they were to ask me thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, by what liberation have you declared final knowledge, saying: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state”?’—being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer thus: ‘Friends, I am one who is internally liberated through the destruction of all clinging. I dwell mindful in such a way that, as I am dwelling mindfully, the taints do not flow in, and I do not disparage myself.’ Being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer in this way.”

“Sādhu [V 1.0048] sādhu, sāriputta. Ayampi kho sāriputta, pariyāyo etasseva atthassa saṃkhittena veyyākaraṇāya – ye āsavā samaṇena vuttā tesvāhaṃ na kaṅkhāmi, te me pahīnāti na vicikicchāmī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvā sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

“Good, good, Sāriputta. This too, Sāriputta, is a way of explaining this same meaning in brief: ‘Regarding the taints spoken of by the Ascetic, I have no doubt; I am not perplexed that they have been abandoned by me.’” This is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Sugata rose from his seat and entered the monastery.

Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto acirapakkantassa bhagavato bhikkhū āmantesi – “pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi, tassa me ahosi dandhāyitattaṃ. Yato ca kho me, āvuso, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ anumodi, tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – divasaṃ cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, divasampāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi. Rattiṃ cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, rattimpāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi. Rattindivaṃ rattidivaṃ (ka.) cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi[T 2.0065], rattindivampāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi. Dve [P 2.0055] rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya…pe… dve rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ…pe… tīṇi rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya…pe… tīṇi rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ…pe… cattāri rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya…pe… cattāri rattindivānipāhaṃ [M 1.0287] bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ…pe… pañca rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya…pe… pañca rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ…pe… cha rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya…pe… cha rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ…pe… satta rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, satta rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehī”ti.

Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the monks: 'Friends, the Blessed One asked me the first question without prior notice, and for me, there was a slowness in answering. But friends, from the moment the Blessed One approved of my first answer, this thought occurred to me: “If the Blessed One were to question me on this matter for a whole day with different words and different methods, I could also answer the Blessed One on this matter for a whole day with different words and different methods. If for a whole night… a whole day and night… two days and nights… three days and nights… four days and nights… five days and nights… six days and nights… if for seven days and nights the Blessed One were to question me on this matter with different words and different methods, I could also answer the Blessed One on this matter for seven days and nights with different words and different methods.”'

Atha kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kaḷārakhattiyo bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āyasmatā, bhante, sāriputtena sīhanādo nadito – pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi, tassa me ahosi dandhāyitattaṃ. Yato [V 1.0049] ca kho me, āvuso, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ anumodi[T 2.0066], tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – divasaṃ cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, divasampāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi; rattiṃ cepi…pe… rattindivaṃ cepi maṃ bhagavā…pe… dve rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā…pe… tīṇi… cattāri… pañca… cha… satta rattindivāni cepi maṃ bhagavā etamatthaṃ puccheyya [P 2.0056] aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, satta rattindivānipāhaṃ bhagavato etamatthaṃ byākareyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehī”ti.

Then the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya rose from his seat, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the bhikkhu Kaḷārakhattiya said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the venerable Sāriputta has uttered a lion’s roar, saying: ‘Friends, the Blessed One asked me the first question without prior notice, and for me, there was a slowness in answering. But friends, from the moment the Blessed One approved of my first answer, this thought occurred to me: “If the Blessed One were to question me on this matter for a whole day with different words and different methods, I could also answer the Blessed One on this matter for a whole day with different words and different methods. If for a whole night… a whole day and night… two days and nights… three… four… five… six… if for seven days and nights the Blessed One were to question me on this matter with different words and different methods, I could also answer the Blessed One on this matter for seven days and nights with different words and different methods.”’”

“Sā hi, bhikkhu, sāriputtassa dhammadhātu suppaṭividdhā, yassā dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā divasaṃ cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, divasampi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi. Rattiṃ cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, rattimpi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya…pe… rattindivaṃ cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, rattindivampi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya… dve rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, dve rattindivānipi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya… tīṇi rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, tīṇi rattindivānipi [T 2.0067] me sāriputto etamatthaṃ [M 1.0288] byākareyya… cattāri rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, cattāri rattindivānipi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya… pañca rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, pañca rattindivānipi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya… cha rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ, cha rattindivānipi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya… satta rattindivāni cepāhaṃ sāriputtaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyaṃ aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehi, satta rattindivānipi me sāriputto etamatthaṃ byākareyya aññamaññehi padehi aññamaññehi pariyāyehī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“For, bhikkhu, that Dhamma element has been well penetrated by Sāriputta. Because of the well-penetration of that Dhamma element, if I were to question Sāriputta on this matter for a day, using different terms and different approaches, Sāriputta could explain this matter to me for a day, using different terms and different approaches. If I were to question him on this matter for a night … for a day and a night … for two days and nights … for three days and nights … for four days and nights … for five days and nights … for six days and nights … if I were to question Sāriputta on this matter for seven days and nights, using different terms and different approaches, Sāriputta could explain this matter to me for seven days and nights, using different terms and different approaches.” The Second.

3. Ñāṇavatthusuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Objects of Knowledge

33. Sāvatthiyaṃ…pe… “catucattārīsaṃ vo, bhikkhave, ñāṇavatthūni desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ [V 1.0050] manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

33. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, I will teach you the forty-four objects of knowledge. Listen to that and pay careful attention. I will speak.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamāni katamāni ca (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), bhikkhave, catucattārīsaṃ ñāṇavatthūni? Jarāmaraṇe [P 2.0057] ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ; jātiyā ñāṇaṃ, jātisamudaye ñāṇaṃ, jātinirodhe ñāṇaṃ, jātinirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ; bhave ñāṇaṃ, bhavasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, bhavanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, bhavanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ; upādāne ñāṇaṃ, upādānasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, upādānanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, upādānanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya [T 2.0068] ñāṇaṃ; taṇhāya ñāṇaṃ, taṇhāsamudaye ñāṇaṃ, taṇhānirodhe ñāṇaṃ, taṇhānirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ; vedanāya ñāṇaṃ, vedanāsamudaye ñāṇaṃ, vedanānirodhe ñāṇaṃ, vedanānirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ; phasse ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatane ñāṇaṃ… nāmarūpe ñāṇaṃ… viññāṇe ñāṇaṃ… saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhārasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhe ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Imāni vuccanti, bhikkhave, catucattārīsaṃ ñāṇavatthūni.

“And what, monks, are the forty-four objects of knowledge? Knowledge in aging and death, knowledge in the origin of aging and death, knowledge in the cessation of aging and death, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death; knowledge in birth, knowledge in the origin of birth, knowledge in the cessation of birth, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of birth; knowledge in existence, knowledge in the origin of existence, knowledge in the cessation of existence, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of existence; knowledge in clinging, knowledge in the origin of clinging, knowledge in the cessation of clinging, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of clinging; knowledge in craving, knowledge in the origin of craving, knowledge in the cessation of craving, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of craving; knowledge in feeling, knowledge in the origin of feeling, knowledge in the cessation of feeling, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of feeling; knowledge in contact… knowledge in the six sense bases… knowledge in name-and-form… knowledge in consciousness… knowledge in formations, knowledge in the origin of formations, knowledge in the cessation of formations, knowledge in the practice leading to the cessation of formations. These, monks, are called the forty-four objects of knowledge.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni [M 1.0289] indriyānaṃ paripāko, ayaṃ vuccati jarā. Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo. Idaṃ vuccati maraṇaṃ. Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ; idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ.

“And what, monks, is aging-and-death? Whatever for those various beings in those various orders of beings is aging, decrepitude, brokenness of teeth, grayness of hair, wrinkled skin, the decline of the lifespan, the ripening of the faculties—this is called aging. Whatever for those various beings from those various orders of beings is passing away, the state of passing away, breaking up, disappearance, death as mortality, the doing of time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the casting off of the body—this is called death. Thus, this aging and this death—this, monks, is called aging-and-death.”

“Jātisamudayā jarāmaraṇasamudayo; jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho; ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“From the arising of birth, there is the arising of aging and death; from the cessation of birth, there is the cessation of aging and death. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death, that is: right view… right concentration.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ [P 2.0058] pajānāti, evaṃ jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānāti, idamassa dhamme ñāṇaṃ[T 2.0069]. So iminā dhammena diṭṭhena viditena akālikena pattena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgatena yaṃ neti.

“When, monks, a noble disciple thus knows aging and death, thus knows the origin of aging and death, thus knows the cessation of aging and death, and thus knows the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death, this is his knowledge in the Dhamma. By this Dhamma that is seen, known, timeless, attained, and penetrated, he applies inference to the past and future.

“Ye [V 1.0051] kho keci atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, sabbe te evameva abbhaññaṃsu, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahi.

“Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past directly knew aging and death, directly knew the origin of aging and death, directly knew the cessation of aging and death, and directly knew the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death, all of them directly knew it in the same way as I do now.

“Yepi hi keci anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṃ abhijānissanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ abhijānissanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ abhijānissanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhijānissanti, sabbe te evameva abhijānissanti, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahīti. Idamassa anvaye ñāṇaṃ.

“Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will directly know aging and death, will directly know the origin of aging and death, will directly know the cessation of aging and death, and will directly know the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death, all of them will directly know it exactly as I do now. This is his knowledge of inference.”

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imāni dve ñāṇāni parisuddhāni honti pariyodātāni – dhamme ñāṇañca anvaye ñāṇañca. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako diṭṭhisampanno itipi, dassanasampanno itipi, āgato imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, passati imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, sekkhena ñāṇena samannāgato itipi, sekkhāya vijjāya samannāgato itipi, dhammasotaṃ samāpanno itipi, ariyo nibbedhikapañño itipi, amatadvāraṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati itipīti.

Bhikkhus, when these two kinds of knowledge of a noble disciple—knowledge in the Dhamma and knowledge in consequence—are purified and cleansed, this noble disciple, bhikkhus, is called: one accomplished in view, one accomplished in vision, one who has arrived at this true Dhamma, one who sees this true Dhamma, one endowed with the knowledge of a trainee, one endowed with the true knowledge of a trainee, one who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrative wisdom, and one who stands having reached the door to the Deathless.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, jāti…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, bhavo… katamañca, bhikkhave, upādānaṃ… katamā ca, bhikkhave taṇhā… katamā ca, bhikkhave, vedanā… katamo ca, bhikkhave, phasso… katamañca, bhikkhave[T 2.0070], saḷāyatanaṃ… katamañca, bhikkhave, nāmarūpaṃ [M 1.0290]… katamañca, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ… katame ca, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā? Tayome, bhikkhave[P 2.0059], saṅkhārā – kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāroti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā.

And what, bhikkhus, is birth? … And what, bhikkhus, is becoming? … And what, bhikkhus, is clinging? … And what, bhikkhus, is craving? … And what, bhikkhus, is feeling? … And what, bhikkhus, is contact? … And what, bhikkhus, are the six sense bases? … And what, bhikkhus, is name-and-form? … And what, bhikkhus, is consciousness? … And what, bhikkhus, are formations? There are these three formations, bhikkhus: bodily formation, verbal formation, and mental formation. These, bhikkhus, are called formations.

“Avijjāsamudayā saṅkhārasamudayo; avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo saṅkhāranirodhagāminī paṭipadā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

From the arising of ignorance, there is the arising of formations; from the cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of formations. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the practice leading to the cessation of formations, that is: Right View… Right Concentration.

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṃ saṅkhāre pajānāti, evaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ pajānāti[V 1.0052], evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānāti, idamassa dhamme ñāṇaṃ. So iminā dhammena diṭṭhena viditena akālikena pattena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgatena yaṃ neti.

When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple thus knows formations, thus knows the origin of formations, thus knows the cessation of formations, and thus knows the practice leading to the cessation of formations, this is his knowledge in the Dhamma. By this Dhamma that is seen, known, timeless, attained, and penetrated, he applies the method to the past and future.

“Ye kho keci atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā saṅkhāre abbhaññaṃsu, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, sabbe te evameva abbhaññaṃsu, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahi.

Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past directly knew formations, directly knew the origin of formations, directly knew the cessation of formations, and directly knew the practice leading to the cessation of formations, all of them directly knew them in the same way as I do now.

“Yepi hi keci anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā saṅkhāre abhijānissanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṃ abhijānissanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṃ abhijānissanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhijānissanti, sabbe te evameva abhijānissanti, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahi. Idamassa anvaye ñāṇaṃ.

Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will directly know formations, will directly know the origin of formations, will directly know the cessation of formations, and will directly know the practice leading to the cessation of formations, all of them will directly know them in the same way as I do now. This is his knowledge in consequence.

“Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imāni dve ñāṇāni parisuddhāni [T 2.0071] honti pariyodātāni – dhamme ñāṇañca anvaye ñāṇañca. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako diṭṭhisampanno itipi, dassanasampanno itipi, āgato imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, passati imaṃ saddhammaṃ itipi, sekkhena ñāṇena samannāgato itipi, sekkhāya vijjāya samannāgato itipi, dhammasotaṃ samāpanno itipi, ariyo nibbedhikapañño itipi, amatadvāraṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati itipī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

Bhikkhus, when these two kinds of knowledge of a noble disciple—knowledge in the Dhamma and knowledge in consequence—are purified and cleansed, this noble disciple, bhikkhus, is called: one accomplished in view, one accomplished in vision, one who has arrived at this true Dhamma, one who sees this true Dhamma, one endowed with the knowledge of a trainee, one endowed with the true knowledge of a trainee, one who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrative wisdom, and one who stands having reached the door to the Deathless. The Third.

4. Dutiyañāṇavatthusuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on the Grounds of Knowledge

34. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “sattasattari vo, bhikkhave, ñāṇavatthūni desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

34. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge. Listen to that and attend closely; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamāni[M 1.0291][P 2.0060], bhikkhave, sattasattari ñāṇavatthūni? Jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ[V 1.0053]; asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ; atītampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ; anāgatampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ; yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, what are the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge? The knowledge that ‘With birth as condition, there is aging-and-death’; the knowledge that ‘When there is no birth, there is no aging-and-death.’ The knowledge that in the past, too, ‘With birth as condition, there was aging-and-death’; the knowledge that ‘When there was no birth, there was no aging-and-death.’ The knowledge that in the future, too, ‘With birth as condition, there will be aging-and-death’; the knowledge that ‘When there is no birth, there will be no aging-and-death.’ And the knowledge that this knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma is also subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, and subject to cessation.”

“Bhavapaccayā jātīti ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādānapaccayā bhavoti ñāṇaṃ… taṇhāpaccayā upādānanti ñāṇaṃ… vedanāpaccayā taṇhāti ñāṇaṃ… phassapaccayā vedanāti ñāṇaṃ… saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti ñāṇaṃ… nāmarūpapaccayā [T 2.0072] saḷāyatananti ñāṇaṃ… viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti ñāṇaṃ… saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti ñāṇaṃ; avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ; atītampi addhānaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ; anāgatampi addhānaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ; yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ. Imāni vuccanti, bhikkhave, sattasattari ñāṇavatthūnī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“The knowledge that ‘With becoming as condition, there is birth’… The knowledge that ‘With clinging as condition, there is becoming’… The knowledge that ‘With craving as condition, there is clinging’… The knowledge that ‘With feeling as condition, there is craving’… The knowledge that ‘With contact as condition, there is feeling’… The knowledge that ‘With the six sense bases as condition, there is contact’… The knowledge that ‘With name-and-form as condition, there are the six sense bases’… The knowledge that ‘With consciousness as condition, there is name-and-form’… The knowledge that ‘With formations as condition, there is consciousness.’ The knowledge that ‘With ignorance as condition, there are formations’; the knowledge that ‘When there is no ignorance, there are no formations.’ The knowledge that in the past, too, ‘With ignorance as condition, there were formations’; the knowledge that ‘When there was no ignorance, there were no formations.’ The knowledge that in the future, too, ‘With ignorance as condition, there will be formations’; the knowledge that ‘When there is no ignorance, there will be no formations.’ And the knowledge that this knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma is also subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, and subject to cessation. These, bhikkhus, are called the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge. The Fourth.”

5. Avijjāpaccayasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Ignorance as a Condition

35. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘katamaṃ nu kho, bhante, jarāmaraṇaṃ, kassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇa’nti? ‘No kallo pañho’ti bhagavā avoca, ‘katamaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ[P 2.0061], kassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇa’nti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘aññaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ aññassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇa’nti, iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu[V 1.0054], diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete [T 2.0073] te, bhikkhu, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa’”nti.

35. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness comes to be... Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.” When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is aging-and-death, and whose is this aging-and-death?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “Bhikkhu, whether one were to say, ‘What is aging-and-death, and whose is this aging-and-death?’ or one were to say, ‘Aging-and-death is one thing, and this aging-and-death belongs to another,’ both of these have the same meaning; only the phrasing is different. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is the same as the body,’ there is no living of the holy life. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,’ there is no living of the holy life. Without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With birth as condition, there is aging-and-death.’”

“Katamā nu kho, bhante, jāti, kassa ca panāyaṃ jātī”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca, “‘katamā jāti, kassa ca panāyaṃ jātī’ti iti [M 1.0292] vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘aññā jāti aññassa ca panāyaṃ jātī’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete te, bhikkhu, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘bhavapaccayā jātī’”ti.

“Venerable sir, what is birth, and whose is this birth?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “Bhikkhu, whether one were to say, ‘What is birth, and whose is this birth?’ or one were to say, ‘Birth is one thing, and this birth belongs to another,’ both of these have the same meaning; only the phrasing is different. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is the same as the body,’ there is no living of the holy life. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,’ there is no living of the holy life. Without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With becoming as condition, there is birth.’”

“Katamo nu kho, bhante, bhavo, kassa ca panāyaṃ bhavo”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca, “‘katamo bhavo, kassa ca panāyaṃ bhavo’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘añño bhavo aññassa ca panāyaṃ bhavo’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti; aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete te, bhikkhu, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘upādānapaccayā bhavo’ti…pe… ‘taṇhāpaccayā upādānanti… vedanāpaccayā [T 2.0074] taṇhāti… phassapaccayā vedanāti… saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti… nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatananti… viññāṇapaccayā [P 2.0062] nāmarūpanti… saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa’”nti.

“Venerable sir, what is becoming, and whose is this becoming?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “Bhikkhu, whether one were to say, ‘What is becoming, and whose is this becoming?’ or one were to say, ‘Becoming is one thing, and this becoming belongs to another,’ both of these have the same meaning; only the phrasing is different. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is the same as the body,’ there is no living of the holy life. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,’ there is no living of the holy life. Without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With clinging as condition, there is becoming.’ ... ‘With craving as condition, there is clinging.’ ... ‘With feeling as condition, there is craving.’ ... ‘With contact as condition, there is feeling.’ ... ‘With the six sense bases as condition, there is contact.’ ... ‘With name-and-form as condition, there are the six sense bases.’ ... ‘With consciousness as condition, there is name-and-form.’ ... ‘With formations as condition, there is consciousness.’”

“Katame nu kho, bhante, saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārā”ti? “No kallo pañho”ti bhagavā avoca, “‘katame saṅkhārā kassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ‘aññe saṅkhārā aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ti iti vā, bhikkhu, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti; aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, bhikkhu, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete te, bhikkhu, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’”ti.

“Venerable sir, what are formations, and whose are these formations?” “That is not a proper question,” the Blessed One said. “Bhikkhu, whether one were to say, ‘What are formations, and whose are these formations?’ or one were to say, ‘Formations are one thing, and these formations belong to another,’ both of these have the same meaning; only the phrasing is different. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is the same as the body,’ there is no living of the holy life. Bhikkhu, when the view exists that ‘the life-principle is one thing and the body is another,’ there is no living of the holy life. Without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With ignorance as condition, there are formations.’”

“Avijjāya [V 1.0055] tveva, bhikkhu, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. ‘Katamaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, aññassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ’ iti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā. Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni.

“Bhikkhu, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are—such as, ‘What is aging-and-death, and whose is this aging-and-death?’ or, ‘Aging-and-death is one thing, and this aging-and-death is of another,’ or, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ or, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another’—all these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future.”

“Avijjāya [M 1.0293] tveva, bhikkhu, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. ‘Katamā jāti, kassa [T 2.0075] ca panāyaṃ jāti’ iti vā, ‘aññā jāti, aññassa ca panāyaṃ jāti’ iti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā. Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni.

“Bhikkhu, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are—such as, ‘What is birth, and whose is this birth?’ or, ‘Birth is one thing, and this birth belongs to another,’ or, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ or, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another’—all these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future.”

“Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhu, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. Katamo bhavo…pe… katamaṃ upādānaṃ… katamā taṇhā… katamā [P 2.0063] vedanā… katamo phasso… katamaṃ saḷāyatanaṃ… katamaṃ nāmarūpaṃ… katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ…pe….

“Bhikkhu, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are: ‘What is becoming?’… and so on… ‘What is clinging?’… ‘What is craving?’… ‘What is feeling?’… ‘What is contact?’… ‘What are the six sense bases?’… ‘What is name-and-form?’… ‘What is consciousness?’… and so on.”

“Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhu, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. ‘Katame saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā, ‘aññe saṅkhārā, aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ, aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā. Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammānī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Monk, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are—such as, ‘What are formations, and whose are these formations?’ or, ‘Formations are one thing, and to another these formations belong,’ or, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ or, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another’—all these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future.” Fifth.

6. Dutiyaavijjāpaccayasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Ignorance as Condition

36. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0056] viharati…pe… “avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

36. Dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Monks, with ignorance as condition, formations arise; with formations as condition, consciousness arises… Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.”

“‘Katamaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇa’nti iti vā, bhikkhave[T 2.0076], yo vadeyya, ‘aññaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, aññassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇa’nti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. ‘Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. ‘Aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete te, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa’”nti.

“‘What is aging-and-death, and whose is this aging-and-death?’—should one say this, monks, or should one say, ‘Aging-and-death is one thing, and this aging-and-death is of another,’—both of these have the same meaning, only the phrasing differs. Monks, if there is the view, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ the living of the holy life is not possible. Monks, if there is the view, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another,’ the living of the holy life is not possible. Monks, without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With birth as condition, aging-and-death comes to be.’”

“Katamā [M 1.0294] jāti…pe… katamo bhavo… katamaṃ upādānaṃ… katamā taṇhā… katamā vedanā… katamo phasso… katamaṃ [P 2.0064] saḷāyatanaṃ… katamaṃ nāmarūpaṃ… katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ… katame saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārāti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ‘aññe saṅkhārā aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ byañjanameva nānaṃ. ‘Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. ‘Aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti. Ete te, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti – ‘avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’”ti.

“‘What is birth?’… and so on… ‘What are formations, and whose are these formations?’—should one say this, monks, or should one say, ‘Formations are one thing, and to another these formations belong,’—both of these have the same meaning, only the phrasing differs. Monks, if there is the view, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ the living of the holy life is not possible. Monks, if there is the view, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another,’ the living of the holy life is not possible. Monks, without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle: ‘With ignorance as condition, formations arise.’”

“Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhave, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. ‘Katamaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kassa ca panidaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, aññassa ca panidaṃ [T 2.0077] jarāmaraṇaṃ’ iti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ [V 1.0057] taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ, aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā. Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni.

“Monks, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are—such as, ‘What is aging-and-death, and whose is this aging-and-death?’ or, ‘Aging-and-death is one thing, and this aging-and-death is of another,’ or, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ or, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another’—all these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future.”

“Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhave, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici. Katamā jāti…pe… katamo bhavo… katamaṃ upādānaṃ… katamā taṇhā… katamā vedanā… katamo phasso… katamaṃ saḷāyatanaṃ… katamaṃ nāmarūpaṃ… katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ… ‘katame saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā, ‘aññe saṅkhārā, aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā; ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ’ iti vā. Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammānī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Monks, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, whatever perplexities, distortions, and vacillations there are—such as, ‘What is birth?’… and so on… ‘What are formations, and whose are these formations?’ or, ‘Formations are one thing, and to another these formations belong,’ or, ‘That which is the life-principle is the same as the body,’ or, ‘The life-principle is one thing, and the body is another’—all these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and are of a nature not to arise again in the future.” Sixth.

7. Natumhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on 'Not Yours'

37. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “nāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kāyo tumhākaṃ napi aññesaṃ. Purāṇamidaṃ[P 2.0065], bhikkhave, kammaṃ abhisaṅkhataṃ abhisañcetayitaṃ vedaniyaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ”.

37. At Sāvatthī... “Monks, this body is not yours, nor is it others'. Monks, this old kamma should be regarded as intentionally formed, intentionally willed, and to be experienced.”

“Tatra [M 1.0295] kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṃ yoniso manasi karoti – ‘iti imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, imassuppādā [T 2.0078] idaṃ uppajjati; imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhati, yadidaṃ – avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī’”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Herein, monks, a learned noble disciple attends well and wisely to dependent origination itself: ‘When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises. When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.’ That is: ‘With ignorance as condition, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness comes to be… Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; with the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness… Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.’” Seventh.

8. Cetanāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Volition

38. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0058]. “Yañca, bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ āramaṇametaṃ (?) hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti. Āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā sati āyatiṃ jāti jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti”.

38. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, that which one wills, and that which one plans, and that which one has a latent tendency for: this becomes a support for the station of consciousness. When there is a support, there is a footing for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is in the future the generation of renewed existence. When there is in the future the generation of renewed existence, there come to be in the future birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.”

“No ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti, atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti. Āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā sati āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

Bhikkhus, if one does not intend and does not plan, but one has a latent tendency, this becomes a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a support, there is an establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is in the future the generation of renewed existence. When there is in the future the generation of renewed existence, there come to be in the future birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā[P 2.0066]. Ārammaṇe asati [T 2.0079] patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti na hoti. Āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā asati āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

But when, Bhikkhus, one neither intends, nor plans, nor has a latent tendency, this does not become a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no support, there is no establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is unestablished and has not grown, there is in the future no generation of renewed existence. When in the future there is no generation of renewed existence, future birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. Eighth.

9. Dutiyacetanāsuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on Volition

39. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0296] viharati…pe… “yañca, bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti. Nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ; saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso; phassapaccayā vedanā…pe… taṇhā… upādānaṃ… bhavo… jāti… jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti”.

39. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, whatever one intends, whatever one plans, and whatever one has a latent tendency for, this becomes a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a support, there is an establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is a descent of name-and-form. With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise; with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises… craving… clinging… existence… birth… aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.”

“No [V 1.0059] ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti, atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti. Nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

Bhikkhus, if one does not intend and does not plan, yet one has a latent tendency, this becomes a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a support, there is an establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is a descent of name-and-form. With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise... Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe [T 2.0080] asati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti na hoti. Nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

But when, Bhikkhus, one neither intends, nor plans, nor has a latent tendency, this does not become a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no support, there is no establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is unestablished and has not grown, there is no descent of name-and-form. From the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease... Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. Ninth.

10. Tatiyacetanāsuttaṃ

10. The Third Discourse on Volition

40. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “yañca[P 2.0067], bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti ārammaṇametaṃ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nati hoti. Natiyā sati āgatigati hoti. Āgatigatiyā sati cutūpapāto hoti. Cutūpapāte sati āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti”.

40. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, whatever one intends, whatever one plans, and whatever one has a latent tendency for, this becomes a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a support, there is an establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is inclination. When there is inclination, there is coming and going. When there is coming and going, there is passing away and rebirth. When there is passing away and rebirth, in the future, birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.”

“No ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe sati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa hoti. Tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nati hoti. Natiyā [M 1.0297] sati āgatigati hoti. Āgatigatiyā sati cutūpapāto hoti. Cutūpapāte sati āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

Bhikkhus, if one does not intend and does not plan, yet one has a latent tendency, this becomes a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a support, there is an establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is established and has grown, there is inclination. When there is inclination, there is coming and going. When there is coming and going, there is passing away and rebirth. When there is passing away and rebirth, in the future, birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṃ [V 1.0060] na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā. Ārammaṇe [T 2.0081] asati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti. Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe nati na hoti. Natiyā asati āgatigati na hoti. Āgatigatiyā asati cutūpapāto na hoti. Cutūpapāte asati āyatiṃ jāti jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

But when, Bhikkhus, one neither intends, nor plans, nor has a latent tendency, this does not become a support for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no support, there is no establishment for consciousness. When that consciousness is unestablished and has not grown, there is no inclination. When there is no inclination, there is no coming and going. When there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and rebirth. When there is no passing away and rebirth, in the future, birth, aging, and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. Tenth.

Kaḷārakhattiyavaggo catuttho.

The Kaḷārakhattiya Chapter, the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Bhūtamidaṃ kaḷārañca, duve ca ñāṇavatthūni;

Avijjāpaccayā [P 2.0068] ca dve, natumhā cetanā tayoti.

The Bhūtamidaṃ and Kaḷāra suttas, two on the Bases of Knowledge, the Avijjāpaccayā sutta, two Na Tumhāka suttas, and three on Volition.

5. Gahapativaggo

5. The Householder Chapter

1. Pañcaverabhayasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Five Fears and Enmities

41. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0082] viharati. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

41. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika who was seated to one side:

“Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti.

“Householder, when for a noble disciple five fears and enmities are pacified, he is endowed with the four factors of stream-entry, and the noble principle has been well seen and well penetrated by him with wisdom, he may, if he wishes, declare of himself: ‘Hell is exhausted for me; the animal birth is exhausted; the sphere of ghosts is exhausted; the planes of misery, bad destinations, and downfall are exhausted. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured, and destined for full enlightenment.’”

“Katamāni [M 1.0298][V 1.0061] pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti? Yaṃ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati, pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṃ taṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti.

“What are the five fears and enmities that are pacified?
