Compared to Mount Sineru, the king of mountains, the seven mung-bean-sized pebbles that have been placed there do not amount to a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part.” “So too, bhikkhus, compared to the attainment of a noble disciple, a person accomplished in view, the attainment of other sectarians—ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers—does not amount to a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part. So great in attainment, bhikkhus, is a person accomplished in view; so great in higher knowledge.” Eleventh.

Abhisamayasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Breakthrough is completed.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this:

Nakhasikhā pokkharaṇī, sambhejjaudake ca dve;

Dve pathavī dve samuddā, tayo ca pabbatūpamāti.

Nakhasikhā and Pokkharaṇī, and two on Sambhejjaudaka; two on Pathavī, two on Samudda, and three with the Mountain Simile.

3. Dhātusaṃyuttaṃ

3. The Connected Discourses on Elements

1. Nānattavaggo

1. The Chapter on Diversity

1. Dhātunānattasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Diversity of Elements

85. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0170][V 1.0125][P 2.0140][M 1.0358] viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

85. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the diversity of elements. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātu rūpadhātu cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu saddadhātu sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu gandhadhātu ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu rasadhātu jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu phoṭṭhabbadhātu kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu dhammadhātu manoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānatta”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the mental-phenomena element, the mind-consciousness element. This, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

2. Phassanānattasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Diversity of Contact

86. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātu sotadhātu ghānadhātu jivhādhātu kāyadhātu manodhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

86. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The eye element, the ear element, the nose element, the tongue element, the body element, the mind element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphasso. Sotadhātuṃ paṭicca… ghānadhātuṃ paṭicca [P 2.0141]… jivhādhātuṃ [V 1.0126] paṭicca… kāyadhātuṃ paṭicca… manodhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati manosamphasso. Evaṃ kho[T 2.0171], bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānatta”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does diversity of contact arise dependent on the diversity of elements? Dependent on the eye element, bhikkhus, eye-contact arises. Dependent on the ear element… dependent on the nose element… dependent on the tongue element… dependent on the body element… dependent on the mind element, mind-contact arises. Thus, bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises.”

3. Nophassanānattasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Not from Diversity of Contact

87. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātu…pe… manodhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

87. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; but diversity of elements does not arise dependent on the diversity of contact. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The eye element… the mind element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca[M 1.0359], bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphasso, no cakkhusamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati cakkhudhātu…pe… manodhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati manosamphasso, no manosamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati manodhātu. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānatta”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And how is it, bhikkhus, that diversity of contact arises dependent on the diversity of elements, but diversity of elements does not arise dependent on the diversity of contact? Dependent on the eye element, bhikkhus, eye-contact arises; but the eye element does not arise dependent on eye-contact… Dependent on the mind element, mind-contact arises; but the mind element does not arise dependent on mind-contact. Thus, bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; but diversity of elements does not arise dependent on the diversity of contact.”

4. Vedanānānattasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling

88. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātu [P 2.0142]…pe… manodhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

88. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on the diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The eye element... the mind element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphasso, cakkhusamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… manodhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati [T 2.0172] manosamphasso, manosamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānatta”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does diversity of contact arise dependent on the diversity of elements, and diversity of feeling arise dependent on the diversity of contact? Dependent on the eye element, bhikkhus, eye-contact arises; dependent on eye-contact, feeling born of eye-contact arises... dependent on the mind element, mind-contact arises; dependent on mind-contact, feeling born of mind-contact arises. Thus, bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on the diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises.”

5. Dutiyavedanānānattasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on the Diversity of Feeling

89. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0127] viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, no vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātu…pe… manodhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

89. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on the diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises. Diversity of contact does not arise dependent on diversity of feeling; diversity of elements does not arise dependent on diversity of contact. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The eye element... the mind element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, no vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ? Cakkhudhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphasso, cakkhusamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, no cakkhusamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca [P 2.0143] uppajjati cakkhusamphasso, no cakkhusamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati cakkhudhātu…pe… manodhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati manosamphasso, manosamphassaṃ [M 1.0360] paṭicca uppajjati manosamphassajā vedanā, no manosamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati manosamphasso, no manosamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati manodhātu. Evaṃ [T 2.0173] kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, no vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānatta”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And how is it, bhikkhus, that dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on the diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises; yet diversity of contact does not arise dependent on diversity of feeling, and diversity of elements does not arise dependent on diversity of contact? Dependent on the eye element, bhikkhus, eye-contact arises; dependent on eye-contact, feeling born of eye-contact arises. Eye-contact does not arise dependent on feeling born of eye-contact; the eye element does not arise dependent on eye-contact... Dependent on the mind element, mind-contact arises; dependent on mind-contact, feeling born of mind-contact arises. Mind-contact does not arise dependent on feeling born of mind-contact; the mind element does not arise dependent on mind-contact. Thus, bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on the diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises; yet diversity of contact does not arise dependent on diversity of feeling, and diversity of elements does not arise dependent on diversity of contact.” Fifth.

6. Bāhiradhātunānattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Diversity of External Elements

90. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Rūpadhātu saddadhātu gandhadhātu rasadhātu phoṭṭhabbadhātu dhammadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānatta”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

90. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the diversity of elements. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The form element, the sound element, the odor element, the taste element, the tangible element, the mental-object element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.” Sixth.

7. Saññānānattasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Diversity of Perceptions

91. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca [V 1.0128] – “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Rūpadhātu…pe… dhammadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

91. At Sāvatthī... “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements arises the diversity of perceptions; dependent on the diversity of perceptions arises the diversity of thoughts; dependent on the diversity of thoughts arises the diversity of desires; dependent on the diversity of desires arises the diversity of torment; dependent on the diversity of torment arises the diversity of seeking. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The form element... the mental-object element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca[P 2.0144], bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ?

“And how, bhikkhus, is it that dependent on the diversity of elements arises the diversity of perceptions; dependent on the diversity of perceptions arises the diversity of thoughts; dependent on the diversity of thoughts arises the diversity of desires; dependent on the diversity of desires arises the diversity of torment; dependent on the diversity of torment arises the diversity of seeking?”

“Rūpadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaññā[T 2.0174], rūpasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaṅkappo, rūpasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpacchando, rūpacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpapariḷāho, rūpapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpapariyesanā…pe… dhammadhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, dhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaṅkappo, dhammasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammacchando, dhammacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariḷāho, dhammapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariyesanā.

“Bhikkhus, dependent on the form element arises perception of form; dependent on perception of form arises thought of form; dependent on thought of form arises desire for form; dependent on desire for form arises torment regarding form; dependent on torment regarding form arises seeking for form... Dependent on the mental-object element arises perception of mental objects; dependent on perception of mental objects arises thought of mental objects; dependent on thought of mental objects arises desire for mental objects; dependent on desire for mental objects arises torment regarding mental objects; dependent on torment regarding mental objects arises seeking for mental objects.”

“Evaṃ, kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ [M 1.0361] paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānatta”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements arises the diversity of perceptions; dependent on the diversity of perceptions arises the diversity of thoughts; dependent on the diversity of thoughts arises the diversity of desires; dependent on the diversity of desires arises the diversity of torment; dependent on the diversity of torment arises the diversity of seeking.” Seventh.

8. Nopariyesanānānattasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Diversity and Non-Arising from Seeking

92. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ; no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ[P 2.0145], no pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, no chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ[V 1.0129], no saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Rūpadhātu…pe… dhammadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

92. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of perceptions arises; dependent on the diversity of perceptions, diversity of thoughts arises; dependent on the diversity of thoughts, diversity of desires arises; dependent on the diversity of desires, diversity of torment arises; dependent on the diversity of torment, diversity of seeking arises. Dependent on the diversity of seeking, diversity of torment does not arise; dependent on the diversity of torment, diversity of desires does not arise; dependent on the diversity of desires, diversity of thoughts does not arise; dependent on the diversity of thoughts, diversity of perceptions does not arise; dependent on the diversity of perceptions, diversity of elements does not arise. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The form element… the mental-object element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca[T 2.0175], bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… pariyesanānānattaṃ; no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, no pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, no chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, no saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ?

“And how, bhikkhus, is it that dependent on the diversity of elements, diversity of perceptions arises; dependent on the diversity of perceptions… diversity of seeking arises; yet dependent on the diversity of seeking, diversity of torment does not arise; dependent on the diversity of torment, diversity of desires does not arise; dependent on the diversity of desires, diversity of thoughts does not arise; dependent on the diversity of thoughts, diversity of perceptions does not arise; dependent on the diversity of perceptions, diversity of elements does not arise?”

“Rūpadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaññā…pe… dhammadhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, dhammasaññaṃ [P 2.0146] paṭicca uppajjati…pe… dhammapariyesanā; no dhammapariyesanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariḷāho, no dhammapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammacchando, no dhammacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaṅkappo, no dhammasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, no dhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammadhātu.

“Bhikkhus, conditioned by the form element, form-perception arises…pe… conditioned by the dhamma element, dhamma-perception arises; conditioned by dhamma-perception…pe… dhamma-pursuit arises. Conditioned by dhamma-pursuit, dhamma-feverishness does not arise; conditioned by dhamma-feverishness, dhamma-desire does not arise; conditioned by dhamma-desire, dhamma-thought does not arise; conditioned by dhamma-thought, dhamma-perception does not arise; conditioned by dhamma-perception, the dhamma element does not arise.”

“Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… pariyesanānānattaṃ; no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, no pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, no chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, no saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānatta”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, conditioned by diversity of elements, diversity of perceptions arises; conditioned by diversity of perceptions…pe… diversity of pursuit arises. Conditioned by diversity of pursuit, diversity of feverishness does not arise; conditioned by diversity of feverishness, diversity of desire does not arise; conditioned by diversity of desire, diversity of thoughts does not arise; conditioned by diversity of thoughts, diversity of perceptions does not arise; conditioned by diversity of perceptions, diversity of elements does not arise.” The Eighth.

9. Bāhiraphassanānattasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Diversity of External Contact

93. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0362] viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ[T 2.0176], phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ[V 1.0130], pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati lābhanānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Rūpadhātu…pe… dhammadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

93. While dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, conditioned by diversity of elements arises diversity of perceptions; conditioned by diversity of perceptions arises diversity of thoughts; conditioned by diversity of thoughts arises diversity of contact; conditioned by diversity of contact arises diversity of feeling; conditioned by diversity of feeling arises diversity of desire; conditioned by diversity of desire arises diversity of feverishness; conditioned by diversity of feverishness arises diversity of pursuit; conditioned by diversity of pursuit arises diversity of gain. And what, bhikkhus, is diversity of elements? The form element…pe… the dhamma element—this, bhikkhus, is called diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati [P 2.0147] saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… lābhanānattaṃ?

“And how, bhikkhus, conditioned by diversity of elements arises diversity of perceptions; conditioned by diversity of perceptions arises…pe… diversity of gain?”

“Rūpadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaññā, rūpasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaṅkappo, rūpasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpasamphasso, rūpasamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpasamphassajā vedanā, rūpasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpacchando, rūpacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpapariḷāho, rūpapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpapariyesanā, rūpapariyesanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati rūpalābho…pe… dhammadhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, dhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaṅkappo, dhammasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasamphasso, dhammasamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasamphassajā vedanā, dhammasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammacchando, dhammacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariḷāho, dhammapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariyesanā, dhammapariyesanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammalābho[T 2.0177].

“Bhikkhus, conditioned by the form element arises form-perception; conditioned by form-perception arises form-thought; conditioned by form-thought arises form-contact; conditioned by form-contact arises feeling born of form-contact; conditioned by feeling born of form-contact arises desire for form; conditioned by desire for form arises form-feverishness; conditioned by form-feverishness arises form-pursuit; conditioned by form-pursuit arises form-gain…pe… Conditioned by the dhamma element arises dhamma-perception; conditioned by dhamma-perception arises dhamma-thought; conditioned by dhamma-thought arises dhamma-contact; conditioned by dhamma-contact arises feeling born of dhamma-contact; conditioned by feeling born of dhamma-contact arises desire for dhammas; conditioned by desire for dhammas arises dhamma-feverishness; conditioned by dhamma-feverishness arises dhamma-pursuit; conditioned by dhamma-pursuit arises dhamma-gain.”

“Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… pariyesanānānattaṃ, pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati lābhanānatta”nti. Navamaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, conditioned by diversity of elements arises diversity of perceptions; conditioned by diversity of perceptions arises…pe… diversity of pursuit; conditioned by diversity of pursuit arises diversity of gain.” The Ninth.

10. Dutiyabāhiraphassanānattasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Diversity of External Contact

94. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātunānattaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ[P 2.0148], phassa… vedanā… chanda… pariḷāha… pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati lābhanānattaṃ; no lābhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ, no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, no pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… chanda… vedanā… phassa… saṅkappa… saññānānattaṃ[V 1.0131], no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca [M 1.0363] uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ? Rūpadhātu…pe… dhammadhātu – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ”.

94. While dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, conditioned by diversity of elements, diversity of perceptions arises; conditioned by diversity of perceptions, diversity of thoughts arises; ...contact... feeling... desire... feverishness... and conditioned by diversity of pursuit, diversity of gain arises. Conditioned by diversity of gain, diversity of pursuit does not arise; conditioned by diversity of pursuit, diversity of feverishness does not arise; ...and so on in reverse... conditioned by diversity of thought, diversity of perceptions does not arise; conditioned by diversity of perceptions, diversity of elements does not arise. And what, bhikkhus, is the diversity of elements? The form element... the dhamma element—this, bhikkhus, is called the diversity of elements.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ? Phassa… vedanā… chanda… pariḷāha… pariyesanā… lābha… no lābhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ, no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāha… chanda… vedanā… phassa… no saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānattaṃ?

“And how, bhikkhus, does diversity of perceptions arise conditioned by diversity of elements, and diversity of thoughts arise conditioned by diversity of perceptions? ...and so on for contact... feeling... desire... feverishness... pursuit... and gain? And how is it that diversity of pursuit does not arise conditioned by diversity of gain; that diversity of feverishness does not arise conditioned by diversity of pursuit; ...and so on in reverse... that diversity of perceptions does not arise conditioned by diversity of thought; and that diversity of elements does not arise conditioned by diversity of perceptions?”

“Rūpadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati rūpasaññā…pe… dhammadhātuṃ [T 2.0178] paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, dhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… dhammapariyesanā, dhammapariyesanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammalābho; no dhammalābhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariyesanā, no dhammapariyesanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammapariḷāho[P 2.0149], no dhammapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammacchando, no dhammacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasamphassajā vedanā, no dhammasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasamphasso, no dhammasamphassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaṅkappo, no dhammasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammasaññā, no dhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhammadhātu.

Bhikkhus, in dependence on the form element, perception of form arises... in dependence on the dhamma element, perception of a dhamma arises. In dependence on perception of a dhamma... seeking for a dhamma arises. In dependence on seeking for a dhamma, gain of a dhamma arises. But seeking for a dhamma does not arise in dependence on the gain of a dhamma; feverish anxiety concerning a dhamma does not arise in dependence on seeking for a dhamma; desire for a dhamma does not arise in dependence on feverish anxiety concerning a dhamma; feeling born of contact with a dhamma does not arise in dependence on desire for a dhamma; contact with a dhamma does not arise in dependence on feeling born of contact with a dhamma; conception of a dhamma does not arise in dependence on contact with a dhamma; perception of a dhamma does not arise in dependence on conception of a dhamma; the dhamma element does not arise in dependence on perception of a dhamma.

“Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati…pe… saṅkappa… phassa… vedanā… chanda… pariḷāha… pariyesanā… lābha… no lābhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ, no pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, no pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, no chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, no vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, no phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, no saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, no saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dhātunānatta”nti. Dasamaṃ.

Thus, Bhikkhus, in dependence on a diversity of elements, a diversity of perceptions arises. In dependence on a diversity of perceptions arises... a diversity of conceptions... a diversity of contacts... a diversity of feelings... a diversity of desires... a diversity of feverish anxieties... a diversity of seekings... a diversity of gains. But a diversity of seekings does not arise in dependence on a diversity of gains; a diversity of feverish anxieties does not arise in dependence on a diversity of seekings; a diversity of desires does not arise in dependence on a diversity of feverish anxieties; a diversity of feelings does not arise in dependence on a diversity of desires; a diversity of contacts does not arise in dependence on a diversity of feelings; a diversity of conceptions does not arise in dependence on a diversity of contacts; a diversity of perceptions does not arise in dependence on a diversity of conceptions; a diversity of elements does not arise in dependence on a diversity of perceptions. The tenth.

Nānattavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Diversity.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Dhātuphassañca [T 2.0179][V 1.0132] no cetaṃ, vedanā apare duve;

Etaṃ ajjhattapañcakaṃ, dhātusaññañca no cetaṃ;

Phassassa apare duve, etaṃ bāhirapañcakanti.

Elements and Contact, and the ‘Not This’ version; two others on Feeling; this is the internal pentad. Elements and Perception, and the ‘Not This’ version; two others on Contact; this is the external pentad.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sattadhātusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Seven Elements

95. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0180][M 1.0364] viharati…pe… “sattimā[P 2.0150], bhikkhave, dhātuyo. Katamā satta? Ābhādhātu, subhadhātu, ākāsānañcāyatanadhātu, viññāṇañcāyatanadhātu, ākiñcaññāyatanadhātu, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanadhātu, saññāvedayitanirodhadhātu – imā kho, bhikkhave, satta dhātuyo”ti.

95. Dwelling at Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these seven elements. What seven? The element of radiance, the element of beauty, the element of the base of infinite space, the element of the base of infinite consciousness, the element of the base of nothingness, the element of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the element of the cessation of perception and feeling. These, Bhikkhus, are the seven elements.”

Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yā cāyaṃ, bhante, ābhādhātu yā ca subhadhātu yā ca ākāsānañcāyatanadhātu yā ca viññāṇañcāyatanadhātu yā ca ākiñcaññāyatanadhātu yā ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanadhātu yā ca saññāvedayitanirodhadhātu – imā nu kho, bhante, dhātuyo kiṃ paṭicca paññāyantī”ti?

When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this element of radiance, this element of beauty, this element of the base of infinite space, this element of the base of infinite consciousness, this element of the base of nothingness, this element of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and this element of the cessation of perception and feeling—venerable sir, in dependence on what are these elements discerned?”

“Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, ābhādhātu – ayaṃ dhātu andhakāraṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, subhadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu asubhaṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, ākāsānañcāyatanadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu rūpaṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, viññāṇañcāyatanadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, ākiñcaññāyatanadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ paṭicca paññāyati. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, saññāvedayitanirodhadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu nirodhaṃ paṭicca paññāyatī”ti.

“Bhikkhu, the element of radiance—this element is discerned in dependence on darkness. Bhikkhu, the element of beauty—this element is discerned in dependence on the un-beautiful. Bhikkhu, the element of the base of infinite space—this element is discerned in dependence on form. Bhikkhu, the element of the base of infinite consciousness—this element is discerned in dependence on the base of infinite space. Bhikkhu, the element of the base of nothingness—this element is discerned in dependence on the base of infinite consciousness. Bhikkhu, the element of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—this element is discerned in dependence on the base of nothingness. Bhikkhu, the element of the cessation of perception and feeling—this element is discerned in dependence on cessation.”

“Yā [V 1.0133] cāyaṃ[T 2.0181], bhante, ābhādhātu yā ca subhadhātu yā ca ākāsānañcāyatanadhātu yā ca viññāṇañcāyatanadhātu yā ca ākiñcaññāyatanadhātu yā ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanadhātu yā ca saññāvedayitanirodhadhātu – imā nu kho, bhante, dhātuyo kathaṃ samāpatti pattabbā”ti?

“Venerable sir, this element of radiance, this element of beauty, this element of the base of infinite space, this element of the base of infinite consciousness, this element of the base of nothingness, this element of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and this element of the cessation of perception and feeling—venerable sir, how are these elements to be attained as attainments?”

“Yā cāyaṃ, bhikkhu, ābhādhātu yā ca subhadhātu yā ca ākāsānañcāyatanadhātu yā ca viññāṇañcāyatanadhātu yā ca [P 2.0151] ākiñcaññāyatanadhātu – imā dhātuyo saññāsamāpatti pattabbā. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu saṅkhārāvasesasamāpatti pattabbā[M 1.0365]. Yāyaṃ, bhikkhu, saññāvedayitanirodhadhātu – ayaṃ dhātu nirodhasamāpatti pattabbā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, the element of radiance, the element of beauty, the element of the base of infinite space, the element of the base of infinite consciousness, and the element of the base of nothingness—these elements are to be attained as perception-attainments. Bhikkhu, the element of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—this element is to be attained as the attainment with residual formations. Bhikkhu, the element of the cessation of perception and feeling—this element is to be attained as the cessation-attainment.” First.

2. Sanidānasuttaṃ

2. With a Cause

96. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “sanidānaṃ, bhikkhave, uppajjati kāmavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati byāpādavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati vihiṃsāvitakko, no anidānaṃ”.

96. Dwelling at Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, a thought of sensual desire arises with a cause, not without a cause. A thought of ill will arises with a cause, not without a cause. A thought of cruelty arises with a cause, not without a cause.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, sanidānaṃ uppajjati kāmavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati byāpādavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati vihiṃsāvitakko, no anidānaṃ? Kāmadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati kāmasaññā, kāmasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati kāmasaṅkappo, kāmasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati kāmacchando, kāmacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati [T 2.0182] kāmapariḷāho, kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati kāmapariyesanā. Kāmapariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyesamāno assutavā puthujjano tīhi ṭhānehi micchā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

“And how, Bhikkhus, does a thought of sensual desire arise with a cause, not without a cause? How does a thought of ill will arise with a cause, not without a cause? How does a thought of cruelty arise with a cause, not without a cause? Bhikkhus, in dependence on the sensual element, sensual perception arises. In dependence on sensual perception, sensual conception arises. In dependence on sensual conception, sensual desire arises. In dependence on sensual desire, sensual feverishness arises. In dependence on sensual feverishness, sensual seeking arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in sensual seeking, an uninstructed ordinary person engages in misconduct in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.”

“Byāpādadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati byāpādasaññā, byāpādasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati byāpādasaṅkappo…pe… byāpādacchando… byāpādapariḷāho… byāpādapariyesanā… byāpādapariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyesamāno assutavā puthujjano tīhi ṭhānehi micchā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

Bhikkhus, dependent on the element of ill will, a perception of ill will arises. Dependent on the perception of ill will, an intention of ill will arises. Dependent on the intention of ill will, a desire for ill will arises. Dependent on the desire for ill will, a fever of ill will arises. Dependent on the fever of ill will, a seeking for ill will arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in seeking for ill will, an uninstructed worldling practices wrongly in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.

“Vihiṃsādhātuṃ[V 1.0134], bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati vihiṃsāsaññā; vihiṃsāsaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vihiṃsāsaṅkappo…pe… vihiṃsāchando… vihiṃsāpariḷāho… vihiṃsāpariyesanā… vihiṃsāpariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave[P 2.0152], pariyesamāno assutavā puthujjano tīhi ṭhānehi micchā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

Bhikkhus, dependent on the element of cruelty, a perception of cruelty arises. Dependent on the perception of cruelty, an intention of cruelty arises. Dependent on the intention of cruelty, a desire for cruelty arises. Dependent on the desire for cruelty, a fever of cruelty arises. Dependent on the fever of cruelty, a seeking for cruelty arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in seeking for cruelty, an uninstructed worldling practices wrongly in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso ādittaṃ tiṇukkaṃ sukkhe tiṇadāye nikkhipeyya; no ce hatthehi ca pādehi ca khippameva nibbāpeyya. Evañhi, bhikkhave, ye tiṇakaṭṭhanissitā pāṇā te anayabyasanaṃ āpajjeyyuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yo hi koci samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā uppannaṃ visamagataṃ saññaṃ na khippameva pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ [M 1.0366] gameti, so diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkhaṃ viharati savighātaṃ saupāyāsaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ; kāyassa ca bhedā paraṃ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.

Just as, Bhikkhus, if a man were to cast a blazing grass torch into a dry grass-thicket, and if he did not quickly extinguish it with his hands and feet, then those creatures dependent on the grass and wood would come to ruin and disaster. So too, Bhikkhus, whatever ascetic or brahmin does not quickly abandon, dispel, make an end of, and bring to non-existence an arisen incongruous perception, he dwells in suffering in this very life, with vexation, with distress, and with fever; and on the dissolution of the body, after death, a woeful destination is to be expected.

“Sanidānaṃ, bhikkhave, uppajjati nekkhammavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ [T 2.0183] uppajjati abyāpādavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati avihiṃsāvitakko, no anidānaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a thought of renunciation arises with a cause, not without a cause. A thought of non-ill will arises with a cause, not without a cause. A thought of non-cruelty arises with a cause, not without a cause.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, sanidānaṃ uppajjati nekkhammavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati abyāpādavitakko, no anidānaṃ; sanidānaṃ uppajjati avihiṃsāvitakko, no anidānaṃ? Nekkhammadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati nekkhammasaññā, nekkhammasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati nekkhammasaṅkappo, nekkhammasaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati nekkhammacchando, nekkhammacchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati nekkhammapariḷāho, nekkhammapariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati nekkhammapariyesanā; nekkhammapariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyesamāno sutavā ariyasāvako tīhi ṭhānehi sammā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

And how, Bhikkhus, does a thought of renunciation arise with a cause, not without a cause? How does a thought of non-ill will arise with a cause, not without a cause? How does a thought of non-cruelty arise with a cause, not without a cause? Bhikkhus, dependent on the element of renunciation, a perception of renunciation arises. Dependent on the perception of renunciation, an intention of renunciation arises. Dependent on the intention of renunciation, a desire for renunciation arises. Dependent on the desire for renunciation, a zeal for renunciation arises. Dependent on the zeal for renunciation, a seeking for renunciation arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in seeking for renunciation, a learned noble disciple practices rightly in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.

“Abyāpādadhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati abyāpādasaññā, abyāpādasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati abyāpādasaṅkappo…pe… abyāpādacchando… abyāpādapariḷāho… abyāpādapariyesanā, abyāpādapariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyesamāno sutavā ariyasāvako tīhi ṭhānehi sammā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

Bhikkhus, dependent on the element of non-ill will, a perception of non-ill will arises. Dependent on the perception of non-ill will, an intention of non-ill will arises. Dependent on the intention of non-ill will, a desire for non-ill will arises. Dependent on the desire for non-ill will, a zeal for non-ill will arises. Dependent on the zeal for non-ill will, a seeking for non-ill will arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in seeking for non-ill will, a learned noble disciple practices rightly in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.

“Avihiṃsādhātuṃ[V 1.0135], bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati avihiṃsāsaññā[P 2.0153], avihiṃsāsaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjati avihiṃsāsaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappaṃ paṭicca uppajjati avihiṃsāchando, avihiṃsāchandaṃ paṭicca uppajjati avihiṃsāpariḷāho, avihiṃsāpariḷāhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati avihiṃsāpariyesanā; avihiṃsāpariyesanaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyesamāno sutavā ariyasāvako tīhi [T 2.0184] ṭhānehi sammā paṭipajjati – kāyena, vācāya, manasā.

Bhikkhus, dependent on the element of non-cruelty, a perception of non-cruelty arises. Dependent on the perception of non-cruelty, an intention of non-cruelty arises. Dependent on the intention of non-cruelty, a desire for non-cruelty arises. Dependent on the desire for non-cruelty, a zeal for non-cruelty arises. Dependent on the zeal for non-cruelty, a seeking for non-cruelty arises. Bhikkhus, while engaged in seeking for non-cruelty, a learned noble disciple practices rightly in three ways: by body, by speech, and by mind.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso ādittaṃ tiṇukkaṃ sukkhe tiṇadāye nikkhipeyya; tamenaṃ hatthehi ca pādehi ca khippameva nibbāpeyya. Evañhi, bhikkhave, ye tiṇakaṭṭhanissitā pāṇā te na anayabyasanaṃ āpajjeyyuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yo hi koci samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā uppannaṃ visamagataṃ saññaṃ khippameva pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti [M 1.0367] anabhāvaṃ gameti, so diṭṭhe ceva dhamme sukhaṃ viharati avighātaṃ anupāyāsaṃ apariḷāhaṃ; kāyassa ca bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Just as, Bhikkhus, if a man were to cast a blazing grass torch into a dry grass-thicket, and he were to quickly extinguish it with his hands and feet, then those creatures dependent on the grass and wood would not come to ruin and disaster. So too, Bhikkhus, whatever ascetic or brahmin quickly abandons, dispels, makes an end of, and brings to non-existence an arisen incongruous perception, he dwells happily in this very life, without vexation, without distress, and without fever; and on the dissolution of the body, after death, a good destination is to be expected.

3. Giñjakāvasathasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse at the Brick Hall

97. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

97. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Ñātika in the Brick Hall. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir!” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Dhātuṃ, bhikkhave, paṭicca uppajjati saññā, uppajjati diṭṭhi, uppajjati vitakko”ti. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā kaccāno saddho kaccāno (ka.) bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yāyaṃ, bhante, diṭṭhi – ‘asammāsambuddhesu sammāsambuddhā’ti, ayaṃ nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhi kiṃ paṭicca paññāyatī”ti?

“Bhikkhus, dependent on an element, perception arises, view arises, thought arises.” When this was said, the Venerable Kaccāna said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this view—‘Among those who are not perfectly self-enlightened, there are perfectly self-enlightened ones’—venerable sir, dependent on what is this view discerned?”

“Mahati kho esā, kaccāna, dhātu yadidaṃ avijjādhātu. Hīnaṃ[P 2.0154], kaccāna, dhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati hīnā saññā, hīnā diṭṭhi, hīno vitakko, hīnā cetanā, hīnā patthanā, hīno paṇidhi, hīno puggalo, hīnā vācā; hīnaṃ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti [T 2.0185] vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti; hīnā tassa upapattīti vadāmi.

“Kaccāna, that is a great element, namely, the element of ignorance. Kaccāna, dependent on an inferior element, inferior perception arises, an inferior view arises, inferior thought arises, inferior volition arises, inferior aspiration arises, inferior resolve arises, an inferior person arises, inferior speech arises; he tells, teaches, makes known, establishes, discloses, analyzes, and clarifies what is inferior; I say that his rebirth is inferior.”

“Majjhimaṃ[V 1.0136], kaccāna, dhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati majjhimā saññā, majjhimā diṭṭhi, majjhimo vitakko, majjhimā cetanā, majjhimā patthanā, majjhimo paṇidhi, majjhimo puggalo, majjhimā vācā; majjhimaṃ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti; majjhimā tassa upapattīti vadāmi.

“Kaccāna, dependent on a middling element, middling perception arises, a middling view, middling thought, middling volition, middling aspiration, middling resolve, a middling person, and middling speech arise; he tells, teaches, makes known, establishes, discloses, analyzes, and clarifies what is middling; I say that his rebirth is middling.”

“Paṇītaṃ, kaccāna, dhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati paṇītā saññā, paṇītā diṭṭhi, paṇīto vitakko, paṇītā cetanā, paṇītā patthanā, paṇīto paṇidhi, paṇīto puggalo, paṇītā vācā; paṇītaṃ ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti; paṇītā tassa upapattīti vadāmī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Kaccāna, dependent on a refined element, refined perception arises, a refined view, refined thought, refined volition, refined aspiration, refined resolve, a refined person, and refined speech arise; he tells, teaches, makes known, establishes, discloses, analyzes, and clarifies what is refined; I say that his rebirth is refined.”

4. Hīnādhimuttikasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Those with Inferior Inclinations

98. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0368] viharati…pe… “dhātusova dhātuso (sī. pī.) ayañca paṭhamārambhavākyeyeva, na sabbattha. tīsu pana addhāsu ca upamāsaṃsandananigamanaṭṭhāne ca idaṃ pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

98. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, beings mingle and associate by way of element. Those with inferior inclinations mingle and associate with those with inferior inclinations; those with virtuous inclinations mingle and associate with those with virtuous inclinations.”

“Atītampi kho khosaddo sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova īdisesu ṭhānesu pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu.

“In the past, too, bhikkhus, beings mingled and associated by way of element. Those with inferior inclinations mingled and associated with those with inferior inclinations; those with virtuous inclinations mingled and associated with those with virtuous inclinations.

“Anāgatampi kho khosaddo sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova īdisesu ṭhānesu pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi sattā saṃsandissanti samessanti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti [T 2.0186] samessanti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti.

“In the future, too, bhikkhus, beings will mingle and associate by way of element. Those with inferior inclinations will mingle and associate with those with inferior inclinations; those with virtuous inclinations will mingle and associate with those with virtuous inclinations.

“Etarahipi [P 2.0155] kho khosaddo sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova īdisesu ṭhānesu pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Even now, bhikkhus, in the present time, beings mingle and associate by way of element. Those with inferior inclinations mingle and associate with those with inferior inclinations; those with virtuous inclinations mingle and associate with those with virtuous inclinations.”

5. Caṅkamasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Walking Meditation

99. Ekaṃ [V 1.0137] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho mahāmoggallāno sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho mahākassapo sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho anuruddho sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho puṇṇo mantāniputto sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho upāli sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; āyasmāpi kho ānando sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati; devadattopi kho sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhagavato avidūre caṅkamati.

99. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha, on the mountain Gijjhakūṭa. At that time, the Venerable Sāriputta was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Mahākassapa also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Anuruddha also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāniputta also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Upāli also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. The Venerable Ānanda also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus. Devadatta also was walking to and fro not far from the Blessed One, together with many bhikkhus.

Atha [M 1.0369] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, sāriputtaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū mahāpaññā. Passatha [T 2.0187] no tumhe, bhikkhave, moggallānaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū mahiddhikā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, kassapaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ[P 2.0156], bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dhutavādā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, anuruddhaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dibbacakkhukā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, puṇṇaṃ mantāniputtaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dhammakathikā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, upāliṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū vinayadharā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, ānandaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahussutā. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, devadattaṃ sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ caṅkamanta”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Sabbe kho ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū pāpicchā”.

Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, do you see Sāriputta walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are of great wisdom. Bhikkhus, do you see Moggallāna walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are of great psychic power. Bhikkhus, do you see Kassapa walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are observers of the ascetic practices. Bhikkhus, do you see Anuruddha walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are possessors of the divine eye. Bhikkhus, do you see Puṇṇa Mantāniputta walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are preachers of the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, do you see Upāli walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are upholders of the Vinaya. Bhikkhus, do you see Ānanda walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are greatly learned. Bhikkhus, do you see Devadatta walking to and fro with many bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, all these bhikkhus are of evil desires.”

“Dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ [V 1.0138] saṃsandanti samenti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi [T 2.0188] saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu.

“Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition; those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition. In the past time also, bhikkhus, it was by element that beings associated and came together. Those of inferior disposition associated and came together with those of inferior disposition; those of virtuous disposition associated and came together with those of virtuous disposition.

“Anāgatampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandissanti samessanti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti.

“Bhikkhus, in the future time also, beings will associate and come together by element. Those of inferior disposition will associate and come together with those of inferior disposition; those of virtuous disposition will associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition.

“Etarahipi [P 2.0157] kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, now also, in the present time, beings associate and come together by element. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition; those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition.” Fifth.

6. Sagāthāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse with Verses

100. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0370] viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu”.

100. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition. In the past, too, bhikkhus, beings associated and came together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition associated and came together with those of inferior disposition.

“Anāgatampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandissanti samessanti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti.

“In the future, too, bhikkhus, beings will associate and come together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition will associate and come together with those of inferior disposition.

“Etarahipi kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti.

“Even now, bhikkhus, in the present, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gūtho gūthena saṃsandati sameti; muttaṃ muttena saṃsandati sameti; kheḷo kheḷena saṃsandati sameti; pubbo pubbena saṃsandati sameti; lohitaṃ lohitena saṃsandati sameti[V 1.0139]; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dhātusova sabbatthapi evameva dissati sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi [T 2.0189] saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho addhānaṃ…pe… anāgatampi kho addhānaṃ…pe… etarahipi kho paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Hīnādhimuttikā hīnādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti.

“Just as, bhikkhus, feces associates and comes together with feces, urine with urine, spittle with spittle, pus with pus, and blood with blood, so too, bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition. In the past, too… in the future, too… even now, in the present, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of inferior disposition associate and come together with those of inferior disposition.

“Dhātusova [P 2.0158] bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu. Kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu.

“Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition. In the past, too, bhikkhus, beings associated and came together by way of element. Those of virtuous disposition associated and came together with those of virtuous disposition.

“Anāgatampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ…pe… etarahipi kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti.

“In the future, too, bhikkhus… even now, in the present, bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, khīraṃ khīrena saṃsandati sameti; telaṃ telena saṃsandati sameti; sappi sappinā saṃsandati sameti; madhu madhunā saṃsandati sameti; phāṇitaṃ phāṇitena saṃsandati sameti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dhātusova [M 1.0371] sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho addhānaṃ… anāgatampi kho addhānaṃ… etarahipi kho paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Kalyāṇādhimuttikā kalyāṇādhimuttikehi saddhiṃ [T 2.0190] saṃsandanti samentī”ti.

“Just as, bhikkhus, milk associates and comes together with milk, oil with oil, ghee with ghee, honey with honey, and molasses with molasses, so too, bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition. In the past, too… in the future, too… even now, in the present, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those of virtuous disposition associate and come together with those of virtuous disposition.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Saṃsaggā vanatho jāto, asaṃsaggena chijjati;

Parittaṃ dārumāruyha, yathā sīde mahaṇṇave.

“From association the forest of defilements is born; by non-association it is cut off. Just as one who embarks on a small piece of wood would sink in the great ocean,

“Evaṃ kusītamāgamma, sādhujīvipi sīdati;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, kusītaṃ hīnavīriyaṃ.

so too, by relying on a lazy person, even one living a good life sinks. Therefore, one should avoid that lazy person of inferior energy.

“Pavivittehi [V 1.0140] ariyehi, pahitattehi jhāyīhi jhāyihi (sī.), jhāyibhi (syā. kaṃ.);

Niccaṃ āraddhavīriyehi, paṇḍitehi sahāvase”ti.

One should dwell together with the wise who are secluded, noble, with minds dispatched, meditative, and ever energetic.”

7. Assaddhasaṃsandanasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Association with the Faithless

101. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 2.0159] viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

101. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by element. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless; those with no fear of wrongdoing with those with no fear of wrongdoing; the unlearned with the unlearned; the lazy with the lazy; the unmindful with the unmindful; the unwise with the unwise.”

“Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; appassutā appassutehi [T 2.0191] saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu.

“In the past, too, bhikkhus, beings associated and came together by element. The faithless associated and came together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless; those with no fear of wrongdoing with those with no fear of wrongdoing; the unlearned with the unlearned; the lazy with the lazy; the unmindful with the unmindful; the unwise with the unwise.

“Anāgatampi [M 1.0372] kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandissanti samessanti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ…pe… appassutā [P 2.0160] appassutehi saddhiṃ…pe… kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ…pe… muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ…pe… duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandissanti samessanti.

“Bhikkhus, in the future time, beings will associate and come together by element. The faithless will associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless; those without fear of wrongdoing with those without fear of wrongdoing... those of little learning with those of little learning... the lazy with the lazy... the unmindful with the unmindful... the unwise will associate and come together with the unwise.

“Etarahipi kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ…pe… anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ…pe… appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ…pe… [V 1.0141] kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ…pe… muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti.

“Even now, bhikkhus, in the present time, beings associate and come together by element. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless... those without fear of wrongdoing with those without fear of wrongdoing... those of little learning with those of little learning... the lazy with the lazy... the unmindful associate and come together with the unmindful; the unwise associate and come together with the unwise.

“Dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ [T 2.0192] saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ…pe… anāgatampi kho, bhikkhave…pe… etarahipi kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; those with a sense of moral shame with those with a sense of moral shame; those with fear of wrongdoing with those with fear of wrongdoing; the learned with the learned; the energetic with the energetic; those with established mindfulness with those with established mindfulness; the wise with the wise. In the past, too, bhikkhus... In the future, too, bhikkhus... Even now, bhikkhus, in the present time, it is by element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful... the wise associate and come together with the wise.” Seventh.

8. Assaddhamūlakasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse Rooted in Faithlessness

102. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā [P 2.0161] assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Atītampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandiṃsu samiṃsu…pe… [V 1.0142] anāgatampi kho, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandissanti samessanti…pe….

102. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by element. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; those with a sense of moral shame with those with a sense of moral shame; the wise with the wise. In the past, too, bhikkhus, beings associated and came together by element... In the future, too, bhikkhus, beings will associate and come together by element...

“Etarahipi [M 1.0373] kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ dhātusova sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti. (1)

“Even now, bhikkhus, in the present time, beings associate and come together by element. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless with the shameless; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; those with a sense of moral shame with those with a sense of moral shame; the wise with the wise.”

“Dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti[T 2.0193]; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe… paṭhamavāro viya vitthāretabbo. (2)

“Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; those without fear of wrongdoing with those without fear of wrongdoing; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; those with fear of wrongdoing with those with fear of wrongdoing; the wise with the wise... This should be expanded as in the first section.

“Dhātusova[V 1.0143], bhikkhave…pe… assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…[P 2.0162]. (3)

“Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by element... The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; those of little learning with those of little learning; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; the learned with the learned; the wise with the wise...”

“Dhātusova, bhikkhave…pe… assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (4)

“Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by element... The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the lazy with the lazy; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; the energetic with the energetic; the wise with the wise...”

“Dhātusova[V 1.0144], bhikkhave…pe… assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti…pe…. Aṭṭhamaṃ. (5)

“Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by element... The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the unmindful with the unmindful; the unwise with the unwise. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; those with established mindfulness with those with established mindfulness; the wise with the wise...” Eighth.

9. Ahirikamūlakasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse Rooted in Shamelessness

103. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova…pe… ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti [T 2.0194] samenti, anottappino [P 2.0163] anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti[M 1.0374], duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ sasandanti samenti, ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…[V 1.0145]. (1)

103. While dwelling at Sāvatthī… “By way of element… The shameless associate and converge with the shameless; the unconscientious with the unconscientious; the unwise with the unwise. The scrupulous associate and converge with the scrupulous; the conscientious with the conscientious; the wise with the wise…”

“Ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (2)

“The shameless associate and converge with the shameless; the unlearned with the unlearned; the unwise with the unwise. The scrupulous associate and converge with the scrupulous; the learned with the learned; the wise with the wise…”

“Ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (3)

“The shameless associate and converge with the shameless; the lazy with the lazy; the unwise with the unwise. The scrupulous associate and converge with the scrupulous; the energetic with the energetic; the wise with the wise…”

“Ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti, paññavanto [V 1.0146] paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti…pe…. Navamaṃ. (4)

“The shameless associate and converge with the shameless; the unmindful with the unmindful; the unwise with the unwise. The scrupulous associate and converge with the scrupulous; the established in mindfulness with the established in mindfulness; the wise with the wise.” Ninth.

10. Anottappamūlakasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse Rooted in Lack of Conscientiousness

104. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0195] viharati…pe… “dhātusova[P 2.0164], bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (1)

104. While dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Monks, by way of element, beings associate and converge. The unconscientious associate and converge with the unconscientious; the unlearned associate and converge with the unlearned; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. The conscientious associate and converge with the conscientious; the learned associate and converge with the learned; the wise associate and converge with the wise…”

“Anottappino [V 1.0147] anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (2)

“The unconscientious associate and converge with the unconscientious; the lazy associate and converge with the lazy; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. The conscientious associate and converge with the conscientious; the energetic associate and converge with the energetic; the wise associate and converge with the wise…”

“Anottappino [M 1.0375] anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti…pe…. Dasamaṃ. (3)

“The unconscientious associate and converge with the unconscientious; the unmindful associate and converge with the unmindful; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. The conscientious associate and converge with the conscientious; the established in mindfulness associate and converge with the established in mindfulness; the wise associate and converge with the wise.” The Tenth.

11. Appassutamūlakasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse Rooted in Little Learning

105. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti [T 2.0196] samenti; kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti [V 1.0148] samenti; āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi [P 2.0165] saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti…pe…. (1)

105. At Sāvatthī... “Monks, beings associate and converge by way of element. Those of little learning associate and converge with those of little learning; the lazy associate and converge with the lazy; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. Those of much learning associate and converge with those of much learning; the energetic associate and converge with the energetic; the wise associate and converge with the wise.”

“Appassutā appassutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; bahussutā bahussutehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti…pe…. Ekādasamaṃ. (2)

“Those of little learning associate and converge with those of little learning; the unmindful associate and converge with the unmindful; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. Those of much learning associate and converge with those of much learning; the established in mindfulness associate and converge with the established in mindfulness; the wise associate and converge with the wise.” The Eleventh.

12. Kusītamūlakasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse Rooted in Laziness

106. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Kusītā kusītehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; muṭṭhassatino muṭṭhassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā [V 1.0149] duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; āraddhavīriyā āraddhavīriyehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; upaṭṭhitassatino upaṭṭhitassatīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentīti…pe…. Dvādasamaṃ.

106. At Sāvatthī... “Monks, beings associate and converge by way of element. The lazy associate and converge with the lazy; the unmindful associate and converge with the unmindful; the unwise associate and converge with the unwise. The energetic associate and converge with the energetic; the established in mindfulness associate and converge with the established in mindfulness; the wise associate and converge with the wise.” The Twelfth.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Sattimā [T 2.0197][M 1.0376] sanidānañca, giñjakāvasathena ca;

Hīnādhimutti caṅkamaṃ, sagāthā assaddhasattamaṃ.

The Seven Elements, and with an origin, and the Giñjaka Dwelling; Low Aspiration, Walking, with verses, the seventh on lack of faith.

Assaddhamūlakā [P 2.0166] pañca, cattāro ahirikamūlakā;

Anottappamūlakā tīṇi, duve appassutena ca.

Five rooted in lack of faith, four rooted in lack of shame; three rooted in lack of moral dread, and two on the unlearned.

Kusītaṃ ekakaṃ vuttaṃ, suttantā tīṇi pañcakā;

Bāvīsati vuttā suttā, dutiyo vaggo pavuccatīti.

One on laziness is spoken; the suttas are fifteen; twenty-two suttas are spoken, thus the Second Chapter is called.

3. Kammapathavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Courses of Action

1. Asamāhitasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Unconcentrated

107. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0198][V 1.0150] viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; asamāhitā asamāhitehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

107. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless associate and come together with the shameless; those without moral dread associate and come together with those without moral dread; the unconcentrated associate and come together with the unconcentrated; the unwise associate and come together with the unwise.'

“Saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; samāhitā samāhitehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

'The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; the conscientious associate and come together with the conscientious; those with moral dread associate and come together with those with moral dread; the concentrated associate and come together with the concentrated; the wise associate and come together with the wise.' First.

2. Dussīlasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Immoral

108. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Assaddhā assaddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ahirikā ahirikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; anottappino anottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; dussīlā dussīlehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; duppaññā duppaññehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

108. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together.
