The faithless associate and come together with the faithless; the shameless associate and come together with the shameless; those without moral dread associate and come together with those without moral dread; the immoral associate and come together with the immoral; the unwise associate and come together with the unwise.'

“Saddhā saddhehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; hirimanā hirimanehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; ottappino ottappīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; sīlavanto [M 1.0377][P 2.0167] sīlavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti [T 2.0199] samenti; paññavanto paññavantehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

'The faithful associate and come together with the faithful; the conscientious associate and come together with the conscientious; those with moral dread associate and come together with those with moral dread; the virtuous associate and come together with the virtuous; the wise associate and come together with the wise.' Second.

3. Pañcasikkhāpadasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Five Training Rules

109. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Pāṇātipātino [V 1.0151] pāṇātipātīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; adinnādāyino adinnādāyīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kāmesumicchācārino kāmesumicchācārīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; musāvādino musāvādīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhāyino surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhāyīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

109. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. Those who destroy life associate and come together with those who destroy life; those who take what is not given associate and come together with those who take what is not given; those who engage in sexual misconduct associate and come together with those who engage in sexual misconduct; those who speak falsely associate and come together with those who speak falsely; those who indulge in distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness associate and come together with those who indulge in distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.'

“Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; adinnādānā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; musāvādā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

'Those who abstain from destroying life associate and come together with those who abstain from destroying life; those who abstain from taking what is not given associate and come together with those who abstain from taking what is not given; those who abstain from sexual misconduct associate and come together with those who abstain from sexual misconduct; those who abstain from false speech associate and come together with those who abstain from false speech; those who abstain from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness associate and come together with those who abstain from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.' Third.

4. Sattakammapathasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Seven Courses of Action

110. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Pāṇātipātino pāṇātipātīhi saddhiṃ [T 2.0200] saṃsandanti samenti; adinnādāyino adinnādāyīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; kāmesumicchācārino kāmesumicchācārīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; musāvādino musāvādīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; pisuṇavācā pisuṇavācehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; pharusavācā pharusavācehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; samphappalāpino samphappalāpīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

110. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. Those who destroy life associate and come together with those who destroy life; those who take what is not given associate and come together with those who take what is not given; those who engage in sexual misconduct associate and come together with those who engage in sexual misconduct; those who speak falsely associate and come together with those who speak falsely; those who speak divisively associate and come together with those who speak divisively; those who speak harshly associate and come together with those who speak harshly; those who engage in idle chatter associate and come together with those who engage in idle chatter.'

“Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā…pe… adinnādānā paṭiviratā… kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā… musāvādā paṭiviratā… pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; samphappalāpā paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

'Those who abstain from destroying life... those who abstain from taking what is not given... those who abstain from sexual misconduct... those who abstain from false speech... those who abstain from divisive speech associate and come together with those who abstain from divisive speech; those who abstain from harsh speech associate and come together with those who abstain from harsh speech; those who abstain from idle chatter associate and come together with those who abstain from idle chatter.' Fourth.

5. Dasakammapathasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Ten Courses of Action

111. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0152][M 1.0378] viharati…pe… “dhātusova[P 2.0168], bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Pāṇātipātino pāṇātipātīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; adinnādāyino…pe… kāmesumicchācārino… musāvādino… pisuṇavācā… pharusavācā… samphappalāpino samphappalāpīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; abhijjhāluno abhijjhālūhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; byāpannacittā byāpannacittehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

111. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, it is by element that beings associate and come together. Those who destroy life associate and come together with those who destroy life; those who take what is not given... those who engage in sexual misconduct... those who speak falsely... those who speak divisively... those who speak harshly... those who engage in idle chatter associate and come together with those who engage in idle chatter; the covetous associate and come together with the covetous; those with a mind of ill will associate and come together with those with a mind of ill will; those with wrong view associate and come together with those with wrong view.'

“Pāṇātipātā [T 2.0201] paṭiviratā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; adinnādānā paṭiviratā…pe… kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā… musāvādā paṭiviratā… pisuṇāya vācāya… pharusāya vācāya… samphappalāpā paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; anabhijjhāluno anabhijjhālūhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; abyāpannacittā abyāpannacittehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

'Those who abstain from destroying life associate and come together with those who abstain from destroying life; those who abstain from taking what is not given... those who abstain from sexual misconduct... those who abstain from false speech... those who abstain from divisive speech... those who abstain from harsh speech... those who abstain from idle chatter associate and come together with those who abstain from idle chatter; the uncovetous associate and come together with the uncovetous; those with minds free from ill will associate and come together with those with minds free from ill will; those with right view associate and come together with those with right view.' Fifth.

6. Aṭṭhaṅgikasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Eight Factors

112. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; micchāsaṅkappā…pe… micchāvācā… micchākammantā… micchāājīvā… micchāvāyāmā… micchāsatino [V 1.0153]… micchāsamādhino micchāsamādhīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti. Sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; sammāsaṅkappā…pe… sammāvācā… sammākammantā… sammāājīvā… sammāvāyāmā… sammāsatino… sammāsamādhino sammāsamādhīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

112. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those with wrong view associate and come together with those with wrong view; those with wrong thought… those with wrong speech… those with wrong action… those with wrong livelihood… those with wrong effort… those with wrong mindfulness… those with wrong concentration associate and come together with those with wrong concentration. Those with right view associate and come together with those with right view; those with right thought… those with right speech… those with right action… those with right livelihood… those with right effort… those with right mindfulness… those with right concentration associate and come together with those with right concentration.” The sixth.

7. Dasaṅgasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Ten Factors

113. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dhātusova, bhikkhave, sattā saṃsandanti samenti. Micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; micchāsaṅkappā…pe… micchāvācā… micchākammantā… micchāājīvā… micchāvāyāmā… micchāsatino [M 1.0379]… micchāsamādhino [T 2.0202][P 2.0169] micchāsamādhīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; micchāñāṇino micchāñāṇīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; micchāvimuttino micchāvimuttīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti”.

113. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, beings associate and come together by way of element. Those with wrong view associate and come together with those with wrong view; those with wrong thought… those with wrong speech… those with wrong action… those with wrong livelihood… those with wrong effort… those with wrong mindfulness… those with wrong concentration associate and come together with those with wrong concentration; those with wrong knowledge associate and come together with those with wrong knowledge; those with wrong liberation associate and come together with those with wrong liberation.”

“Sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikehi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; sammāsaṅkappā…pe… sammāvācā… sammākammantā… sammāājīvā… sammāvāyāmā… sammāsatino… sammāsamādhino… sammāñāṇino sammāñāṇīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samenti; sammāvimuttino sammāvimuttīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanti samentī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Those with right view associate and come together with those with right view; those with right thought… those with right speech… those with right action… those with right livelihood… those with right effort… those with right mindfulness… those with right concentration… those with right knowledge associate and come together with those with right knowledge; those with right liberation associate and come together with those with right liberation.” The seventh.

Sattannaṃ suttantānaṃ uddānaṃ –

The summary verse for the seven suttas:

Asamāhitaṃ [V 1.0154] dussīlaṃ, pañca sikkhāpadāni ca;

Satta kammapathā vuttā, dasakammapathena ca;

Chaṭṭhaṃ aṭṭhaṅgiko vutto, dasaṅgena ca sattamaṃ.

Unconcentrated and Immoral, and the Five Precepts; The Seven Courses of Action are taught, and also the Ten Courses of Action; The sixth is called the Eight-Factored, and the seventh the Ten-Factored.

Kammapathavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on the Courses of Action is concluded.

4. Catutthavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter

1. Catudhātusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Four Elements

114. Ekaṃ [T 2.0203] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme…pe… “catasso imā, bhikkhave, dhātuyo. Katamā catasso? Pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu – imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso dhātuyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

114. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park… “Bhikkhus, there are these four elements. Which four? The earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the four elements.” The first.

2. Pubbesambodhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse Before Enlightenment

115. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “pubbeva [P 2.0170] me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho pathavīdhātuyā assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko āpodhātuyā assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko tejodhātuyā [M 1.0380] assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko vāyodhātuyā assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’”nti?

115. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still a Bodhisatta who was not yet fully enlightened, this thought occurred to me: ‘What is the gratification in the earth element, what is the drawback, and what is the escape? What is the gratification in the water element, what is the drawback, and what is the escape? What is the gratification in the fire element, what is the drawback, and what is the escape? What is the gratification in the air element, what is the drawback, and what is the escape?’”

“Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yaṃ kho pathavīdhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ pathavīdhātuyā assādo; yaṃ yā (sī.) pathavīdhātu aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ pathavīdhātuyā ādīnavo; yo pathavīdhātuyā chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ pathavīdhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ āpodhātuṃ paṭicca…pe… yaṃ tejodhātuṃ paṭicca…pe… yaṃ vāyodhātuṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ vāyodhātuyā assādo; yaṃ vāyodhātu aniccā [V 1.0155] dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ vāyodhātuyā ādīnavo; yo vāyodhātuyā chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ vāyodhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ’”.

“Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘Whatever pleasure and joy arise in dependence on the earth element, this is the gratification in the earth element. That the earth element is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, this is the drawback in the earth element. The removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for the earth element, this is the escape from the earth element. Whatever pleasure and joy arise in dependence on the water element… in dependence on the fire element… in dependence on the air element, this is the gratification in the air element. That the air element is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, this is the drawback in the air element. The removal of desire and lust, the abandoning of desire and lust for the air element, this is the escape from the air element.’”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ[T 2.0204], bhikkhave, imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ na abbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti abhisambuddho (sī. syā. kaṃ.) paccaññāsiṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not directly know, as it really is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, for so long, bhikkhus, I did not claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans.

“Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca [P 2.0171] pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (sī. pī. ka.), ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“But, bhikkhus, when I directly knew, as it really is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, then, bhikkhus, I claimed to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation of mind. This is the last birth. Now there is no further becoming.’” The second.

3. Acariṃsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Search

116. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “pathavīdhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ, yo pathavīdhātuyā assādo tadajjhagamaṃ, yāvatā pathavīdhātuyā assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Pathavīdhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ, yo pathavīdhātuyā ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ[M 1.0381], yāvatā pathavīdhātuyā ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Pathavīdhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ, yaṃ pathavīdhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ, yāvatā pathavīdhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ”.

116. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in the earth element. Whatever gratification there is in the earth element, that I discovered. To whatever extent there is gratification in the earth element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the drawback in the earth element. Whatever drawback there is in the earth element, that I discovered. To whatever extent there is a drawback in the earth element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from the earth element. Whatever escape there is from the earth element, that I discovered. To whatever extent there is an escape from the earth element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom.”

“Āpodhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave…pe… tejodhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave… vāyodhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ [T 2.0205] acariṃ, yo vāyodhātuyā assādo tadajjhagamaṃ, yāvatā vāyodhātuyā assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Vāyodhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ, yo vāyodhātuyā ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ, yāvatā vāyodhātuyā ādīnavo paññāya me so [V 1.0156] sudiṭṭho. Vāyodhātuyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ, yaṃ vāyodhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ, yāvatā vāyodhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ.

“Monks, concerning the water element… concerning the fire element… Monks, I sought the gratification in the air element. Whatever gratification there is in the air element, that I attained. To whatever extent there is gratification in the air element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Monks, I sought the drawback in the air element. Whatever drawback there is in the air element, that I attained. To whatever extent there is a drawback in the air element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Monks, I sought the escape from the air element. Whatever escape there is from the air element, that I attained. To whatever extent there is an escape from the air element, that has been well seen by me with wisdom.”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ na abbhaññāsiṃ, neva [P 2.0172] tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ.

“Monks, for as long as I did not directly know, as it truly is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, for so long, Monks, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans.”

“Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“But when, Monks, I directly knew, as it truly is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, then, Monks, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation. This is the final birth. Now there is no more renewed existence.’” The Third.

4. Nocedaṃsuttaṃ

4. 4. The Discourse on 'If This Were Not'

117. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā pathavīdhātuyā sārajjeyyuṃ[T 2.0206]. Yasmā [M 1.0382] ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi pathavīdhātuyā assādo, tasmā sattā pathavīdhātuyā sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi pathavīdhātuyā ādīnavo, tasmā sattā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā pathavīdhātuyā nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi pathavīdhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā pathavīdhātuyā nissaranti”.

117. At Sāvatthī… “Monks, if there were no gratification in the earth element, beings would not be infatuated with the earth element. But because there is gratification in the earth element, beings are infatuated with the earth element. If, monks, there were no drawback in the earth element, beings would not become disenchanted with the earth element. But because there is a drawback in the earth element, beings become disenchanted with the earth element. If, monks, there were no escape from the earth element, beings would not escape from the earth element. But because there is an escape from the earth element, beings escape from the earth element.”

“No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, āpodhātuyā assādo abhavissa…pe… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, tejodhātuyā…pe… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, vāyodhātuyā assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā vāyodhātuyā sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi vāyodhātuyā assādo, tasmā sattā vāyodhātuyā sārajjanti. No [P 2.0173] cedaṃ, bhikkhave, vāyodhātuyā ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ [V 1.0157] sattā vāyodhātuyā nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi vāyodhātuyā ādīnavo, tasmā sattā vāyodhātuyā nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, vāyodhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā vāyodhātuyā nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi vāyodhātuyā nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā vāyodhātuyā nissaranti.

“Monks, if there were no gratification in the water element… if, monks, in the fire element… if, monks, there were no gratification in the air element, beings would not be infatuated with the air element. But because there is gratification in the air element, beings are infatuated with the air element. If, monks, there were no drawback in the air element, beings would not become disenchanted with the air element. But because there is a drawback in the air element, beings become disenchanted with the air element. If, monks, there were no escape from the air element, beings would not escape from the air element. But because there is an escape from the air element, beings escape from the air element.”

“Yāvakīvañcime, bhikkhave, sattā imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ na abbhaññaṃsu, neva tāvime bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā [T 2.0207] samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaṃyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādikatena cetasā vihariṃsu.

“Monks, for as long as these beings had not directly known, as it truly is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, for so long, monks, these beings had not escaped, were not disjoined, and were not liberated from this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans; they did not dwell with a mind made boundless.

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaṃyuttā vippamuttā vimariyādikatena cetasā viharantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“But when, monks, beings have directly known, as it truly is, the gratification in these four elements as gratification, the drawback as drawback, and the escape as escape, then, monks, beings have escaped, become disjoined, and are liberated from this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, and they dwell with a mind made boundless.” The Fourth.

5. Ekantadukkhasuttaṃ

5. 5. The Discourse on What is Entirely Suffering

118. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0383] viharati…pe… “pathavīdhātu ce ca (sī. syā. kaṃ.) hidaṃ, bhikkhave, ekantadukkhā abhavissa dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā pathavīdhātuyā sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātu sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā pathavīdhātuyā sārajjanti”.

118. At Sāvatthī… “Monks, if this earth element were entirely suffering, attended by suffering, steeped in suffering, and not steeped in pleasure, beings would not be attached to this earth element. But because, monks, the earth element is pleasure, attended by pleasure, steeped in pleasure, and not steeped in suffering, beings are attached to the earth element.”

“Āpodhātu [P 2.0174] ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave…pe… tejodhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave… vāyodhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave, ekantadukkhā abhavissa dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, nayidaṃ sattā vāyodhātuyā sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vāyodhātu sukhā sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, tasmā sattā vāyodhātuyā sārajjanti.

“Monks, if this water element… if this fire element… if this air element were entirely suffering, attended by suffering, steeped in suffering, and not steeped in pleasure, beings would not be attached to this air element. But because, monks, the air element is pleasure, attended by pleasure, steeped in pleasure, and not steeped in suffering, beings are attached to the air element.”

“Pathavīdhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave, ekantasukhā abhavissa sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā [V 1.0158] dukkhena, nayidaṃ sattā pathavīdhātuyā [T 2.0208] nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātu dukkhā dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, tasmā sattā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindanti.

“Bhikkhus, if this earth element were exclusively pleasant, followed by pleasure, steeped in pleasure, and not steeped in suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with this earth element. But because, bhikkhus, the earth element is suffering, followed by suffering, steeped in suffering, and not steeped in pleasure, beings therefore become disenchanted with the earth element.”

“Āpodhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave…pe… tejodhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave… vāyodhātu ce hidaṃ, bhikkhave, ekantasukhā abhavissa sukhānupatitā sukhāvakkantā anavakkantā dukkhena, nayidaṃ sattā vāyodhātuyā nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vāyodhātu dukkhā dukkhānupatitā dukkhāvakkantā anavakkantā sukhena, tasmā sattā vāyodhātuyā nibbindantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if this water element… if this fire element… if this air element were exclusively pleasant, followed by pleasure, steeped in pleasure, and not steeped in suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with this air element. But because, bhikkhus, the air element is suffering, followed by suffering, steeped in suffering, and not steeped in pleasure, beings therefore become disenchanted with the air element.”

6. Abhinandasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Delighting

119. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “yo, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo āpodhātuṃ abhinandati…pe… yo tejodhātuṃ… yo vāyodhātuṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi”.

119. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the water element… one who delights in the fire element… one who delights in the air element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering.”

“Yo [M 1.0384][P 2.0175] ca kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo āpodhātuṃ…pe… yo tejodhātuṃ… yo vāyodhātuṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“But, bhikkhus, one who does not delight in the earth element does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the water element… one who does not delight in the fire element… one who does not delight in the air element does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

7. Uppādasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Arising

120. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “yo, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā [T 2.0209] uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṃ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo āpodhātuyā…pe… yo tejodhātuyā… yo vāyodhātuyā uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo rogānaṃ ṭhiti jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo”.

120. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever arising, establishment, re-becoming, and manifestation there is of the earth element, that is the arising of suffering, the establishment of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Whatever arising… of the water element… of the fire element… Whatever arising, establishment, re-becoming, and manifestation there is of the air element, that is the arising of suffering, the establishment of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.”

“Yo [V 1.0159] ca kho, bhikkhave, pathavīdhātuyā nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṃ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo āpodhātuyā…pe… yo tejodhātuyā… yo vāyodhātuyā nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho rogānaṃ vūpasamo jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And whatever, bhikkhus, is the cessation, calming, and disappearance of the earth element, that is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Whatever cessation… of the water element… of the fire element… Whatever is the cessation, calming, and disappearance of the air element, that is the cessation of suffering, the calming of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.”

8. Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

121. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “catasso imā, bhikkhave, dhātuyo. Katamā catasso? Pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ [P 2.0176] nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā; na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti”.

121. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four elements. Which four? The earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element. Whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, do not understand as it really is the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these four elements, those ascetics or brahmins are not, in my view, considered ascetics among ascetics, nor brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones do not dwell having, in this very life, realized for themselves through direct knowledge, attained, and entered upon the goal of an ascetic or the goal of a brahmin.”

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti[T 2.0210], te ca kho [M 1.0385] me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā; te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“But whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, understand as it really is the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these four elements, those ascetics or brahmins are, in my view, considered ascetics among ascetics, and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones dwell having, in this very life, realized for themselves through direct knowledge, attained, and entered upon the goal of an ascetic and the goal of a brahmin.”

9. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

122. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “catasso imā, bhikkhave, dhātuyo. Katamā catasso? Pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imāsaṃ catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti…pe… pajānanti…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

122. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four elements. Which four? The earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element. Whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, do not understand as it really is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these four elements… to be elaborated… those who understand… they dwell having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, attained, and entered upon it.”

10. Tatiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

10. The Third Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

123. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0160] viharati…pe… “ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā pathavīdhātuṃ nappajānanti, pathavīdhātusamudayaṃ nappajānanti, pathavīdhātunirodhaṃ nappajānanti, pathavīdhātunirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti…pe… āpodhātuṃ [P 2.0177] nappajānanti… tejodhātuṃ nappajānanti… vāyodhātuṃ nappajānanti, vāyodhātusamudayaṃ nappajānanti, vāyodhātunirodhaṃ nappajānanti, vāyodhātunirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā; na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti”.

123. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand the earth element, do not understand the origin of the earth element, do not understand the cessation of the earth element, and do not understand the path leading to the cessation of the earth element… who do not understand the water element… the fire element… the air element, do not understand the origin of the air element, do not understand the cessation of the air element, and do not understand the path leading to the cessation of the air element—those ascetics or brahmins are not, in my view, considered ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. Nor do those venerable ones dwell having, in this very life, realized for themselves with direct knowledge the goal of an ascetic or the goal of a brahmin, and having attained it.”

“Ye [T 2.0211] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā pathavīdhātuṃ pajānanti, pathavīdhātusamudayaṃ pajānanti, pathavīdhātunirodhaṃ pajānanti, pathavīdhātunirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti… ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā…pe… āpodhātuṃ pajānanti… tejodhātuṃ pajānanti… vāyodhātuṃ pajānanti, vāyodhātusamudayaṃ pajānanti, vāyodhātunirodhaṃ pajānanti, vāyodhātunirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, te [M 1.0386] ca kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā; te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand the earth element, understand the origin of the earth element, understand the cessation of the earth element, and understand the path leading to the cessation of the earth element… and whatever ascetics or brahmins… understand the water element… the fire element… the air element, understand the origin of the air element, understand the cessation of the air element, and understand the path leading to the cessation of the air element—those ascetics and brahmins are reckoned as ascetics among ascetics and as brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, having realized for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life the state of an ascetic and the state of a brahmin, dwell having attained it.” The Tenth.

Catuttho vaggo.

The Fourth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Catasso pubbe acariṃ, nocedañca dukkhena ca;

Abhinandañca uppādo, tayo samaṇabrāhmaṇāti.

Four, Formerly, Teacher, If Not This, and With Suffering; And Delight, Arising, and the three on Ascetics and Brahmins.

Dhātusaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Elements is concluded.

4. Anamataggasaṃyuttaṃ

4. The Connected Discourses on the Unascertainable Beginning

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Tiṇakaṭṭhasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Grass and Wood

124. Evaṃ [T 2.0212][V 1.0161][P 2.0178][M 1.0387] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

124. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Anamataggoyaṃ anamataggāyaṃ (pī. ka.) bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso yaṃ imasmiṃ jambudīpe tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ taṃ chetvā tacchetvā (bahūsu) ekajjhaṃ saṃharitvā caturaṅgulaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ ghaṭikaṃ katvā nikkhipeyya – ‘ayaṃ me mātā, tassā me mātu ayaṃ mātā’ti, apariyādinnāva apariyādiṇṇāva (sī.) bhikkhave, tassa purisassa mātumātaro assu, atha imasmiṃ jambudīpe tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Evaṃ dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ tibbaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ byasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, kaṭasī kaṭasi (sī. pī. ka.) kaṭā chavā sayanti etthāti kaṭasī vaḍḍhitā. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ alaṃ virajjituṃ alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is of unascertainable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering through. Suppose, bhikkhus, a man were to cut up whatever grass, wood, branches, and leaves there are in this Jambudīpa, and having gathered them together into one pile and made them into four-finger-length pieces, he were to lay them down, saying: ‘This is my mother; this is that mother’s mother of mine.’ The mothers of that man’s mother would not be exhausted, bhikkhus, yet the grass, wood, branches, and leaves in this Jambudīpa would be consumed and exhausted. For what reason? This saṃsāra, bhikkhus, is of unascertainable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering through. For such a long time, bhikkhus, you have experienced suffering, you have experienced severity, you have experienced calamity, and the charnel grounds have been added to. This is enough, bhikkhus, to become disenchanted with all formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.” The First.

2. Pathavīsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Earth

125. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 2.0179] viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave[T 2.0213], saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati [V 1.0162] avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ kolaṭṭhimattaṃ kolaṭṭhimattaṃ mattikāguḷikaṃ karitvā nikkhipeyya – ‘ayaṃ me pitā, tassa me pitu ayaṃ pitā’ti, apariyādinnāva bhikkhave, tassa purisassa pitupitaro assu, athāyaṃ mahāpathavī parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya[M 1.0388]. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Evaṃ dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ tibbaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ byasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, kaṭasī vaḍḍhitā. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

125. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without a discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving. Suppose, bhikkhus, a man were to make this great earth into clay balls, each the size of a jujube seed, and set them down, saying: ‘This is my father; this is my father’s father.’ The line of that man’s fathers and forefathers would not be exhausted, bhikkhus, yet this great earth would come to an end, to exhaustion. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without a discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving. For such a long time, bhikkhus, you have experienced suffering, experienced intense suffering, experienced calamity, and the charnel grounds have grown. It is enough, bhikkhus, to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.” The Second.

3. Assusuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Tears

126. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ, yaṃ vā vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ amanāpasampayogā manāpavippayogā kandantānaṃ rodantānaṃ rudantānaṃ (sī.) assu passannaṃ passandaṃ (ka. sī.), pasandaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), pasannaṃ (pī. ka.) paggharitaṃ, yaṃ vā catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti? “Yathā kho mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāma, etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ yaṃ no iminā [P 2.0180] dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ amanāpasampayogā manāpavippayogā kandantānaṃ rodantānaṃ assu passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti.

126. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without a discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: the tears that have flowed from you while roaming and wandering on through this long course, lamenting and weeping because of association with the disagreeable and separation from the agreeable—or the water in the four great oceans?” “As we understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, venerable sir, this indeed is more: the tears that have flowed from us while roaming and wandering on through this long course, lamenting and weeping because of association with the disagreeable and separation from the agreeable—not the water in the four great oceans.”

“Sādhu [T 2.0214] sādhu, bhikkhave, sādhu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha. Etadeva, bhikkhave, bahutaraṃ yaṃ vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ amanāpasampayogā manāpavippayogā kandantānaṃ rodantānaṃ assu passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, mātumaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ; tesaṃ vā mātumaraṇaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ amanāpasampayogā manāpavippayogā kandantānaṃ rodantānaṃ assu passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, pitumaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ …pe… bhātumaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ… bhaginimaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ… puttamaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ… dhītumaraṇaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ… ñātibyasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ… bhogabyasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave[V 1.0163], rogabyasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, tesaṃ vo rogabyasanaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ amanāpasampayogā manāpavippayogā kandantānaṃ rodantānaṃ assu passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro [M 1.0389] …pe… yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Good, good, monks! It is good that you understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way. Monks, the tears you have shed that have flowed while running on and wandering through this long course—lamenting and weeping because of association with the disagreeable and separation from the agreeable—are more abundant, and not the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, monks, you have experienced the death of a mother. For you who have experienced the death of a mother, lamenting and weeping because of association with the disagreeable and separation from the agreeable, the tears you have shed that have flowed are more abundant, and not the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, monks, you have experienced the death of a father… the death of a brother… the death of a sister… the death of a son… the death of a daughter… the loss of relatives… the loss of wealth. For a long time, monks, you have experienced the calamity of disease. For you who have experienced the calamity of disease, lamenting and weeping because of association with the disagreeable and separation from the agreeable, the tears you have shed that have flowed are more abundant, and not the water in the four great oceans. For what reason? This saṃsāra, monks, is without a discoverable beginning… It is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.” The Third.

4. Khīrasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Milk

127. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ, yaṃ vā vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ [P 2.0181] saṃsarataṃ mātuthaññaṃ pītaṃ, yaṃ vā catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti? “Yathā kho mayaṃ[T 2.0215], bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāma, etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ yaṃ no iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ mātuthaññaṃ pītaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti.

127. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Monks, this saṃsāra is without a discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering. What do you think, monks? Which is more: the mother's milk that you have drunk while running on and wandering through this long course, or the water in the four great oceans?” “Venerable Sir, as we understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is this, venerable sir, that is more: the mother's milk that we have drunk while running on and wandering through this long course. The water in the four great oceans is not more.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave, sādhu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha. Etadeva, bhikkhave, bahutaraṃ yaṃ vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ mātuthaññaṃ pītaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Good, good, monks! It is good that you understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way. Monks, the mother's milk that you have drunk while running on and wandering through this long course is more abundant, and not the water in the four great oceans. For what reason? This saṃsāra, monks, is without a discoverable beginning… it is enough to be liberated.” The Fourth.

5. Pabbatasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Mountain

128. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… ārāme. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kīvadīgho nu kho, bhante, kappo”ti? “Dīgho kho, bhikkhu, kappo. So na sukaro saṅkhātuṃ ettakāni vassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassāni iti vā”ti.

128. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī… Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: ‘How long indeed, venerable sir, is an eon?’ ‘Long indeed, monk, is an eon. It is not easy to count it as so many years, or as so many hundreds of years, or as so many thousands of years, or as so many hundreds of thousands of years.’”

“Sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā, bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca. “Seyyathāpi[V 1.0164], bhikkhu, mahāselo pabbato yojanaṃ āyāmena yojanaṃ vitthārena yojanaṃ ubbedhena acchinno asusiro ekagghano. Tamenaṃ puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena kāsikena vatthena [M 1.0390] sakiṃ sakiṃ parimajjeyya. Khippataraṃ kho so, bhikkhu, mahāselo pabbato iminā upakkamena parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya[T 2.0216], na tveva kappo. Evaṃ dīgho, bhikkhu, kappo. Evaṃ dīghānaṃ kho, bhikkhu[P 2.0182], kappānaṃ neko kappo saṃsito, nekaṃ kappasataṃ saṃsitaṃ, nekaṃ kappasahassaṃ saṃsitaṃ, nekaṃ kappasatasahassaṃ saṃsitaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhu, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi…pe… yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhu, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“But is it possible, venerable sir, to make a simile?” “It is possible, monk,” the Blessed One said. “Suppose, monk, there were a great rocky mountain—a yojana in length, a yojana in width, a yojana in height—without cracks, without hollows, one solid mass. A man, after the passing of every hundred years, would wipe it once with a cloth from Kāsi. That great rocky mountain, monk, would by this effort more quickly come to an end and be exhausted, but not the eon. So long, monk, is an eon. And of such long eons, monk, not just one eon has been wandered through, not just one hundred eons, not just one thousand eons, not just one hundred thousand eons have been wandered through. For what reason? This saṃsāra, monk, is without a discoverable beginning. A first point… It is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.” The Fifth.

6. Sāsapasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Mustard Seed

129. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kīvadīgho, nu kho, bhante, kappo”ti? “Dīgho kho, bhikkhu, kappo. So na sukaro saṅkhātuṃ ettakāni vassāni iti vā…pe… ettakāni vassasatasahassāni iti vā”ti.

129. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk went to the Blessed One… Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, how long is an eon?’ ‘Long, monk, is an eon. It is not easy to count it as so many years… or as so many hundreds of thousands of years.’”

“Sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā, bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, āyasaṃ nagaraṃ yojanaṃ āyāmena yojanaṃ vitthārena yojanaṃ ubbedhena, puṇṇaṃ sāsapānaṃ guḷikābaddhaṃ cūḷikābaddhaṃ (sī. pī.). Tato puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena ekamekaṃ sāsapaṃ uddhareyya. Khippataraṃ kho so, bhikkhu mahāsāsaparāsi iminā upakkamena parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, na tveva kappo. Evaṃ dīgho kho, bhikkhu, kappo. Evaṃ dīghānaṃ kho, bhikkhu, kappānaṃ neko kappo saṃsito, nekaṃ kappasataṃ saṃsitaṃ, nekaṃ kappasahassaṃ saṃsitaṃ, nekaṃ kappasatasahassaṃ saṃsitaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhu, saṃsāro [T 2.0217] …pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Venerable sir, is it possible to make a comparison?” “It is possible, monk,” the Blessed One said. “Suppose, monk, there were an iron city a yojana in length, a yojana in width, and a yojana in height, full of mustard seeds packed into a solid mass. From there a man would take out a single mustard seed at the passing of every hundred years. That great heap of mustard seeds, monk, would by this effort be more quickly exhausted and depleted, but not so the eon. So long, monk, is an eon. Of such long eons, monk, not just one eon has been wandered through, not just one hundred eons, not just one thousand eons, not just one hundred thousand eons. For what reason? This saṃsāra, monk, is of an inconceivable beginning… It is enough to be liberated.” The sixth.

7. Sāvakasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Disciples

130. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha [P 2.0183] kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā…pe… ekamantaṃ [V 1.0165] nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kīvabahukā nu kho, bhante, kappā abbhatītā atikkantā”ti? “Bahukā kho, bhikkhave[M 1.0391], kappā abbhatītā atikkantā. Te na sukarā saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakā kappā iti vā, ettakāni kappasatāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasatasahassāni iti vā’”ti.

130. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then a number of monks went to the Blessed One… Seated to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how many are the eons that have passed and gone by?” “Many, monks, are the eons that have passed and gone by. It is not easy to count them as: ‘so many eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of eons,’ or ‘so many thousands of eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of eons.’”

“Sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā, bhikkhave”ti bhagavā avoca. “Idhassu, bhikkhave, cattāro sāvakā vassasatāyukā vassasatajīvino. Te divase divase kappasatasahassaṃ kappasatasahassaṃ anussareyyuṃ. Ananussaritāva bhikkhave, tehi kappā assu, atha kho te cattāro sāvakā vassasatāyukā vassasatajīvino vassasatassa accayena kālaṃ kareyyuṃ. Evaṃ bahukā kho, bhikkhave, kappā abbhatītā atikkantā. Te na sukarā saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakā kappā iti vā, ettakāni kappasatāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasatasahassāni iti vā’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, is it possible to make a comparison?” “It is possible, monks,” the Blessed One said. “Suppose, monks, there were four disciples, each with a lifespan of a hundred years, living for a hundred years. Each day, they would recollect one hundred thousand eons. The eons would not yet have been fully recollected by them, monks, when those four disciples, each with a lifespan of a hundred years, living for a hundred years, would pass away at the end of a hundred years. So very many, monks, are the eons that have passed and gone by. It is not easy to count them as: ‘so many eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of eons,’ or ‘so many thousands of eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of eons.’ For what reason? This saṃsāra, monks, is of an inconceivable beginning… It is enough to be liberated.” The seventh.

8. Gaṅgāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Ganges

131. Rājagahe viharati veḷuvane. Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 2.0218] bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kīvabahukā nu kho, bho gotama, kappā abbhatītā atikkantā”ti? “Bahukā kho, brāhmaṇa, kappā abbhatītā atikkantā. Te na sukarā saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakā kappā iti vā, ettakāni kappasatāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasatasahassāni iti vā’”ti.

131. He was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove. Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded their courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: “How many eons, Master Gotama, have passed and gone by?” “Many, brahmin, are the eons that have passed and gone by. It is not easy to count them as: ‘so many eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of eons,’ or ‘so many thousands of eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of eons.’”

“Sakkā [P 2.0184] pana, bho gotama, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā, brāhmaṇā”ti bhagavā avoca. “Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, yato cāyaṃ gaṅgā nadī pabhavati yattha ca mahāsamuddaṃ appeti, yā etasmiṃ antare vālikā sā na sukarā saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakā vālikā iti vā, ettakāni vālikasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vālikasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vālikasatasahassāni [V 1.0166] iti vā’ti. Tato bahutarā kho, brāhmaṇa, kappā abbhatītā atikkantā. Te na sukarā saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakā kappā iti [M 1.0392] vā, ettakāni kappasatāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni kappasatasahassāni iti vā’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, brāhmaṇa, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Evaṃ dīgharattaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, dukkhaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ tibbaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ byasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, kaṭasī vaḍḍhitā. Yāvañcidaṃ[T 2.0219], brāhmaṇa, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti.

“Master Gotama, is it possible to make a comparison?” “It is possible, brahmin,” the Blessed One said. “Suppose, brahmin, from where this Ganges river originates to where it enters the great ocean, the sand in between is not easy to count as: ‘so many grains of sand,’ or ‘so many hundreds of grains of sand,’ or ‘so many thousands of grains of sand,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of grains of sand.’ More numerous than that, brahmin, are the eons that have passed and gone by. They are not easy to count as: ‘so many eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of eons,’ or ‘so many thousands of eons,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of eons.’ For what reason? This saṃsāra, brahmin, is of an inconceivable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings veiled by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering through. Thus for a long time, brahmin, suffering has been experienced, severity has been experienced, calamity has been experienced, and the charnel ground has grown. This is enough, brahmin, to become disenchanted with all conditioned things, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.”

Evaṃ vutte, so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

When this was said, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! … May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, beginning from today.” The eighth.

9. Daṇḍasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Stick

132. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, daṇḍo uparivehāsaṃ khitto sakimpi mūlena nipatati, sakimpi majjhena nipatati, sakimpi antena nipatati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, avijjānīvaraṇā [P 2.0185] sattā taṇhāsaṃyojanā sandhāvantā saṃsarantā sakimpi asmā lokā paraṃ lokaṃ gacchanti, sakimpi parasmā lokā imaṃ lokaṃ āgacchanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Navamaṃ.

132. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Monks, this saṃsāra is of an inconceivable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings veiled by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering through. Just as, monks, a stick thrown up into the air sometimes falls on its base and sometimes on its tip; in the same way, monks, beings veiled by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and wandering through, sometimes go from this world to another world, and sometimes come from another world to this world. For what reason? This saṃsāra, monks, is of an inconceivable beginning… It is enough to be liberated.” The ninth.

10. Puggalasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Person

133. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

133. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak mountain. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Anamataggoyaṃ[V 1.0167], bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, kappaṃ sandhāvato saṃsarato siyā evaṃ mahā aṭṭhikaṅkalo aṭṭhipuñjo aṭṭhirāsi yathāyaṃ vepullo pabbato, sace [T 2.0220] saṃhārako assa, sambhatañca na vinasseyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti.

“Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning… For a single person, bhikkhus, transmigrating and wandering on for an eon, there could be a great skeleton, a pile of bones, a mound of bones as large as this Mount Vepulla, if there were a collector for it and the collection did not perish. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning… it is enough to be liberated.”

Idamavoca [M 1.0393] bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Gone One, the Teacher, further said this:

“Ekassekena kappena, puggalassaṭṭhisañcayo;

Siyā pabbatasamo rāsi, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā.

“The collection of bones of a single person over one eon would be a heap the size of a mountain,” so it has been said by the Great Seer.

“So kho panāyaṃ akkhāto, vepullo pabbato mahā;

Uttaro gijjhakūṭassa, magadhānaṃ giribbaje.

“This great mountain, Vepulla, is declared to be north of Vulture Peak in Giribbaja of the Magadhans.

“Yato ca ariyasaccāni, sammappaññāya passati;

Dukkhaṃ dukkhasamuppādaṃ, dukkhassa ca atikkamaṃ;

Ariyaṃ caṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, dukkhūpasamagāminaṃ.

“But when one sees with right wisdom the Noble Truths—suffering, the origin of suffering, the overcoming of suffering, and the Noble Eightfold Path leading to the stilling of suffering—

“Sa sattakkhattuṃparamaṃ, sandhāvitvāna puggalo;

Dukkhassantakaro [P 2.0186] hoti, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayā”ti. dasamaṃ;

“That person, having transmigrated for at most seven times, makes an end of suffering through the destruction of all fetters.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Tiṇakaṭṭhañca pathavī, assu khīrañca pabbataṃ;

Sāsapā sāvakā gaṅgā, daṇḍo ca puggalena cāti.

Grass and wood, and earth; tears, milk, and the mountain; mustard seeds, disciples, and the Ganges; and the stick, and the person.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Duggatasuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on the Unfortunate

134. Ekaṃ [T 2.0221][V 1.0168] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhu āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, passeyyātha duggataṃ durūpetaṃ niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘amhehipi evarūpaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ iminā dīghena addhunā’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu…pe… yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ alaṃ virajjituṃ alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

134. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings transmigrating and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving. Bhikkhus, should you see someone unfortunate and ill-favored, you should conclude: ‘We too have experienced such in this long course.’ For what reason? … Indeed, bhikkhus, it is quite enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned things, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.”

2. Sukhitasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on the Fortunate

135. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0394] viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… yaṃ, bhikkhave, passeyyātha sukhitaṃ susajjitaṃ, niṭṭhamettha [P 2.0187] gantabbaṃ – ‘amhehipi evarūpaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ iminā dīghena addhunā’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

135. Dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning… Bhikkhus, should you see someone fortunate and well-adorned, you should conclude: ‘We too have experienced such in this long course.’ For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned… enough to be liberated.”

3. Tiṃsamattasuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on the Thirty

136. Rājagahe viharati veḷuvane. Atha kho tiṃsamattā pāveyyakā pāṭheyyakā (katthaci) vinayapiṭake mahāvagge kathinakkhandhakepi bhikkhū sabbe āraññikā sabbe piṇḍapātikā sabbe paṃsukūlikā sabbe tecīvarikā sabbe sasaṃyojanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “ime kho tiṃsamattā pāveyyakā bhikkhū sabbe āraññikā sabbe piṇḍapātikā sabbe paṃsukūlikā [T 2.0222] sabbe tecīvarikā sabbe sasaṃyojanā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imesaṃ tathā dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ yathā nesaṃ imasmiṃyeva āsane anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucceyyu”nti. Atha [V 1.0169] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

136. Dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove. Then thirty bhikkhus from Pāvā—all forest-dwellers, all alms-food-eaters, all rag-robe-wearers, all triple-robe-wearers, all still with fetters—approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “These thirty bhikkhus from Pāvā are all forest-dwellers, all alms-food-eaters, all rag-robe-wearers, all triple-robe-wearers, all still with fetters. What if I were to teach them the Dhamma in such a way that, right here in this very seat, their minds would be liberated from the taints without clinging?” Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ, yaṃ vā vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, yaṃ vā catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti? “Yathā kho mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāma, etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yaṃ no iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ sīsacchinnānaṃ [P 2.0188] lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udaka”nti.

“Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings transmigrating and wandering on, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: the blood that has been shed and has flowed from you when your heads were cut off while transmigrating and wandering on in this long course, or the water in the four great oceans?” “Venerable sir, as we understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, this is indeed more: the blood that has been shed and has flowed from us when our heads were cut off while transmigrating and wandering on in this long course; not the water in the four great oceans.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave, sādhu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha. Etadeva, bhikkhave, bahutaraṃ, yaṃ vo iminā dīghena addhunā sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu [M 1.0395] udakaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, gunnaṃ sataṃ gobhūtānaṃ sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, mahiṃsānaṃ mahisānaṃ (sī. pī.) sataṃ mahiṃsabhūtānaṃ sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ [T 2.0223] …pe… dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, urabbhānaṃ sataṃ urabbhabhūtānaṃ…pe… ajānaṃ sataṃ ajabhūtānaṃ… migānaṃ sataṃ migabhūtānaṃ… kukkuṭānaṃ sataṃ kukkuṭabhūtānaṃ… sūkarānaṃ sataṃ sūkarabhūtānaṃ… dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, corā gāmaghātāti gahetvā sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, corā pāripanthikāti gahetvā sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ. Dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, corā pāradārikāti gahetvā sīsacchinnānaṃ lohitaṃ passannaṃ paggharitaṃ, na tveva catūsu mahāsamuddesu udakaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti.

“Good, good, bhikkhus! It is good, bhikkhus, that you understand the Dhamma taught by me in this way. This is indeed more, bhikkhus: the blood that has been shed and has flowed from you when your heads were cut off while transmigrating and wandering on in this long course; not the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, bhikkhus, while you were cows, the blood shed and flowed when your heads were cut off was more than the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, bhikkhus, while you were buffaloes… sheep… goats… deer… chickens… pigs, the blood shed and flowed when your heads were cut off was more than the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, bhikkhus, having been seized as village-plundering thieves, the blood shed and flowed when your heads were cut off was more than the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, bhikkhus, having been seized as highway-robbing thieves, the blood shed and flowed when your heads were cut off was more than the water in the four great oceans. For a long time, bhikkhus, having been seized as adulterous thieves, the blood shed and flowed when your heads were cut off was more than the water in the four great oceans. For what reason? This saṃsāra, bhikkhus, is without discoverable beginning…pe… it is enough to be liberated.”

“Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Imasmiñca [P 2.0189] pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tiṃsamattānaṃ pāveyyakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsū”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Those bhikkhus, satisfied, delighted in the Blessed One’s words. And while this exposition was being spoken, the minds of the thirty bhikkhus from Pāvā were liberated from the taints without clinging. The third.

4. Mātusuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Mother

137. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0170] viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo namātābhūtapubbo iminā dīghena addhunā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Catutthaṃ.

137. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning… It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been one's mother in this long journey. For what reason? This saṃsāra, bhikkhus, is without discoverable beginning… It is enough to be liberated.” The fourth.

5. Pitusuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Father

138. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro…pe… na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo napitābhūtapubbo [T 2.0224] …pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

138. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning… It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been one's father… It is enough to be liberated.” The fifth.

6. Bhātusuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Brother

139. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo nabhātābhūtapubbo…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

139. At Sāvatthī… “It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been one's brother… It is enough to be liberated.” The sixth.

7. Bhaginisuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Sister

140. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0396] viharati…pe… “na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo nabhaginibhūtapubbo…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Sattamaṃ.

140. At Sāvatthī… “It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been one's sister… It is enough to be liberated.” The seventh.

8. Puttasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Son

141. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 2.0190] viharati…pe… “na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo naputtabhūtapubbo…pe… alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

141. At Sāvatthī… “It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been one's son… It is enough to be liberated.” The eighth.

9. Dhītusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Daughter

142. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0171] viharati…pe… “anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Na so, bhikkhave, satto sulabharūpo yo na dhītābhūtapubbo iminā dīghena addhunā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Evaṃ dīgharattaṃ vo, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ tibbaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ byasanaṃ paccanubhūtaṃ, kaṭasī vaḍḍhitā. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti. Navamaṃ.

142. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are transmigrating and wandering on. It is not easy, bhikkhus, to find a being who has not formerly been a daughter in this long journey. For what reason? This saṃsāra, bhikkhus, is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are transmigrating and wandering on. For such a long time, bhikkhus, you have experienced suffering, you have experienced intense suffering, you have experienced disaster, and the charnel grounds have grown. Therefore, bhikkhus, it is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.” The ninth.

10. Vepullapabbatasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Vepulla Mountain

143. Ekaṃ [T 2.0225] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

143. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak Mountain. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘pācīnavaṃso’tveva samaññā udapādi. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave[P 2.0191], samayena manussānaṃ ‘tivarā’tveva samaññā udapādi. Tivarānaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ cattārīsa vassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ ahosi. Tivarā, bhikkhave, manussā pācīnavaṃsaṃ pabbataṃ catūhena ārohanti, catūhena orohanti. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave[M 1.0397], samayena kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti. Kakusandhassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa vidhurasañjīvaṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ ahosi aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto. Evaṃ aniccā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; evaṃ addhuvā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; evaṃ anassāsikā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccituṃ.

“Bhikkhus, this saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are transmigrating and wandering on. Formerly, bhikkhus, this Vepulla Mountain had the designation ‘Pācīnavaṃsa.’ At that time, bhikkhus, the people had the designation ‘Tivarā.’ The lifespan of the Tivarā people, bhikkhus, was forty thousand years. The Tivarā people, bhikkhus, would ascend Pācīnavaṃsa Mountain in four days and descend in four days. At that time, bhikkhus, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had arisen in the world. The Blessed One Kakusandha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had a foremost, auspicious pair of disciples named Vidhura and Sañjīva. See, bhikkhus, that very designation of this mountain has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Blessed One has attained final Nibbāna. So impermanent, bhikkhus, are conditioned formations; so unstable, bhikkhus, are conditioned formations; so without solace, bhikkhus, are conditioned formations. Therefore, bhikkhus, it is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ[V 1.0172], bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘vaṅkako’tveva [T 2.0226] samaññā udapādi. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena manussānaṃ ‘rohitassā’tveva samaññā udapādi. Rohitassānaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ tiṃsavassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ ahosi. Rohitassā, bhikkhave, manussā vaṅkakaṃ pabbataṃ tīhena ārohanti, tīhena orohanti. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena koṇāgamano bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti. Koṇāgamanassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa bhiyyosuttaraṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ ahosi aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto. Evaṃ [P 2.0192] aniccā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā…pe… alaṃ vimuccituṃ.

“Formerly, monks, this Vepulla Mountain had the designation ‘Vaṅkaka.’ At that time, monks, the people had the designation ‘Rohitassa.’ The lifespan of the Rohitassa people, monks, was thirty thousand years. The Rohitassa people, monks, would ascend Vaṅkaka Mountain in three days and descend in three days. At that time, monks, the Blessed One Koṇāgamana, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had arisen in the world. The Blessed One Koṇāgamana, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had a foremost, auspicious pair of disciples named Bhiyyosa and Uttara. See, monks, that very designation of this mountain has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Blessed One has attained final Nibbāna. So impermanent, monks, are conditioned formations… it is enough to be liberated.”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘supasso’tveva suphassotveva (sī.) samaññā udapādi. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena manussānaṃ ‘suppiyā’tveva appiyātveva (sī.) samaññā udapādi. Suppiyānaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ vīsativassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ ahosi. Suppiyā, bhikkhave, manussā supassaṃ pabbataṃ dvīhena ārohanti, dvīhena orohanti. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti. Kassapassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa tissabhāradvājaṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ ahosi aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto. Evaṃ aniccā[T 2.0227], bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; evaṃ addhuvā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā…pe… alaṃ vimuccituṃ.

“Formerly, monks, this Vepulla Mountain had the designation ‘Supassa.’ At that time, monks, the people had the designation ‘Suppiya.’ The lifespan of the Suppiya people, monks, was twenty thousand years. The Suppiya people, monks, would ascend Supassa Mountain in two days and descend in two days. At that time, monks, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had arisen in the world. The Blessed One Kassapa, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had a foremost, auspicious pair of disciples named Tissa and Bhāradvāja. See, monks, that very designation of this mountain has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Blessed One has attained final Nibbāna. So impermanent, monks, are conditioned formations; so unstable, monks, are conditioned formations… it is enough to be liberated.”

“Etarahi [M 1.0398] kho pana, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘vepullo’tveva samaññā udapādi. Etarahi kho pana, bhikkhave, imesaṃ manussānaṃ ‘māgadhakā’tveva samaññā udapādi. Māgadhakānaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ appakaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ parittaṃ lahukaṃ lahusaṃ (sī.); yo ciraṃ jīvati so vassasataṃ appaṃ vā bhiyyo.
