Māgadhakā, bhikkhave, manussā vepullaṃ pabbataṃ muhuttena ārohanti muhuttena orohanti. Etarahi kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno. Mayhaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, sāriputtamoggallānaṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Bhavissati, bhikkhave, so samayo yā ayañcevimassa pabbatassa [P 2.0193] samaññā antaradhāyissati, ime [V 1.0173] ca manussā kālaṃ karissanti, ahañca parinibbāyissāmi. Evaṃ aniccā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; evaṃ addhuvā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; evaṃ anassāsikā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccitu”nti.

“But now, monks, this Vepulla Mountain has the designation ‘Vepulla.’ And now, monks, these people have the designation ‘Māgadhaka.’ The lifespan of the Māgadhaka people, monks, is short, limited, and swift; whoever lives long, lives for a hundred years or a little more. The Māgadhaka people, monks, ascend Vepulla Mountain in a moment and descend in a moment. And now, monks, I, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, have arisen in the world. And I, monks, have a foremost, auspicious pair of disciples named Sāriputta and Moggallāna. There will come a time, monks, when this very designation of the mountain will vanish, these people will pass away, and I too will attain final Nibbāna. Thus impermanent, monks, are conditioned formations; thus unstable, monks, are conditioned formations; thus without solace, monks, are conditioned formations. Insofar as this is so, monks, it is enough to become disenchanted with all conditioned formations, enough to become dispassionate towards them, enough to be liberated from them.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Pācīnavaṃso tivarānaṃ, rohitassāna vaṅkako;

Suppiyānaṃ supassoti, māgadhānañca vepullo.

“Pācīnavaṃsa for the Tivarā, Vaṅkaka for the Rohitassā; Supassa for the Suppiyā, and Vepulla for the Māgadhā.”

“Aniccā [T 2.0228] vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho”ti. dasamaṃ;

“Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned formations, of a nature to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their stilling is bliss.” The tenth.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Duggataṃ sukhitañceva, tiṃsa mātāpitena ca;

Bhātā bhaginī putto ca, dhītā vepullapabbataṃ.

The unfortunate and the fortunate, thirty, and with mother and father; brother, sister, son, and daughter, Vepulla Mountain.

Anamataggasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Unknowable Beginning is completed.

5. Kassapasaṃyuttaṃ

5. The Connected Discourses on Kassapa

1. Santuṭṭhasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Contentment

144. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0229][V 1.0174][P 2.0194][M 1.0399] viharati…pe… “santuṭṭhāyaṃ santuṭṭhoyaṃ (sī.), bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca cīvarahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjati; aladdhā ca cīvaraṃ na paritassati; laddhā ca cīvaraṃ agadhito agathito (sī.) amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati”.

144. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Monks, this Kassapa is content with whatever robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with whatever robe. He does not, for the sake of a robe, resort to improper seeking. And not having obtained a robe, he is not distressed; and having obtained a robe, he uses it unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and knowing the escape.”

“Santuṭṭhāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena piṇḍapātena, itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca piṇḍapātahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjati; aladdhā ca piṇḍapātaṃ na paritassati; laddhā ca piṇḍapātaṃ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

“Monks, this Kassapa is content with whatever almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with whatever almsfood. He does not, for the sake of almsfood, resort to improper seeking. And not having obtained almsfood, he is not distressed; and having obtained almsfood, he uses it unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and knowing the escape.”

“Santuṭṭhāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena senāsanena, itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca senāsanahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjati; aladdhā ca senāsanaṃ na paritassati; laddhā ca senāsanaṃ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

“Monks, this Kassapa is content with whatever lodging, and he speaks in praise of contentment with whatever lodging. He does not, for the sake of lodging, resort to improper seeking. And not having obtained lodging, he is not distressed; and having obtained lodging, he uses it unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and knowing the escape.”

“Santuṭṭhāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, itarītaragilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjati; aladdhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ na paritassati; laddhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ agadhito amucchito [T 2.0230] anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

Bhikkhus, this Kassapa is content with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick, and he speaks in praise of contentment with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick. He does not, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, resort to improper seeking. And not having obtained medicinal requisites for the sick, he is not anxious; and having obtained them, he uses them unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and discerning the escape.

“Tasmātiha[V 1.0175], bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca [P 2.0195] vaṇṇavādino; na ca cīvarahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjissāma; aladdhā ca cīvaraṃ na ca paritassissāma; laddhā ca cīvaraṃ agadhitā amucchitā anajjhāpannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjissāma’”. (Evaṃ sabbaṃ kātabbaṃ).

Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus in this Dispensation: ‘We will be content with whatever robes, and we will speak in praise of contentment with whatever robes. We will not, for the sake of robes, resort to improper seeking. Not having obtained a robe, we will not be anxious; and having obtained a robe, we will use it unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and discerning the escape.’ (Thus should all this be done.)

“‘Santuṭṭhā [M 1.0400] bhavissāma itarītarena piṇḍapātena…pe… santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena senāsanena…pe… santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, itarītaragilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādino; na ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjissāma aladdhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ na paritassissāma; laddhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ agadhitā amucchitā anajjhāpannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ. Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa yo vā pana (sī.), yo vā (pī.) kassapasadiso, ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

‘We will be content with whatever almsfood… and so on… we will be content with whatever lodging… and so on… we will be content with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick, and we will speak in praise of contentment with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick. We will not, for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, resort to improper seeking. Not having obtained medicinal requisites for the sick, we will not be anxious; and having obtained them, we will use them unattached, uninfatuated, and unaddicted, seeing the danger and discerning the escape.’ Thus indeed, bhikkhus, should you train. For, bhikkhus, I shall admonish you with the example of Kassapa, or of one who is like Kassapa. And when you have been admonished, you should practice accordingly. The First.

2. Anottappīsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on One Without Moral Dread

145. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca sāriputto bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye. Atha [T 2.0231] kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākassapena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “vuccati hidaṃ, āvuso kassapa, anātāpī anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya; ātāpī ca kho ottappī [P 2.0196] bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti.

145. Thus have I heard. At one time the Venerable Mahākassapa and the Venerable Sāriputta were dwelling near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Mahākassapa. After concluding their courteous and amiable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated thus, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “It is said, friend Kassapa, that one who is without ardour and without moral dread is incapable of awakening, incapable of Nibbāna, incapable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage. But one who is ardent and has moral dread is capable of awakening, capable of Nibbāna, and capable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage.”

“Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, anātāpī hoti anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya; kittāvatā ca panāvuso, ātāpī [V 1.0176] hoti ottappī bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti? “Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti [M 1.0401] na ātappaṃ karoti, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ātappaṃ karoti, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammānuppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ātappaṃ karoti, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na [T 2.0232] ātappaṃ karoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anātāpī hoti”.

“Friend, to what extent is one without ardour and without moral dread, incapable of awakening, incapable of Nibbāna, and incapable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage? And to what extent, friend, is one ardent and with moral dread, capable of awakening, capable of Nibbāna, and capable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage?” “Here, friend, a bhikkhu does not generate ardour, thinking: ‘If unarisen evil, unwholesome states were to arise in me, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not generate ardour, thinking: ‘If arisen evil, unwholesome states in me are not abandoned, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not generate ardour, thinking: ‘If unarisen wholesome states do not arise in me, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not generate ardour, thinking: ‘If arisen wholesome states in me were to cease, they would lead to my detriment.’ Thus, friend, one is without ardour.”

“Kathañcāvuso, anottappī hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ottappati, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ottappati, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammānuppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ottappati, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti na ottappati. Evaṃ [P 2.0197] kho, āvuso, anottappī hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anātāpī anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya.

“And how, friend, is one without moral dread? Here, friend, a bhikkhu does not feel moral dread, thinking: ‘If unarisen evil, unwholesome states were to arise in me, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not feel moral dread, thinking: ‘If arisen evil, unwholesome states in me are not abandoned, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not feel moral dread, thinking: ‘If unarisen wholesome states do not arise in me, they would lead to my detriment.’ He does not feel moral dread, thinking: ‘If arisen wholesome states in me were to cease, they would lead to my detriment.’ Thus, friend, one is without moral dread. In this way, friend, one who is without ardour and without moral dread is incapable of awakening, incapable of Nibbāna, and incapable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage.

“Kathañcāvuso, ātāpī hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ātappaṃ karoti, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ātappaṃ karoti, anuppannā me kusalā dhammā…pe… ātappaṃ karoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ātāpī hoti.

“And how, friend, is one ardent? Here, friend, a bhikkhu generates ardour, thinking: ‘If unarisen evil, unwholesome states were to arise in me, they would lead to my detriment.’ He generates ardour, thinking: ‘If arisen evil, unwholesome states in me are not abandoned, they would lead to my detriment.’ …and so on… He generates ardour. Thus, friend, one is ardent.

“Kathañcāvuso, ottappī hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā [T 2.0233] me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ottappati, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ottappati, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammā anuppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ottappati, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu’nti ottappati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ottappī hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ātāpī ottappī bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And how, friend, is one scrupulous? Here, friend, a bhikkhu feels moral dread, thinking: ‘If unarisen evil, unwholesome states were to arise in me, they would conduce to my harm.’ He feels moral dread, thinking: ‘If arisen evil, unwholesome states in me are not abandoned, they would conduce to my harm.’ He feels moral dread, thinking: ‘If unarisen wholesome states do not arise in me, they would conduce to my harm.’ He feels moral dread, thinking: ‘If arisen wholesome states in me were to cease, they would conduce to my harm.’ Thus, friend, one is scrupulous. In this way, friend, one who is ardent and scrupulous is capable of awakening, capable of Nibbāna, and capable of achieving the unsurpassed security from bondage.” The second.

3. Candūpamasuttaṃ

3. 3. The Discourse on the Simile of the Moon

146. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0177] viharati…pe… “candūpamā, bhikkhave, kulāni upasaṅkamatha – apakasseva [P 2.0198] kāyaṃ, apakassa cittaṃ, niccanavakā kulesu appagabbhā appagabbā (ka.). Seyyathāpi[M 1.0402], bhikkhave, puriso jarudapānaṃ vā olokeyya pabbatavisamaṃ vā nadīviduggaṃ vā – apakasseva kāyaṃ, apakassa cittaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, candūpamā kulāni upasaṅkamatha – apakasseva kāyaṃ, apakassa cittaṃ, niccanavakā kulesu appagabbhā”.

146. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, approach families like the moon—keeping the body aloof, keeping the mind aloof, always like newcomers, not presumptuous in families. Just as, bhikkhus, a man would look down into an old well, or a rugged mountain precipice, or a difficult river crossing—keeping the body aloof, keeping the mind aloof; in the same way, bhikkhus, approach families like the moon—keeping the body aloof, keeping the mind aloof, always like newcomers, not presumptuous in families.”

“Kassapo, bhikkhave, candūpamo kulāni upasaṅkamati – apakasseva kāyaṃ, apakassa cittaṃ, niccanavako kulesu appagabbho. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, kathaṃrūpo bhikkhu arahati kulāni upasaṅkamitu”nti? “Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.

“Bhikkhus, Kassapa approaches families like the moon—keeping the body aloof, keeping the mind aloof, always like a newcomer, not presumptuous in families. What do you think, bhikkhus, what kind of bhikkhu is worthy to approach families?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide, the Blessed One as their refuge. It would be good if the Blessed One himself would illuminate the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it.”

Atha kho [T 2.0234] bhagavā ākāse pāṇiṃ cālesi. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ ākāse pāṇi na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno kulāni upasaṅkamato kulesu cittaṃ na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati – ‘labhantu lābhakāmā, puññakāmā karontu puññānī’ti; yathāsakena lābhena attamano hoti sumano, evaṃ paresaṃ lābhena attamano hoti sumano; evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahati kulāni upasaṅkamituṃ.

Then the Blessed One waved his hand in the air. “Just as, bhikkhus, this hand in the air does not cling, is not caught, is not bound; in the same way, bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu who approaches families, his mind does not cling, is not caught, is not bound to those families—‘Let those who desire gain attain gain, let those who desire merit make merit.’ As he is pleased and glad-minded with his own gain, so is he pleased and glad-minded with the gain of others. Such a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is worthy to approach families.

“Kassapassa, bhikkhave, kulāni upasaṅkamato kulesu cittaṃ na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati – ‘labhantu lābhakāmā, puññakāmā karontu puññānī’ti; yathāsakena lābhena attamano hoti sumano; evaṃ paresaṃ lābhena attamano hoti sumano.

“Bhikkhus, when Kassapa approaches families, his mind does not cling, is not caught, is not bound to those families—‘Let those who desire gain attain gain, let those who desire merit make merit.’ As he is pleased and glad-minded with his own gain, so is he pleased and glad-minded with the gain of others.

“Taṃ [P 2.0199] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, kathaṃrūpassa bhikkhuno aparisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti, kathaṃrūpassa bhikkhuno parisuddhā dhammadesanā hotī”ti? “Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho[V 1.0178]. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“What do you think, bhikkhus, for what kind of bhikkhu is the teaching of the Dhamma impure, and for what kind of bhikkhu is the teaching of the Dhamma pure?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide, the Blessed One as their refuge. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One himself would illuminate the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it.” “Well then, bhikkhus, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃcitto paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘aho vata me dhammaṃ suṇeyyuṃ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṃ pasīdeyyuṃ, pasannā ca [M 1.0403] me pasannākāraṃ [T 2.0235] kareyyu’nti; evarūpassa kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno aparisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever bhikkhu teaches the Dhamma to others with such a mind: ‘Oh, that they would listen to the Dhamma from me! And having listened, that they would have confidence in the Dhamma! And that those who have become confident would show me a sign of their confidence!’—for such a bhikkhu, the teaching of the Dhamma is impure.

“Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃcitto paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti viññūhi (?). Aho, vata me dhammaṃ suṇeyyuṃ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṃ ājāneyyuṃ, ājānitvā ca pana tathattāya paṭipajjeyyu’nti. Iti dhammasudhammataṃ paṭicca paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti, kāruññaṃ paṭicca anuddayaṃ anudayaṃ (bahūsu) dvittakāraṇaṃ pana gavesitabbaṃ paṭicca anukampaṃ upādāya paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. Evarūpassa kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno parisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti.

“But, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who teaches the Dhamma to others with such a mind: ‘Well proclaimed by the Blessed One is the Dhamma, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise for themselves. Oh, that they would listen to my teaching, and having listened, understand the Dhamma, and having understood, practice accordingly!’ Thus he teaches the Dhamma to others on account of the Dhamma's excellence, on account of compassion, on account of sympathy, and based on kindness. For such a bhikkhu, the teaching of the Dhamma is pure.

“Kassapo, bhikkhave, evaṃcitto paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Aho, vata [P 2.0200] me dhammaṃ suṇeyyuṃ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṃ ājāneyyuṃ, ājānitvā ca pana tathattāya paṭipajjeyyu’nti. Iti dhammasudhammataṃ paṭicca paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti, kāruññaṃ paṭicca anuddayaṃ paṭicca anukampaṃ upādāya paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa kassapasadiso, ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabba”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, Kassapa teaches the Dhamma to others with such a mind: ‘Well proclaimed by the Blessed One is the Dhamma, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise for themselves. Oh, that they would listen to my teaching, and having listened, understand the Dhamma, and having understood, practice accordingly!’ Thus he teaches the Dhamma to others on account of the Dhamma's excellence, on account of compassion, on account of sympathy, and based on kindness. I will exhort you, bhikkhus, by means of Kassapa, or by means of one who is like Kassapa. And having been exhorted, you should practice accordingly.” The third.

4. Kulūpakasuttaṃ

4. 4. The Discourse on One Who Frequents Families

147. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, kathaṃrūpo bhikkhu [T 2.0236] arahati kulūpako hotuṃ, kathaṃrūpo bhikkhu na arahati kulūpako hotu”nti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… bhagavā etadavoca –

147. At Sāvatthī. “What do you think, bhikkhus, what kind of bhikkhu is worthy to be one who frequents families, and what kind of bhikkhu is not worthy to be one who frequents families?” “Venerable sir, for us the teachings are rooted in the Blessed One...” The Blessed One said this:

“Yo [V 1.0179] hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati – ‘dentuyeva me, mā nādaṃsu; bahukaññeva me dentu, mā thokaṃ; paṇītaññeva me dentu, mā lūkhaṃ; sīghaññeva me dentu, mā dandhaṃ; sakkaccaññeva me dentu, mā asakkacca’nti. Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṃcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Thokaṃ denti, no bahukaṃ…pe… lūkhaṃ denti, no paṇītaṃ… dandhaṃ denti, no sīghaṃ, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṃ [M 1.0404] dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Asakkaccaṃ denti, no sakkaccaṃ; tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so [P 2.0201] tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na arahati kūlūpako hotuṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a certain bhikkhu approaches families with such a mind: ‘May they give to me, may they not fail to give; may they give much to me, not little; may they give what is fine to me, not what is coarse; may they give quickly to me, not slowly; may they give respectfully to me, not disrespectfully.’ If, bhikkhus, they do not give to that bhikkhu who approaches families with such a mind, that bhikkhu is afflicted by it; for that reason, he experiences suffering and displeasure. They give little, not much... they give what is coarse, not what is fine... they give slowly, not quickly, and that bhikkhu is afflicted by it; for that reason, he experiences suffering and displeasure. They give disrespectfully, not respectfully, and that bhikkhu is afflicted by it; for that reason, he experiences suffering and displeasure. Such a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is not worthy to be one who frequents families.

“Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati – ‘taṃ kutettha labbhā parakulesu – dentuyeva me, mā nādaṃsu; bahukaññeva me dentu, mā thokaṃ; paṇītaññeva me dentu, mā lūkhaṃ; dīghaññeva me dentu, mā dandhaṃ; sakkaccaññeva me dentu, mā asakkacca’nti. Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṃcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ [T 2.0237] paṭisaṃvedayati. Thokaṃ denti, no bahukaṃ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Lūkhaṃ denti, no paṇītaṃ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Dandhaṃ denti, no sīghaṃ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Asakkaccaṃ denti, no sakkaccaṃ; tena bhikkhu na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahati kulūpako hotuṃ.

“And, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu approaches families with such a mind: ‘From where could this be obtained in other families? May they give to me, may they not fail to give; may they give much to me, not little; may they give what is fine to me, not what is coarse; may they give quickly to me, not slowly; may they give respectfully to me, not disrespectfully.’ If, bhikkhus, they do not give to that bhikkhu who approaches families with such a mind, that bhikkhu is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give little, not much; that bhikkhu is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give what is coarse, not what is fine; that bhikkhu is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give slowly, not quickly; that bhikkhu is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give disrespectfully, not respectfully; that bhikkhu is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. Such a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is worthy to be one who frequents families.

“Kassapo, bhikkhave, evaṃcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati – ‘taṃ kutettha labbhā parakulesu – dentuyeva me, mā nādaṃsu; bahukaññeva me dentu, mā thokaṃ; paṇītaññeva me dentu, mā lūkhaṃ; sīghaññeva me dentu, mā dandhaṃ; sakkaccaññeva me dentu, mā asakkacca’nti. Tassa ce, bhikkhave, kassapassa evaṃcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Thokaṃ denti, no bahukaṃ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Lūkhaṃ denti[V 1.0180], no paṇītaṃ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Dandhaṃ denti, no sīghaṃ; tena kassapo na sandīyati; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Asakkaccaṃ denti, no sakkaccaṃ; tena kassapo na sandīyati[P 2.0202]; so na tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedayati. Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa kassapasadiso. Ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabba”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, Kassapa approaches families with such a mind: ‘From where could this be obtained in other families? May they give to me, may they not fail to give; may they give much to me, not little; may they give what is fine to me, not what is coarse; may they give quickly to me, not slowly; may they give respectfully to me, not disrespectfully.’ If, bhikkhus, they do not give to Kassapa who approaches families with such a mind, Kassapa is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give little, not much; Kassapa is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give what is coarse, not what is fine; Kassapa is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give slowly, not quickly; Kassapa is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. They give disrespectfully, not respectfully; Kassapa is not afflicted by it; he does not, for that reason, experience suffering and displeasure. Bhikkhus, I shall instruct you by means of Kassapa, or by one who is like Kassapa. And you, having been instructed, should practice for the purpose of being in accordance with that teaching.” The Fourth.

5. Jiṇṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Aged

148. Evaṃ [T 2.0238][M 1.0405] me sutaṃ…pe… rājagahe veḷuvane. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “jiṇṇosi dāni tvaṃ, kassapa, garukāni ca te imāni sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanāni. Tasmātiha tvaṃ, kassapa, gahapatāni gahapatikāni (sī.) ceva cīvarāni dhārehi, nimantanāni ca bhuñjāhi, mama ca santike viharāhī”ti.

148. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa: 'Kassapa, you are now old, and these worn-out, hempen rag-robes of yours are heavy. Therefore, Kassapa, you should wear robes offered by householders, eat invited alms-food, and dwell near me.'

“Ahaṃ kho, bhante, dīgharattaṃ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, paṃsukūliko ceva paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, tecīvariko ceva tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, appiccho ceva appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, santuṭṭho ceva santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, pavivitto ceva pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, asaṃsaṭṭho ceva asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa vīriyārabbhassa (ka.) ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

“Venerable sir, for a long time I have been a forest-dweller and one who speaks in praise of forest-dwelling; an alms-food-eater and one who speaks in praise of eating alms-food; a rag-robe-wearer and one who speaks in praise of wearing rag-robes; a three-robe-wearer and one who speaks in praise of wearing three robes; one of few wishes and one who speaks in praise of having few wishes; content and one who speaks in praise of contentment; secluded and one who speaks in praise of seclusion; unassociated with others and one who speaks in praise of non-association; one with aroused energy and one who speaks in praise of arousing energy.”

“Kiṃ kaṃ (ka.) pana tvaṃ, kassapa, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno dīgharattaṃ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva…pe… paṃsukūliko ceva… tecīvariko ceva… appiccho ceva… santuṭṭho ceva… pavivitto ceva… asaṃsaṭṭho ceva… āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti?

“But, Kassapa, seeing what benefit have you for a long time been a forest-dweller and one who speaks in praise of forest-dwelling; an alms-food-eater… one with aroused energy and one who speaks in praise of arousing energy?”

“Dve [T 2.0239][V 1.0181] khvāhaṃ, bhante, atthavase sampassamāno dīgharattaṃ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko [P 2.0203] ceva…pe… paṃsukūliko ceva… tecīvariko ceva… appiccho ceva… santuṭṭho ceva… pavivitto ceva… asaṃsaṭṭho ceva… āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī. Attano ca diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ sampassamāno, pacchimañca janataṃ anukampamāno – ‘appeva nāma pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjeyyuṃ’ āpajjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ.). ‘Ye kira te ahesuṃ buddhānubuddhasāvakā te dīgharattaṃ āraññikā ceva ahesuṃ āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino…pe… piṇḍapātikā ceva ahesuṃ [M 1.0406] …pe… paṃsukūlikā ceva ahesuṃ… tecīvarikā ceva ahesuṃ… appicchā ceva ahesuṃ… santuṭṭhā ceva ahesuṃ… pavivittā ceva ahesuṃ… asaṃsaṭṭhā ceva ahesuṃ… āraddhavīriyā ceva ahesuṃ vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādino’ti. Te tathattāya paṭipajjissanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.

Venerable sir, seeing two benefits, I have for a long time been a forest-dweller and one who speaks in praise of forest-dwelling... and so on... one with aroused energy and one who speaks in praise of arousing energy. I see my own pleasant abiding in this very life, and I am compassionate towards future generations, thinking: 'Perhaps future generations will follow this seen example. They may think: "Indeed, those disciples who were enlightened in succession to the Buddha were, for a long time, forest-dwellers and spoke in praise of forest-dwelling... and so on... they had aroused energy and spoke in praise of arousing energy."' They will practice to attain that state, and that will be for their welfare and happiness for a long time.

“Ime khvāhaṃ, bhante, dve atthavase sampassamāno dīgharattaṃ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva…pe… paṃsukūliko ceva… tecīvariko ceva… appiccho ceva… santuṭṭho ceva… pavivitto ceva… asaṃsaṭṭho ceva… āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

Venerable sir, it is from seeing these two benefits that I have for a long time been a forest-dweller and one who speaks in praise of forest-dwelling; an alms-food-eater... and so on... a rag-robe-wearer... a three-robe-wearer... one of few wishes... content... secluded... unassociated... one with aroused energy and one who speaks in praise of arousing energy.

“Sādhu sādhu, kassapa. Bahujanahitāya kira tvaṃ, kassapa, paṭipanno [T 2.0240] bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Tasmātiha tvaṃ, kassapa, sāṇāni ceva paṃsukūlāni dhārehi nibbasanāni, piṇḍāya ca carāhi, araññe ca viharāhī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Good, good, Kassapa. Indeed, Kassapa, you have undertaken this practice for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Therefore, Kassapa, continue to wear your worn-out, hempen rag-robes, wander for alms-food, and dwell in the forest.”

6. Ovādasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Admonition

149. Rājagahe veḷuvane. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū; karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ. Ahaṃ vā, kassapa[P 2.0204], bhikkhū ovadeyyaṃ tvaṃ vā; ahaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ kareyyaṃ tvaṃ vā”ti.

149. At Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa who was sitting to one side: “Kassapa, admonish the bhikkhus. Kassapa, give a Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus. Kassapa, either I should admonish the bhikkhus, or you should. Either I should give a Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus, or you should.”

“Dubbacā [V 1.0182] kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā, appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṃ. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, addasaṃ bhaṇḍañca bhaṇḍuñca (sī.) nāma bhikkhuṃ ānandassa saddhivihāriṃ abhijikañca ābhiñjikañca (sī. ka.), ābhijjikañca (syā. kaṃ.) nāma bhikkhuṃ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṃ aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadante – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’”ti.

“Venerable sir, the bhikkhus nowadays are difficult to speak to. They are endowed with qualities that make them difficult to speak to; they are intolerant and do not accept instruction respectfully. Here, Venerable sir, I saw the bhikkhu named Bhaṇḍa, the co-resident of the Venerable Ānanda, and the bhikkhu named Abhijika, the co-resident of the Venerable Anuruddha, outdoing each other based on their learning, saying: ‘Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?’”

Atha [M 1.0407] kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena bhaṇḍañca bhikkhuṃ ānandassa saddhivihāriṃ abhijikañca bhikkhuṃ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū [T 2.0241] etadavoca – “satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain bhikkhu: “Come, bhikkhu. In my name, summon the bhikkhu Bhaṇḍa, the co-resident of Ānanda, and the bhikkhu Abhijika, the co-resident of Anuruddha, saying: ‘The Teacher summons the venerable ones.’” “Yes, Venerable sir,” that bhikkhu replied to the Blessed One. Having assented, he approached those bhikkhus and said to them: “The Teacher summons the venerable ones.”

“Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadatha – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Kiṃ nu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha – ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadatha – ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’”ti? “No [P 2.0205] hetaṃ, bhante”. “No ce kira me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha, atha kiṃ carahi tumhe, moghapurisā, kiṃ jānantā kiṃ passantā evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadatha – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’”ti.

“Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to that bhikkhu. Having assented, they approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to those bhikkhus who were sitting to one side: “Bhikkhus, is it true, as is said, that you outdo each other based on learning, saying: ‘Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?’” “Yes, Venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, do you understand the Dhamma taught by me to be like this: ‘Come, bhikkhus, outdo each other based on learning, saying: “Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?”’” “Certainly not, Venerable sir.” “If, bhikkhus, you do not understand the Dhamma taught by me to be like this, then, you foolish men, knowing what, seeing what, have you gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, that you outdo each other based on learning, saying: ‘Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?’”

Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “accayo no, bhante, accagamā, yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale yathā bāle yathā mūḷhe yathā akusale (pī.), yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ (?), ye mayaṃ evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadimha – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati[V 1.0183], ko sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’ti. Tesaṃ [T 2.0242] no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti.

Then those bhikkhus, having fallen with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, a transgression has overcome us, foolish, deluded, and unskillful as we are, in that we, having gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, outdid each other based on learning, saying: ‘Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?’ Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept this transgression of ours as a transgression for the sake of restraint in the future.”

“Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, accayo accagamā yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṃ sutena accāvadittha – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṃ bhāsissati, ko [M 1.0408] sundarataraṃ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṃ bhāsissatī’ti. Yato ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarotha, taṃ vo mayaṃ mayaṃ accayaṃ (sī.) paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhi hesā, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti āyatiñca saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Indeed, bhikkhus, a transgression has overcome you, foolish, deluded, and unskillful as you were, in that you, having gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, outdid each other based on learning, saying: ‘Come, bhikkhu! Who will speak more? Who will speak more beautifully? Who will speak longer?’ But since you, bhikkhus, having seen the transgression as a transgression, make amends in accordance with the Dhamma, we accept it from you. For it is growth in the Noble One’s Discipline when one, having seen a transgression as a transgression, makes amends in accordance with the Dhamma and undertakes restraint for the future.”

7. Dutiyaovādasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on Exhortation

150. Rājagahe viharati veḷuvane sāvatthi, tatra-etadavoca (sī.). Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū; karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ. Ahaṃ vā, kassapa[P 2.0206], bhikkhū ovadeyyaṃ tvaṃ vā; ahaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ kareyyaṃ tvaṃ vā”ti.

150. He was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa approached the Blessed One… and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa as he was sitting to one side: “Exhort the bhikkhus, Kassapa; give a Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus, Kassapa. Either I, Kassapa, should exhort the bhikkhus, or you should; either I should give a Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus, or you should.”

“Dubbacā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā akkhamā appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṃ. Yassa kassaci, bhante, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī hiri (sabbattha) natthi kusalesu dhammesu, ottappaṃ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, vīriyaṃ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā [T 2.0243] ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati āgacchanti (sī.), hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.

“Venerable Sir, the bhikkhus nowadays are difficult to admonish; they are endowed with qualities that make them difficult to admonish. They are impatient and do not accept instruction respectfully. For anyone, Venerable Sir, who has no faith in wholesome qualities, no moral shame in wholesome qualities, no moral dread in wholesome qualities, no energy in wholesome qualities, and no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.

“Seyyathāpi, bhante, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena, hāyati maṇḍalena, hāyati ābhāya, hāyati ārohapariṇāhena. Evameva kho, bhante, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi [V 1.0184]… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi… kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.

“Just as, Venerable Sir, during the waning fortnight, for the moon, whatever night or day comes, it only declines in color, declines in its disc, declines in radiance, declines in its magnitude and extent; just so, Venerable Sir, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities… no moral shame… no moral dread… no energy… no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.

“‘Assaddho purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘ahiriko purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘anottappī purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘kusīto purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘duppañño purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘kodhano [M 1.0409] purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘upanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ; ‘na santi bhikkhū ovādakā’ti, bhante, parihānametaṃ.

“‘A person who is without faith,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is shameless,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is without moral dread,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is lazy,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is of little wisdom,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is prone to anger,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘A person who is rancorous,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline. ‘There are no bhikkhus who give exhortation,’ Venerable Sir, this is a decline.

“Yassa kassaci, bhante, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi kusalesu dhammesu, ottappaṃ atthi kusalesu dhammesu, vīriyaṃ atthi kusalesu dhammesu, paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.

“For anyone, Venerable Sir, who has faith in wholesome qualities, has moral shame in wholesome qualities, has moral dread in wholesome qualities, has energy in wholesome qualities, and has wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.

“Seyyathāpi, bhante, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena, vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena[P 2.0207], vaḍḍhati ābhāya, vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena. Evameva [T 2.0244] kho, bhante, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu… hirī atthi…pe… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.

“Just as, Venerable Sir, during the waxing fortnight, for the moon, whatever night or day comes, it only grows in color, grows in its disc, grows in radiance, grows in its magnitude and extent; just so, Venerable Sir, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities… has moral shame… has moral dread… has energy… has wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.

“‘Saddho purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘hirimā purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘ottappī purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘āraddhavīriyo purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘paññavā purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘akkodhano purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘anupanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, aparihānametaṃ; ‘santi bhikkhū ovādakā’ti, bhante, aparihānameta”nti.

“‘A person who has faith,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person who has moral shame,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person who has moral dread,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person of aroused energy,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person who has wisdom,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person not prone to anger,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘A person who is not rancorous,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline. ‘There are bhikkhus who give exhortation,’ Venerable Sir, this is non-decline.”

“Sādhu sādhu, kassapa. Yassa kassaci, kassapa, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… hirī [V 1.0185] natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.

“Good, good, Kassapa. For anyone, Kassapa, who has no faith in wholesome qualities… no moral shame… no moral dread… no energy… and no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.

“Seyyathāpi, kassapa, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena…pe… hāyati ārohapariṇāhena. Evameva kho, kassapa, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi. ‘Assaddho [T 2.0245] purisapuggalo’ti, kassapa, parihānametaṃ[M 1.0410]; ahiriko…pe… anottappī… kusīto… duppañño… kodhano… ‘upanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, kassapa, parihānametaṃ; ‘na santi bhikkhū ovādakā’ti, kassapa, parihānametaṃ.

“Just as, Kassapa, during the waning fortnight, for the moon, whatever night or day comes, it only declines in color… declines in its magnitude and extent; just so, Kassapa, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities… no moral shame… no moral dread… no energy… no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth. ‘A person who is without faith,’ Kassapa, this is a decline; a person who is shameless… a person who is without moral dread… a person who is lazy… a person who is of little wisdom… a person who is prone to anger… ‘a person who is rancorous,’ Kassapa, this is a decline; ‘there are no bhikkhus who give exhortation,’ Kassapa, this is a decline.

“Yassa kassaci, kassapa, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.

“For anyone, Kassapa, who has faith in wholesome qualities… has moral shame… has moral dread… has energy… has wisdom in wholesome qualities, for him, whatever night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.”

“Seyyathāpi, kassapa, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso [P 2.0208] vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena, vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena, vaḍḍhati ābhāya, vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena. Evameva kho, kassapa, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.

“Just as, Kassapa, during the waxing fortnight, as each night or day comes, the moon grows in color, grows in its disk, grows in radiance, and grows in height and circumference. Even so, Kassapa, for anyone whatsoever who has faith in wholesome states, has moral shame… has moral dread… has energy… has wisdom in wholesome states, for them, as each night or day comes, only growth in wholesome states is to be expected, not decline.”

“‘Saddho purisapuggalo’ti, kassapa, aparihānametaṃ; hirimā…pe… ottappī… āraddhavīriyo… paññavā… akkodhano… ‘anupanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, kassapa, aparihānametaṃ; ‘santi bhikkhū ovādakā’ti, kassapa, aparihānameta”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“‘A faithful individual,’ Kassapa, this is non-decline; ‘an individual with moral shame’… ‘an individual with moral dread’… ‘an energetic individual’… ‘a wise individual’… ‘a non-angry individual’… ‘a non-resentful individual,’ Kassapa, this is non-decline; ‘there are monks who give admonition,’ Kassapa, this is non-decline.” Seventh.

8. Tatiyaovādasuttaṃ

8. The Third Discourse on Admonition

151. Rājagahe kalandakanivāpe sāvatthi, ārāme (sī.). Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[V 1.0186]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0246] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū; karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ. Ahaṃ vā, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṃ ovadeyyaṃ tvaṃ vā; ahaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ kareyyaṃ tvaṃ vā”ti.

151. At Rājagaha, in the Kalandakanivāpa. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the Venerable Mahākassapa sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: “Admonish the monks, Kassapa; give the monks a talk on the Dhamma. Either I, Kassapa, should admonish the monks, or you; either I should give the monks a talk on the Dhamma, or you.”

“Dubbacā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā, appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsanī”nti. “Tathā hi pana, kassapa, pubbe therā bhikkhū āraññikā ceva ahesuṃ āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, piṇḍapātikā ceva ahesuṃ piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino[M 1.0411], paṃsukūlikā ceva ahesuṃ paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, tecīvarikā ceva ahesuṃ tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, appicchā ceva ahesuṃ appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādino, santuṭṭhā ceva ahesuṃ santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādino, pavivittā ceva ahesuṃ pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādino, asaṃsaṭṭhā ceva ahesuṃ [P 2.0209] asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādino, āraddhavīriyā ceva ahesuṃ vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādino.

“Venerable sir, the monks nowadays are difficult to speak to; they are endowed with qualities that make them difficult to speak to, are impatient, and do not accept instruction respectfully.” “Indeed, Kassapa, in the past the elder monks were forest-dwellers and spoke in praise of being a forest-dweller; they were alms-food eaters and spoke in praise of being an alms-food eater; they were rag-robe wearers and spoke in praise of being a rag-robe wearer; they were three-robe wearers and spoke in praise of being a three-robe wearer; they had few desires and spoke in praise of having few desires; they were content and spoke in praise of contentment; they were secluded and spoke in praise of seclusion; they were unentangled and spoke in praise of non-entanglement; they had aroused energy and spoke in praise of the undertaking of energy.”

“Tatra yo hoti bhikkhu āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, paṃsukūliko ceva paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, tecīvariko ceva tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, appiccho ceva appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, santuṭṭho ceva santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, pavivitto ceva pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, asaṃsaṭṭho [T 2.0247] ceva asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, taṃ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṃ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṃ bhikkhu, sikkhākāmo vatāyaṃ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṃ āsanaṃ nisīdāhī’”ti.

“Among them, whichever monk was a forest-dweller and a speaker in praise of being a forest-dweller, an alms-food eater and a speaker in praise of being an alms-food eater, a rag-robe wearer and a speaker in praise of being a rag-robe wearer, a three-robe wearer and a speaker in praise of being a three-robe wearer, one of few desires and a speaker in praise of having few desires, content and a speaker in praise of contentment, secluded and a speaker in praise of seclusion, unentangled and a speaker in praise of non-entanglement, one with aroused energy and a speaker in praise of the undertaking of energy—the elder monks would invite him with a seat, saying: ‘Come, monk. What is this monk’s name? This monk is indeed good! This monk is indeed desirous of the training! Come, monk, here is a seat. Please sit down.’”

“Tatra, kassapa, navānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘yo kira so hoti bhikkhu āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva…pe… paṃsukūliko ceva… tecīvariko ceva… appiccho ceva… santuṭṭho ceva… pavivitto ceva… asaṃsaṭṭho ceva… āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, taṃ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti – ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṃ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṃ bhikkhu, sikkhākāmo vatāyaṃ [V 1.0187] bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṃ āsanaṃ nisīdāhī’ti. Te tathattāya paṭipajjanti; tesaṃ taṃ hoti dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.

“Then, Kassapa, it would occur to the junior monks: ‘Whichever monk, it seems, is a forest-dweller and a speaker in praise of being a forest-dweller, an alms-food eater… a rag-robe wearer… a three-robe wearer… one of few desires… content… secluded… unentangled… one with aroused energy and a speaker in praise of the undertaking of energy—the elder monks invite him with a seat, saying: “Come, monk. What is this monk’s name? This monk is indeed good! This monk is indeed desirous of the training! Come, monk, here is a seat. Please sit down.”’ They would then practice for that same attainment. For them, that was for their welfare and happiness for a long time.”

“Etarahi pana, kassapa, therā bhikkhū na ceva āraññikā na ca āraññikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva piṇḍapātikā na ca piṇḍapātikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva paṃsukūlikā na ca paṃsukūlikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva tecīvarikā na ca tecīvarikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva appicchā na ca appicchatāya vaṇṇavādino, na ceva santuṭṭhā na ca santuṭṭhiyā vaṇṇavādino, na ceva pavivittā na ca pavivekassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva asaṃsaṭṭhā na ca asaṃsaggassa vaṇṇavādino[P 2.0210], na ceva āraddhavīriyā na [T 2.0248] ca vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādino.

“But nowadays, Kassapa, the elder monks are neither forest-dwellers nor speakers in praise of being a forest-dweller; neither alms-food eaters nor speakers in praise of being an alms-food eater; neither rag-robe wearers nor speakers in praise of being a rag-robe wearer; neither three-robe wearers nor speakers in praise of being a three-robe wearer; neither of few desires nor speakers in praise of having few desires; neither content nor speakers in praise of contentment; neither secluded nor speakers in praise of seclusion; neither unentangled nor speakers in praise of non-entanglement; neither with aroused energy nor speakers in praise of the undertaking of energy.”

“Tatra [M 1.0412] yo hoti bhikkhu ñāto yasassī lābhī cīvara-piṇḍapāta-senāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ taṃ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti – ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṃ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṃ bhikkhu, sabrahmacārikāmo vatāyaṃ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṃ āsanaṃ nisīdāhī’”ti.

“Now, whichever monk is well-known, of great repute, and a receiver of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, the elder monks invite him with a seat, saying: ‘Come, monk. What is this monk’s name? This monk is indeed good! This monk is indeed liked by his companions in the holy life! Come, monk, here is a seat. Please sit down.’”

“Tatra, kassapa, navānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘yo kira so hoti bhikkhu ñāto yasassī lābhī cīvara-piṇḍapāta-senāsana-gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ taṃ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti – ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṃ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṃ bhikkhu, sabrahmacārikāmo vatāyaṃ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṃ āsanaṃ nisīdāhī’ti. Te tathattāya paṭipajjanti. Tesaṃ taṃ hoti dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Yañhi taṃ, kassapa, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘upaddutā brahmacārī brahmacārūpaddavena abhipatthanā abhibhavanā (sī.) brahmacārī brahmacāriabhipatthanenā’ti brahmacāriabhibhavanenāti (sī.), etarahi taṃ, kassapa, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘upaddutā brahmacārī brahmacārūpaddavena abhipatthanā brahmacārī brahmacāriabhipatthanenā’”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“In that regard, Kassapa, this thought occurs to the junior monks: ‘The monk who is well-known, famous, and a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites—the elder monks invite him with a seat, saying: “Come, monk! What is this monk’s name? Indeed, this monk is excellent! Indeed, this monk is beloved by his companions in the holy life! Come, monk, this is a seat; please sit.”’ They practice in order to attain that state. For them, that leads to their long-term harm and suffering. Kassapa, if one were to speak rightly, one would say this: ‘Practitioners of the holy life are afflicted by the calamity of the holy life; practitioners of the holy life are full of longing due to the longing that arises for practitioners of the holy life.’ Now, Kassapa, if one were to speak rightly, one would say this: ‘Practitioners of the holy life are afflicted by the calamity of the holy life; practitioners of the holy life are full of longing due to the longing that arises for practitioners of the holy life.’” Eighth.

9. Jhānābhiññasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Jhāna and the Supernormal Knowledges

152. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi [V 1.0188] vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi[P 2.0211], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati”.

152. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Monks, for as long as I wish, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion.”

“Ahaṃ[T 2.0249], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, I enter and dwell in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without initial application and without sustained application, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, with the stilling of initial and sustained application... enters and dwells in the second jhāna.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati pītiyā [M 1.0413] ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, with the fading away of rapture, I dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and I experience happiness with the body. I enter and dwell in the third jhāna, regarding which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one dwells in happiness.’ Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, with the fading away of rapture, dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and he experiences happiness with the body. He enters and dwells in the third jhāna, regarding which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one dwells in happiness.’”

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, I enter and dwell in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, with the abandoning of pleasure... enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi[T 2.0250], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘Space is infinite,’ I enter and dwell in the base of infinite space. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, by completely transcending perceptions of form... enters and dwells in the base of infinite space.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ [V 1.0189] viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi[P 2.0212], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, aware that ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ I enter and dwell in the base of infinite consciousness. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, aware that ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ enters and dwells in the base of infinite consciousness.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘There is nothing,’ I enter and dwell in the base of nothingness. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes... enters and dwells in the base of nothingness.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, I enter and dwell in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes... enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave…pe… saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, by completely transcending the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, I enter and dwell in the cessation of perception and feeling. Kassapa too, monks... enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling.

“Ahaṃ[M 1.0414], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhomi [T 2.0251] – ekopi hutvā bahudhā homi, bahudhāpi hutvā eko homi; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ, tirokuṭṭaṃ, tiropākāraṃ, tiropabbataṃ, asajjamāno gacchāmi, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karomi, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchāmi, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamāmi, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasāmi parimajjāmi; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattemi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti.

“Monks, for as long as I wish, I experience the many kinds of psychic power: having been one, I become many; having been many, I become one; I appear and disappear; I go unhindered through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; I dive in and out of the earth as if in water; I walk on unbroken water as if on earth; I travel cross-legged in the sky like a winged bird; I touch and stroke with my hand these moon and sun, so powerful and mighty; I wield mastery with my body even as far as the Brahmā world. Kassapa too, monks, for as long as he wishes, experiences the many kinds of psychic power... he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world.”

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāmi, dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati dibbāya sotadhātuyā…pe… dūre santike ca.

Bhikkhus, whenever I wish, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, I hear both kinds of sounds, divine and human, those far and near. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, whenever he wishes, with the divine ear element… hears sounds both far and near.

“Ahaṃ[V 1.0190][P 2.0213], bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāmi, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāmi, sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ…pe… vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ… samohaṃ vā cittaṃ… vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ… saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ… vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ… mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ… amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ… sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ… anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ… samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ… asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ… vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ… avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajānāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati parasattānaṃ [T 2.0252] parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāti…pe… avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajānāti.

Bhikkhus, whenever I wish, I understand the minds of other beings and individuals by encompassing them with my own mind: I understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust; a mind without lust as a mind without lust; a mind with hate… a mind without hate… a mind with delusion… a mind without delusion… a constricted mind… a scattered mind… a sublime mind… an unsublime mind… a surpassable mind… an unsurpassed mind… a concentrated mind… an unconcentrated mind… a liberated mind… an unliberated mind as an unliberated mind. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, whenever he wishes, understands the minds of other beings and individuals by encompassing them with his own mind: he understands a mind with lust as a mind with lust… an unliberated mind as an unliberated mind.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi, anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto[M 1.0415], so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.

Bhikkhus, whenever I wish, I recollect my manifold past lives—that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of world-contraction, many eons of world-expansion, many eons of world-contraction and expansion: ‘There I was, so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such food, such experience of pleasure and pain, such a life-span. Passing away from there, I arose elsewhere. There too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such food, such experience of pleasure and pain, such a life-span. Passing away from there, I arose here.’ Thus with its aspects and details, I recollect my manifold past lives. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, whenever he wishes, recollects his manifold past lives—that is, one birth… Thus with its aspects and details, he recollects his manifold past lives.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne [P 2.0214] upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte [T 2.0253] pajānāmi – ‘ime vata, bhonto, sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā, ime vā pana, bhonto, sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena [V 1.0191] samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.

Bhikkhus, whenever I wish, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, I see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and bad destinations—and I understand beings passing on according to their kamma: ‘Indeed, these beings who engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, who reviled the noble ones, held wrong views, and undertook actions based on wrong views—after the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in perdition, in hell. But these other beings, who engaged in good conduct of body, speech, and mind, who did not revile the noble ones, held right views, and undertook actions based on right views—after the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.’ Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, I see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and bad destinations—and I understand beings passing on according to their kamma. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, whenever he wishes, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, sees beings passing away… and understands beings passing on according to their kamma.

“Ahaṃ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Navamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, I dwell having realized for myself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it.” Ninth.

10. Upassayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse at the Nuns’ Quarters

153. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā [T 2.0254] ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā [P 2.0215] pattacīvaramādāya yenāyasmā [M 1.0416] mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, bahukicco tvaṃ bahukaraṇīyo”ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, bahukicco tvaṃ bahukaraṇīyo”ti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti.

153. Thus have I heard. At one time the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached, he said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Come, venerable Kassapa, let us approach a certain nuns’ quarters.” “Go, friend Ānanda. You have many duties, many things to do.” A second time, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Come, venerable Kassapa, let us approach a certain nuns’ quarters.” “Go, friend Ānanda. You have many duties, many things to do.” A third time, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Come, venerable Kassapa, let us approach a certain nuns’ quarters.”

Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhuniyo yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā [V 1.0192] āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmā mahākassapo dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo tā bhikkhuniyo dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then, in the morning, the Venerable Mahākassapa, having dressed, took his bowl and robe, and with the Venerable Ānanda as his attendant monk, approached a certain nuns' residence. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then many nuns approached the Venerable Mahākassapa, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Venerable Mahākassapa instructed, established, roused, and gladdened those nuns, who were seated to one side, with a talk on the Dhamma. Then, having instructed, established, roused, and gladdened those nuns with a talk on the Dhamma, the Venerable Mahākassapa rose from his seat and departed.

Atha [T 2.0255] kho thullatissā bhikkhunī anattamanā anattamanavācaṃ nicchāresi – “kiṃ pana ayyo mahākassapo, ayyassa ānandassa vedehamunino sammukhā dhammaṃ bhāsitabbaṃ maññati? Seyyathāpi nāma sūcivāṇijako sūcikārassa [P 2.0216] santike sūciṃ vikketabbaṃ maññeyya; evameva ayyo mahākassapo ayyassa ānandassa vedehamunino sammukhā dhammaṃ bhāsitabbaṃ maññatī”ti.

Then the bhikkhunī Thullatissā, displeased, uttered words of displeasure: “Why does the noble Mahākassapa think the Dhamma should be spoken in the presence of the noble Ānanda, the wise sage? It is just as if a needle merchant were to think of selling a needle in the presence of a needle maker. In the very same way, the noble Mahākassapa thinks the Dhamma should be spoken in the presence of the noble Ānanda, the wise sage.”

Assosi kho āyasmā mahākassapo thullatissāya bhikkhuniyā imaṃ vācaṃ bhāsamānāya. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, āvuso ānanda, ahaṃ sūcivāṇijako, tvaṃ sūcikāro; udāhu ahaṃ sūcikāro, tvaṃ sūcivāṇijako”ti? “Khama[M 1.0417], bhante kassapa, bālo mātugāmo”ti. “Āgamehi tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, mā te saṅgho uttari upaparikkhi”.

The Venerable Mahākassapa heard the bhikkhunī Thullatissā speaking these words. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “What is this, friend Ānanda? Am I the needle merchant and you the needle maker, or am I the needle maker and you the needle merchant?” “Forbear, Venerable Kassapa. A woman is foolish.” “Wait, friend Ānanda, lest the Saṅgha investigate you further.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, āvuso ānanda, api nu tvaṃ bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto – ‘ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ānandopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, friend Ānanda? Were you compared by the Blessed One in the presence of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus thus: ‘Bhikkhus, for as long as I wish, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. Ānanda too, bhikkhus, for as long as he wishes, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto – ‘ahaṃ, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi [T 2.0256] vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi.
