Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvadeva ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī’ti…pe…[V 1.0193]. (Navannaṃ anupubbavihārasamāpattīnaṃ pañcannañca abhiññānaṃ evaṃ vitthāro veditabbo.)

“But I, friend, was compared by the Blessed One in the presence of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus thus: ‘Bhikkhus, for as long as I wish, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, for as long as he wishes, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states… enters and dwells in the first jhāna.’ (The elaboration is to be understood in the same way for the nine successive attainments and the five direct knowledges.)”

“Taṃ [V 1.0196][P 2.0217] kiṃ maññasi, āvuso ānanda, api nu tvaṃ bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto – ‘ahaṃ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi. Ānandopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, friend Ānanda? Were you compared by the Blessed One in the presence of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus thus: ‘Bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for myself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, I enter and dwell therein. Ānanda too, bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, enters and dwells therein’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto – ‘ahaṃ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi. Kassapopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’”ti.

“But I, friend, was compared by the Blessed One in the presence of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus thus: ‘Bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for myself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, I enter and dwell therein. Kassapa too, bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, enters and dwells therein.’”

“Sattaratanaṃ vā, āvuso, nāgaṃ aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanaṃ vā tālapattikāya chādetabbaṃ maññeyya, yo me cha abhiññā chādetabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

“Friend, one who would think my six direct knowledges could be concealed might as well think a seven-cubit or seven-and-a-half-cubit elephant could be concealed with a palm leaf.”

Cavittha ca pana thullatissā bhikkhunī brahmacariyamhāti. Dasamaṃ.

And the bhikkhunī Thullatissā fell away from the holy life. The tenth.

11. Cīvarasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Robe

154. Ekaṃ [T 2.0257][M 1.0418] samayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando dakkhiṇagirismiṃ cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ.

154. At one time the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding place. Now at that time the Venerable Ānanda was wandering in the Southern Hills with a large company of bhikkhus.

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa tiṃsamattā saddhivihārino bhikkhū sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattā bhavanti yebhuyyena kumārabhūtā. Atha [P 2.0218] kho āyasmā ānando dakkhiṇagirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ cārikaṃ caritvā yena rājagahaṃ veḷuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpo yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo [V 1.0197] etadavoca – “kati nu kho, āvuso ānanda, atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṃ paññatta”nti?

At that time, about thirty bhikkhus who were the Venerable Ānanda’s co-residents had rejected the training and returned to the lower life; they were mostly young men. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having wandered in the Southern Hills for as long as he wished, went to Rājagaha, to the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place, where the Venerable Mahākassapa was, and approached him. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākassapa and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Venerable Mahākassapa said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “For how many reasons, friend Ānanda, was the meal in a group of three in families prescribed by the Blessed One?”

“Tayo kho, bhante kassapa, atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṃ paññattaṃ – dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, mā pāpicchā pakkhaṃ nissāya saṅghaṃ bhindeyyuṃ vinayapiṭake cūḷavagge saṃghabhedakakkhandhake vajirabuddhiyaṃ aññathā sambandho dassito, kulānuddayatāya ca. Ime kho, bhante kassapa, tayo atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṃ paññatta”nti.

“Venerable Kassapa, the meal in a group of three in families was prescribed by the Blessed One on account of three reasons: for the restraint of immoral persons, for the comfortable living of virtuous bhikkhus, so that those with evil desires might not split the Saṅgha by relying on a faction, and out of compassion for families. These, Venerable Kassapa, are the three reasons on account of which the meal in a group of three in families was prescribed by the Blessed One.”

“Atha kiñcarahi tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, imehi navehi bhikkhūhi indriyesu aguttadvārehi bhojane amattaññūhi jāgariyaṃ ananuyuttehi saddhiṃ cārikaṃ carasi? Sassaghātaṃ maññe carasi, kulūpaghātaṃ maññe carasi. Olujjati ullujjati (sī. aṭṭhakathāsu ca) kho te, āvuso ānanda, parisā; palujjanti kho [T 2.0258] te, āvuso, navappāyā. Na vāyaṃ kumārako mattamaññāsī”ti.

“Then for what reason, friend Ānanda, do you wander on tour with these new bhikkhus who have their sense-doors unguarded, do not know the measure in eating, and are not devoted to wakefulness? I think you go about destroying the crops; I think you go about bringing ruin to families. Your assembly is breaking apart, friend Ānanda; your new members are falling away. This boy does not know the measure.”

“Api me, bhante kassapa, sirasmiṃ palitāni jātāni. Atha ca pana mayaṃ ajjāpi āyasmato mahākassapassa kumārakavādā na muccāmā”ti. “Tathā [P 2.0219] hi pana tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, imehi navehi bhikkhūhi indriyesu aguttadvārehi bhojane amattaññūhi jāgariyaṃ ananuyuttehi saddhiṃ cārikaṃ carasi, sassaghātaṃ maññe carasi, kulūpaghātaṃ maññe carasi. Olujjati [M 1.0419] kho te, āvuso ānanda, parisā; palujjanti kho te, āvuso, navappāyā. palujjati kho te āvuso ānanda parisā (ka. sī.) Na vāyaṃ kumārako mattamaññāsī”ti.

“Venerable Kassapa, gray hairs have appeared on my head, yet even now we are not free from the Venerable Mahākassapa’s calling us ‘youngster’.” “That is precisely why, friend Ānanda, you wander on tour with these new bhikkhus who have their sense-doors unguarded, do not know the measure in eating, and are not devoted to wakefulness. I think you go about destroying the crops; I think you go about bringing ruin to families. Your assembly is breaking apart, friend Ānanda; your new members are falling away. This boy does not know the measure.”

Assosi kho thullanandā bhikkhunī – “ayyena kira mahākassapena ayyo ānando vedehamuni kumārakavādena apasādito”ti.

The bhikkhunī Thullanandā heard: “It is said that the noble Mahākassapa has disparaged the noble Ānanda, the sage of the Videhas, by calling him a youngster.”

Atha kho thullanandā bhikkhunī anattamanā anattamanavācaṃ nicchāresi – “kiṃ pana ayyo mahākassapo aññatitthiyapubbo samāno ayyaṃ ānandaṃ vedehamuniṃ kumārakavādena apasādetabbaṃ maññatī”ti! Assosi kho āyasmā mahākassapo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā imaṃ vācaṃ bhāsamānāya.

Then the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, being displeased, uttered a displeased word: “Why then does the noble Mahākassapa, who was formerly a follower of another doctrine, think that the noble Ānanda, the sage of the Videhas, should be disparaged by being called a youngster?” The Venerable Mahākassapa heard this word being spoken by the bhikkhunī Thullanandā.

Atha [V 1.0198] kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “tagghāvuso ānanda, thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā sahasā appaṭisaṅkhā vācā bhāsitā. Yatvāhaṃ, āvuso, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, nābhijānāmi aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisitā uddisituṃ (sī. pī. ka.), aññatra tena bhagavatā arahatā [T 2.0259] sammāsambuddhena. Pubbe me, āvuso, agārikabhūtassa sato etadahosi – ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho rajopatho (sī.), abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena paṭapilotikānaṃ [P 2.0220] saṅghāṭiṃ kāretvā karitvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ye loke arahanto te uddissa kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃ.

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Indeed, friend Ānanda, a word was spoken by the bhikkhunī Thullanandā hastily and without reflection. For, friend, from when I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness, I do not know of having pointed to any other teacher besides that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Formerly, friend, when I was a householder, this thought occurred to me: ‘The household life is confining, a path of dust; the going forth is the open air. It is not easy for one dwelling in a house to practice this holy life, utterly complete, utterly pure, polished like a conch shell. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’ So, friend, after some time, having had a patchwork robe of rags made, and dedicating it to those in the world who are Arahants, I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness.

So evaṃ pabbajito samāno addhānamaggappaṭipanno addasaṃ bhagavantaṃ antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca nāḷandaṃ bahuputte cetiye nisinnaṃ. Disvāna me etadahosi – ‘satthārañca vatāhaṃ passeyyaṃ, bhagavantameva passeyyaṃ; sugatañca vatāhaṃ passeyyaṃ, bhagavantameva passeyyaṃ; sammāsambuddhañca vatāhaṃ passeyyaṃ; bhagavantameva passeyya’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi; satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmī’ti[M 1.0420]. Evaṃ vutte maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā etadavoca – ‘yo kho, kassapa, evaṃ sabbacetasā samannāgataṃ sāvakaṃ ajānaññeva vadeyya jānāmīti, apassaññeva vadeyya passāmīti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Ahaṃ kho pana, kassapa, jānaññeva vadāmi jānāmīti, passaññeva [T 2.0260] vadāmi passāmī’ti.

“Having thus gone forth, while traveling on the long road, I saw the Blessed One seated at the Bahuputta Cetiya, between Rājagaha and Nāḷandā. Seeing him, this thought occurred to me: ‘If I were to see the Teacher, may I see the Blessed One himself! If I were to see the Well-Gone One, may I see the Blessed One himself! If I were to see the Perfectly Enlightened One, may I see the Blessed One himself!’ Then, friend, right there I fell with my head at the Blessed One’s feet and said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher; I am a disciple. Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher; I am a disciple.’ When this was said, friend, the Blessed One said this to me: ‘Kassapa, if anyone, not knowing, were to say, “I know,” or, not seeing, were to say, “I see,” regarding a disciple so endowed with all sincerity of mind, his head would split apart. But I, Kassapa, knowing, say, “I know,” and seeing, say, “I see.”’

Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘tibbaṃ me hirottappaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ bhavissati theresu navesu majjhimesū’ti. Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus in this Dispensation: “Intense shame and fear of wrongdoing will be established in me towards the elder, new, and middle bhikkhus.” Thus indeed, Kassapa, should you train.’

Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kiñci dhammaṃ suṇissāmi kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi karitvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇissāmī’ti. Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus in this Dispensation: “Whatever teaching connected with the wholesome I shall hear, I will listen to all of it, paying respect, taking it to heart, applying my whole mind, and with an attentive ear.” Thus indeed, Kassapa, should you train.’

Tasmātiha [V 1.0199] te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘sātasahagatā ca me kāyagatāsati na vijahissatī’ti. Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbanti.

‘Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus in this Dispensation: “And mindfulness directed to the body, accompanied by pleasure, will not abandon me.” Thus indeed, Kassapa, should you train.’

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Sattāhameva [P 2.0221] khvāhaṃ, āvuso, saraṇo sāṇo (sī.) raṭṭhapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjiṃ”. Aṭṭhamiyā aññā udapādi.

“Then, friend, the Blessed One, having admonished me with this exhortation, rose from his seat and departed. For seven days only, friend, I ate the almsfood of the realm while still with defilements. On the eighth day, final knowledge arose.”

“Atha kho, āvuso, bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṃ rukkhamūlaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Atha khvāhaṃ, āvuso, paṭapilotikānaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ catugguṇaṃ paññapetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘idha, bhante, bhagavā nisīdatu, yaṃ mamassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’ti. Nisīdi kho, āvuso, bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā etadavoca – ‘mudukā kho tyāyaṃ, kassapa, paṭapilotikānaṃ saṅghāṭī’ti. ‘Paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā paṭapilotikānaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ anukampaṃ upādāyā’ti. ‘Dhāressasi pana me tvaṃ, kassapa, sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti. ‘Dhāressāmahaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti. “So [T 2.0261] khvāhaṃ, āvuso, paṭapilotikānaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ bhagavato pādāsiṃ. Ahaṃ pana bhagavato sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanāni paṭipajjiṃ”.

Then, friend, the Blessed One stepped off the road and approached the foot of a certain tree. Then, friend, I spread out my outer robe of worn-out cloths, folded in four, and said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One sit here. May that be for my welfare and happiness for a long time.’ The Blessed One, friend, indeed sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to me: ‘Soft, Kassapa, is this your outer robe of worn-out cloths.’ ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept my outer robe of worn-out cloths out of compassion.’ ‘But will you then wear my worn-out, hempen, dust-heap robes, Kassapa?’ ‘Venerable sir, I will wear the Blessed One’s worn-out, hempen, dust-heap robes.’ So, friend, I gave the outer robe of worn-out cloths to the Blessed One, and I, for my part, undertook to wear the Blessed One’s worn-out, hempen, dust-heap robes.

“Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo, paṭiggahitāni [M 1.0421] paṭiggahetā (sī.) sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti, mamaṃ taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo, paṭiggahitāni sāṇāni paṃsukūlāni nibbasanānī’”ti.

Friend, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘The Blessed One’s son, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of the Dhamma, created by the Dhamma, heir to the Dhamma, has accepted the worn-out, hempen, dust-heap robes,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, would say: ‘The Blessed One’s son, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of the Dhamma, created by the Dhamma, heir to the Dhamma, has accepted the worn-out, hempen, dust-heap robes.’

“Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ [P 2.0222] pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi…pe… (navannaṃ anupubbavihārasamāpattinaṃ pañcannañca abhiññānaṃ evaṃ vitthāro veditabbo)[V 1.0200].

Friend, whenever I wish, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. Friend, whenever I wish… (and so on for the nine successive attainments and the five direct knowledges; this should be understood in detail).

“Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi; sattaratanaṃ vā, āvuso, nāgaṃ aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanaṃ vā tālapattikāya chādetabbaṃ maññeyya, yo me cha abhiññā chādetabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

Friend, with the destruction of the taints, I dwell having realized for myself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. Friend, one might think of covering a seven-cubit elephant or a seven-and-a-half-cubit elephant with a palm leaf; so too one who would think of covering my six direct knowledges.

Cavittha ca pana thullanandā bhikkhunī brahmacariyamhāti. Ekādasamaṃ.

And the bhikkhunī Thullanandā fell away from the holy life. The Eleventh.

12. Paraṃmaraṇasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on After Death

155. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca sāriputto [T 2.0262] bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākassapena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, āvuso kassapa, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panāvuso, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Evampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ [P 2.0223] nu kho, āvuso, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panāvuso, neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Evampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato [M 1.0422] paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kasmā cetaṃ, āvuso[V 1.0203], abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Na hetaṃ, āvuso, atthasaṃhitaṃ nādibrahmacariyakaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Tasmā taṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti.

155. On one occasion, the Venerable Mahākassapa and the Venerable Sāriputta were dwelling in Bārāṇasī, at Isipatana, in the Deer Park. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta, having arisen from seclusion, approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having exchanged courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Friend Kassapa, does the Tathāgata exist after death?” “This, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’” “Then, friend, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?” “This too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’” “Friend, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?” “This, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then, friend, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” “But why, friend, has this not been declared by the Blessed One?” “Because, friend, it is not connected with the goal, is not fundamental to the holy life, and does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, or to Nibbāna. That is why it has not been declared by the Blessed One.”

“Atha kiñcarahāvuso, byākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Idaṃ ‘dukkha’nti kho[T 2.0263], āvuso, byākataṃ bhagavatā; ayaṃ ‘dukkhasamudayo’ti byākataṃ bhagavatā; ayaṃ ‘dukkhanirodho’ti byākataṃ bhagavatā; ayaṃ ‘dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti byākataṃ bhagavatā”ti. “Kasmā cetaṃ, āvuso, byākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Etañhi, āvuso, atthasaṃhitaṃ etaṃ ādibrahmacariyakaṃ etaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Tasmā taṃ byākataṃ bhagavatā”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

“Then what, friend, has been declared by the Blessed One?” “‘This is suffering,’ friend, has been declared by the Blessed One; ‘This is the origin of suffering,’ has been declared by the Blessed One; ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ has been declared by the Blessed One; ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,’ has been declared by the Blessed One.” “And why, friend, has this been declared by the Blessed One?” “Because, friend, this is connected with the goal, this is fundamental to the holy life, this leads to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, to Nibbāna. That is why it has been declared by the Blessed One.” The Twelfth.

13. Saddhammappatirūpakasuttaṃ

13. The Discourse on the Counterfeit of the True Dhamma

156. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 2.0224] nisinno kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena pubbe appatarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni ahesuṃ bahutarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahiṃsu? Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yenetarahi bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahantī”ti? “Evañcetaṃ, kassapa, hoti sattesu hāyamānesu saddhamme antaradhāyamāne, bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni honti appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahanti. Na tāva, kassapa, saddhammassa antaradhānaṃ hoti yāva na saddhammappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati. Yato ca kho, kassapa, saddhammappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati, atha saddhammassa antaradhānaṃ hoti”.

156. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Mahākassapa said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why in the past there were fewer training rules and more bhikkhus were established in final knowledge? And what, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why now there are more training rules and fewer bhikkhus are established in final knowledge?” “It is thus, Kassapa. When beings are declining and the good Dhamma is disappearing, there are more training rules and fewer bhikkhus are established in final knowledge. The good Dhamma does not disappear, Kassapa, as long as a counterfeit of the good Dhamma has not arisen in the world. But when, Kassapa, a counterfeit of the good Dhamma arises in the world, then the good Dhamma disappears.”

“Seyyathāpi, kassapa, na tāva jātarūpassa antaradhānaṃ [T 2.0264] hoti yāva na jātarūpappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati. Yato ca kho, kassapa, jātarūpappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati, atha jātarūpassa antaradhānaṃ hoti. Evameva kho, kassapa, na tāva saddhammassa antaradhānaṃ hoti yāva [V 1.0204][M 1.0423] na saddhammappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati. Yato ca kho, kassapa, saddhammappatirūpakaṃ loke uppajjati, atha saddhammassa antaradhānaṃ hoti.

“Just as, Kassapa, genuine gold does not disappear as long as counterfeit gold has not arisen in the world. But when, Kassapa, counterfeit gold arises in the world, then genuine gold disappears. In the same way, Kassapa, the good Dhamma does not disappear as long as a counterfeit of the good Dhamma has not arisen in the world. But when, Kassapa, a counterfeit of the good Dhamma arises in the world, then the good Dhamma disappears.”

“Na kho, kassapa, pathavīdhātu saddhammaṃ antaradhāpeti, na āpodhātu saddhammaṃ antaradhāpeti, na tejodhātu saddhammaṃ antaradhāpeti, na vāyodhātu saddhammaṃ antaradhāpeti; atha kho idheva te uppajjanti moghapurisā ye imaṃ saddhammaṃ antaradhāpenti. Seyyathāpi, kassapa, nāvā ādikeneva opilavati; na kho, kassapa, evaṃ saddhammassa antaradhānaṃ hoti.

“It is not, Kassapa, that the earth element makes the good Dhamma disappear, nor the water element, nor the fire element, nor the air element; but rather, it is the foolish persons who arise right here that make this good Dhamma disappear. Just as a ship, Kassapa, sinks only by being overloaded; it is not in such a way, Kassapa, that the good Dhamma disappears.”

“Pañca khome, kassapa, okkamaniyā dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṃvattanti. Katame pañca? Idha, kassapa, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari agāravā viharanti appatissā, dhamme agāravā viharanti appatissā, saṅghe agāravā viharanti appatissā, sikkhāya [P 2.0225] agāravā viharanti appatissā, samādhismiṃ agāravā viharanti appatissā – ime kho, kassapa, pañca okkamaniyā dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṃvattanti.

“Kassapa, there are these five debilitating things that lead to the confusion and disappearance of the good Dhamma. What five? Here, Kassapa, bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers dwell without reverence and deference for the Teacher. They dwell without reverence and deference for the Dhamma. They dwell without reverence and deference for the Saṅgha. They dwell without reverence and deference for the training. They dwell without reverence and deference for concentration. These, Kassapa, are the five debilitating things that lead to the confusion and disappearance of the good Dhamma.”

“Pañca khome, kassapa, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya [T 2.0265] anantaradhānāya saṃvattanti. Katame pañca? Idha, kassapa, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, dhamme sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, saṅghe sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, sikkhāya sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, samādhismiṃ sagāravā viharanti sappatissā – ime kho, kassapa, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṃvattantī”ti. Terasamaṃ.

“Kassapa, these five things lead to the stability, non-confusion, and non-disappearance of the good Dhamma. What five? Here, Kassapa, bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers dwell with reverence and deference for the Teacher, with reverence and deference for the Dhamma, with reverence and deference for the Saṅgha, with reverence and deference for the training, and with reverence and deference for concentration. These, Kassapa, are the five things that lead to the stability, non-confusion, and non-disappearance of the good Dhamma.” Thirteenth.

Kassapasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Kassapa Saṃyutta is completed.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Santuṭṭhañca anottappī, candūpamaṃ kulūpakaṃ;

Jiṇṇaṃ tayo ca ovādā, jhānābhiññā upassayaṃ;

Cīvaraṃ paraṃmaraṇaṃ, saddhammappatirūpakanti.

Contentment and the Heedless, Moon-like and the Family-seeker; The Aged, three on Exhortation, Absorption-and-direct-knowledge, and the Lodging; The Robe, After Death, and the Counterfeit of the Good Dhamma.

6. Lābhasakkārasaṃyuttaṃ

6. The Connected Discourses on Gains and Honor

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Dāruṇasuttaṃ

1. Harsh

157. Evaṃ [T 2.0266][V 1.0205][M 1.0424] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā [P 2.0226] etadavoca –

157. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘uppannaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahissāma, na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and fame are harsh, bitter, and rough, an impediment to the attainment of the unsurpassed security from bondage. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘We will abandon arisen gain, honor, and fame, and arisen gain, honor, and fame will not stand overwhelming our minds.’ Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” First.

2. Baḷisasuttaṃ

2. The Fishhook

158. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, bāḷisiko āmisagataṃ baḷisaṃ gambhīre udakarahade pakkhipeyya. Tamenaṃ aññataro āmisacakkhu maccho gileyya. Evañhi so, bhikkhave, maccho gilabaḷiso bāḷisikassa anayaṃ āpanno byasanaṃ āpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāḷisikassa”.

158. Dwelling at Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and fame are harsh, bitter, and rough, an impediment to the attainment of the unsurpassed security from bondage. Suppose, bhikkhus, a fisherman were to cast a baited hook into a deep lake. A certain fish, with its eye on the bait, would swallow it. Thus, bhikkhus, that fish, having swallowed the hook, has met with misfortune, has met with disaster, and is subject to the fisherman’s will.”

“Bāḷisikoti kho, bhikkhave, mārassetaṃ pāpimato adhivacanaṃ. Baḷisanti kho, bhikkhave[V 1.0206], lābhasakkārasilokassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Yo hi koci[T 2.0267], bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ assādeti nikāmeti, ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gilabaḷiso mārassa anayaṃ āpanno byasanaṃ āpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave[M 1.0425], lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘uppannaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahissāma, na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

“‘Fisherman,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for Māra, the Evil One. ‘Hook,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for gain, honor, and fame. Whatever bhikkhu, bhikkhus, enjoys and desires arisen gain, honor, and fame, this bhikkhu is called one who has swallowed Māra's hook; he has met with misfortune, has met with disaster, and is to be done with as the Evil One wishes. So harsh, bhikkhus, is gain, honor, and fame—sharp, coarse, and an impediment to the attainment of the unsurpassed security from bondage. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘We will abandon arisen gain, honor, and fame, and arisen gain, honor, and fame will not stand overwhelming our minds.’ Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.”

3. Kummasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Tortoise

159. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo[P 2.0227], bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ udakarahade mahākummakulaṃ ciranivāsi ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro kummo aññataraṃ kummaṃ etadavoca – ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta kumma, etaṃ padesaṃ agamāsī’ti. Agamāsi kho, bhikkhave, so kummo taṃ padesaṃ. Tamenaṃ luddo papatāya vijjhi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, so kummo yena so kummo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, so kummo taṃ kummaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna taṃ kummaṃ etadavoca – ‘kacci tvaṃ, tāta kumma, na taṃ padesaṃ agamāsī’ti? ‘Agamāsiṃ khvāhaṃ, tāta kumma, taṃ padesa’nti. ‘Kacci [T 2.0268] panāsi, tāta kumma, akkhato anupahato’ti? ‘Akkhato khomhi, tāta kumma, anupahato, atthi ca me idaṃ suttakaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandha’nti. ‘Tagghasi, tāta kumma, khato, taggha upahato. Etena hi te, tāta kumma, suttakena pitaro ca pitāmahā ca anayaṃ āpannā byasanaṃ āpannā. Gaccha dāni tvaṃ, tāta kumma, na dāni tvaṃ amhāka’”nti.

159. At Sāvatthī… “Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… for attainment. Once upon a time, bhikkhus, in a certain lake, a large family of tortoises had been living for a long time. Then, bhikkhus, one tortoise said to another tortoise: ‘My dear tortoise, do not go to that region.’ But that tortoise, bhikkhus, went to that region. A hunter pierced him with a spike on a line. Then, bhikkhus, that tortoise approached the other tortoise. That tortoise, bhikkhus, saw the other tortoise coming from afar. Having seen him, he said to that tortoise: ‘My dear tortoise, did you not go to that region?’ ‘I did go to that region, my dear tortoise.’ ‘But are you, my dear tortoise, unwounded and unharmed?’ ‘I am unwounded and unharmed, my dear tortoise, but this little string is following behind me.’ ‘Indeed, my dear tortoise, you are wounded; indeed, you are harmed. For by this little string, my dear tortoise, your fathers and grandfathers met with misfortune and disaster. Go now, my dear tortoise; you are no longer one of us.’”

“Luddoti kho, bhikkhave, mārassetaṃ pāpimato adhivacanaṃ. Papatāti kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasilokassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Suttakanti kho, bhikkhave, nandirāgassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ assādeti nikāmeti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu giddho papatāya bhikkhu papatāya (syā. kaṃ.), bhikkhu viddho papatāya (?) anayaṃ āpanno byasanaṃ āpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo [V 1.0207] pāpimato. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi [P 2.0228] vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“‘Hunter,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for Māra, the Evil One. ‘Spike on a line,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for gain, honor, and fame. ‘Little string,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for delight and lust. Any bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who savors and desires arisen gain, honor, and fame—this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be greedy for the spike on a line, to have met with misfortune and come to ruin, and to be at the mercy of the Evil One. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.”

4. Dīghalomikasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Long-Fleeced One

160. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0426] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dīghalomikā eḷakā kaṇṭakagahanaṃ paviseyya. Sā tatra tatra sajjeyya, tatra tatra gayheyya gaccheyya (sī.), gaṇheyya (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), tatra tatra bajjheyya, tatra tatra anayabyasanaṃ āpajjeyya. ‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā [T 2.0269] piṇḍāya pavisati. So tatra tatra sajjati, tatra tatra gayhati, tatra tatra bajjhati, tatra tatra anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba’”nti. Catutthaṃ.

160. At Sāvatthī… “Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… for attainment. Suppose, bhikkhus, a long-fleeced ewe were to enter a thorny thicket. She would get stuck here and there, get caught here and there, get bound here and there, and would meet with misfortune and ruin. In the same way, bhikkhus, some bhikkhu here, being overcome by gain, honor, and fame, with his mind consumed, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, enters a village or a town for alms-food. He gets stuck here and there, gets caught here and there, gets bound here and there, and meets with misfortune and ruin. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.”

5. Mīḷhakasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Dung-Eating Insect

161. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mīḷhakā gūthādī gūthapūrā puṇṇā gūthassa. Purato cassa mahāgūthapuñjo. Sā tena aññā mīḷhakā atimaññeyya – ‘ahamhi gūthādī gūthapūrā puṇṇā gūthassa, purato ca myāyaṃ mahāgūthapuñjo’ti. Evameva [P 2.0229] kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisati. So tattha bhuttāvī ca hoti yāvadattho, nimantito ca svātanāya, piṇḍapāto cassa pūro. So ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhugaṇassa majjhe vikatthati – ‘bhuttāvī camhi yāvadattho, nimantito camhi svātanāya, piṇḍapāto ca myāyaṃ pūro, lābhī camhi cīvara-piṇḍapāta-senāsana-gilānappaccaya-bhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ, ime panaññe bhikkhū appapuññā appesakkhā na lābhino cīvara-piṇḍapātasenāsana-gilānappaccaya-bhesajja-parikkhārāna’nti. So tena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto aññe pesale bhikkhū atimaññati. Tañhi tassa, bhikkhave[T 2.0270], moghapurisassa [V 1.0208] hoti dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

161. At Sāvatthī… “Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… for the attainment. Just as, bhikkhus, a dung-eating insect, full of dung, replete with dung, and with a great heap of dung before it, might disparage other dung-eating insects on account of it, thinking: ‘I am a dung-eater, full of dung, replete with dung, and this great heap of dung is before me.’ In the same way, bhikkhus, some bhikkhu here, his mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and fame, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms. There he has eaten his fill, is invited for the next day, and his alms-bowl is full. Having gone to the monastery, he boasts in the midst of the assembly of bhikkhus: ‘I have eaten my fill and am invited for the next day. This alms-bowl of mine is full. I am a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. But these other bhikkhus are of little merit, of little influence; they are not recipients of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick.’ His mind overcome and consumed by that gain, honor, and fame, he disparages other virtuous bhikkhus. That, bhikkhus, leads to the long-term harm and suffering of that foolish person. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.”

6. Asanisuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Thunderbolt

162. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0427] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. upari tatiyavagge tatiyacatutthasuttesu “mā ca kho tvaṃ tāta sekhaṃ… anupāpuṇātū”ti āgataṃ. tena nayena idhāpi attho gahetabbo. ettha hi kiṃ saddena paṭikkhepatthopi sakkā ñātuṃ, yathā “sayaṃ abhiññāya kamuddiseyya”nti. tasmā kaṃ… āgacchatūti ettha kamapi… mā āgacchatūti ca, kaṃ sekhaṃ… anupāpuṇātūti ettha kamapi sekhaṃ… mā pāpuṇātūti ca attho veditabbo. aṭṭhakathāṭīkāsu ca ayamevattho ñāpito Kaṃ, bhikkhave, asanivicakkaṃ āgacchatu upari tatiyavagge tariyacatutthasuttesu “mā ca kho tvaṃ tāta sekhaṃ… anupāpuṇātū”ti āgataṃ. tena nayena idhāpi attho gahetabbo. ettha hi kiṃ saddena paṭikkhepatthopi sakkā ñātuṃ, yathā “sayaṃ abhiññāya kamuddiseyya”nti. tasmā kaṃ… āgacchatūti ettha kamapi… mā āgacchatūtica, taṃ sekhaṃ… anupāpuṇātūti ettha kamapi sekhaṃ… mā pāpuṇātūti ca attho veditabbo. aṭṭhakathāṭīkāsu ca ayamevattho ñāpito, sekhaṃ asanivicakkaṃ, taṃ sekhaṃ (pī. ka.), asanivicakkaṃ, sekhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), asanivicakkaṃ āgacchatu, kaṃ sekhaṃ (?) appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇātu” anupāpuṇāti (pī. ka.).

162. At Sāvatthī… and so on… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh… and so on… an obstacle to attainment. Bhikkhus, upon what person does the thunderbolt-wheel fall? Upon a trainee whose mind has not attained the goal, whom gain, honor, and praise overtake.”

“Asanivicakkanti kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasilokassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“‘Thunderbolt-wheel,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for gain, honor, and praise. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… and so on… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The sixth.

7. Diddhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Poisoned Dart

163. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo[P 2.0230], bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Kaṃ, bhikkhave, diddhagatena visallena sallena diṭṭhigatena visallena (ka. sī.), diṭṭhigatena sallena (syā. kaṃ.), diṭṭhigatena visallena sallena (ka.), diṭṭhagatena visallena sallena (pī.) vijjhatu, sekhaṃ vijjhatu, taṃ sekhaṃ (sī.), vijjhati, taṃ sekhaṃ (pī. ka.) appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇātu” anupāpuṇāti (pī. ka.).

163. At Sāvatthī… and so on… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh… and so on… an obstacle to attainment. Bhikkhus, whom does a poison-smeared dart pierce? A trainee whose mind has not attained the goal, whom gain, honor, and praise overtake.”

“Sallanti kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasilokassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“‘Dart,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for gain, honor, and praise. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… and so on… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The seventh.

8. Siṅgālasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Jackal

164. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ [M 1.0428] jarasiṅgālassa siṅgālassa (ka.), jarasigālassa (sī. syā. kaṃ.) vassamānassā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Eso kho, bhikkhave, jarasiṅgālo ukkaṇḍakena [T 2.0271] ukkaṇḍakena (sī.), ukkaṇṇakena (syā. kaṃ. pī.) nāma rogajātena phuṭṭho neva bilagato ramati, na rukkhamūlagato ramati, na ajjhokāsagato ramati; yena [V 1.0209] yena gacchati, yattha yattha tiṭṭhati, yattha yattha nisīdati, yattha yattha nipajjati; tattha tattha anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto neva suññāgāragato ramati, na rukkhamūlagato ramati, na ajjhokāsagato ramati; yena yena gacchati, yattha yattha tiṭṭhati, yattha yattha nisīdati, yattha yattha nipajjati; tattha tattha anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ [P 2.0231] dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

164. At Sāvatthī… and so on… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh… and so on… an obstacle to attainment. Have you not heard, bhikkhus, the sound of the old jackal howling at dawn?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “That old jackal, bhikkhus, is afflicted by a disease called ukkaṇḍaka. He finds no delight whether he goes to a burrow, to the foot of a tree, or to an open space. Wherever he goes, wherever he stands, wherever he sits, wherever he lies down, there he meets with misfortune and ruin. So too, bhikkhus, here a certain bhikkhu is overcome and his mind is consumed by gain, honor, and praise. He finds no delight whether he goes to an empty dwelling, to the foot of a tree, or to an open space. Wherever he goes, wherever he stands, wherever he sits, wherever he lies down, there he meets with misfortune and ruin. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… and so on… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The eighth.

9. Verambhasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Verambha Winds

165. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Upari, bhikkhave, ākāse verambhā verambā (sī. pī.) nāma vātā vāyanti. Tattha yo pakkhī gacchati tamenaṃ verambhā vātā khipanti. Tassa verambhavātakkhittassa aññeneva pādā gacchanti, aññena pakkhā gacchanti, aññena sīsaṃ gacchati, aññena kāyo gacchati. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisati arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya arakkhitena cittena, anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā, asaṃvutehi indriyehi. So tattha [T 2.0272] passati mātugāmaṃ dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā. Tassa mātugāmaṃ disvā dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. So rāgānuddhaṃsitena cittena sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati. Tassa aññe cīvaraṃ haranti, aññe pattaṃ haranti, aññe nisīdanaṃ haranti, aññe sūcigharaṃ haranti, verambhavātakkhittasseva sakuṇassa. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Navamaṃ.

165. At Sāvatthī… and so on… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh… and so on… an obstacle to attainment. Above, bhikkhus, in the sky, winds called Verambha blow. Any bird that goes there is thrown down by the Verambha winds. When thrown down by the Verambha winds, its feet go one way, its wings another, its head another, and its body yet another. So too, bhikkhus, here a certain bhikkhu, overcome and with his mind consumed by gain, honor, and praise, dresses in the morning, takes his bowl and robe, and enters a village or town for alms with body unguarded, speech unguarded, mind unguarded, mindfulness unestablished, and senses unrestrained. There he sees a woman improperly dressed or improperly covered. Upon seeing the woman improperly dressed or improperly covered, lust assails his mind. With his mind assailed by lust, he renounces the training and returns to a lower life. Some take his robe, others his bowl, others his sitting cloth, and still others his needle case—just like the bird thrown down by the Verambha winds. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… and so on… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The ninth.

10. Sagāthakasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse with Verses

166. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0429] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ passāmi sakkārena [P 2.0232] abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannaṃ. Idha panāhaṃ, bhikkhave[V 1.0210], ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ passāmi asakkārena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannaṃ. Idha panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ passāmi sakkārena ca asakkārena ca tadubhayena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti.

166. At Sāvatthī… and so on… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh… and so on… an obstacle to attainment. Here, bhikkhus, I see a certain person whose mind is overcome and consumed by honor, who, with the breakup of the body, after death, has been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. Here, bhikkhus, I see a certain person whose mind is overcome and consumed by lack of honor, who, with the breakup of the body, after death, has been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. Here, bhikkhus, I see a certain person whose mind is overcome and consumed by both honor and lack of honor, who, with the breakup of the body, after death, has been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… and so on… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Yassa [T 2.0273] sakkariyamānassa, asakkārena cūbhayaṃ;

Samādhi na vikampati, appamāṇavihārino appamādavihārino (pī. ka.) appamāṇoti hettha phalasamādhi, na sati.

“For one dwelling heedfully, whether being honored or not honored, or by both, their concentration does not waver.

“Taṃ jhāyinaṃ sātatikaṃ, sukhumaṃ diṭṭhivipassakaṃ;

Upādānakkhayārāmaṃ, āhu sappuriso itī”ti. dasamaṃ;

“That one—a meditator, persevering, with subtle insight into the view, who delights in the destruction of clinging—they call a true person.” The tenth.

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Dāruṇo baḷisaṃ kummaṃ, dīghalomi ca mīḷhakaṃ;

Asani diddhaṃ siṅgālaṃ, verambhena sagāthakanti.

Harsh, the Hook, the Tortoise, the Long-haired One, and the Dung-eater; the Thunderbolt, the Poisoned, the Jackal, with Verambha, and With Verses.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Suvaṇṇapātisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Golden Bowl

167. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0274][M 1.0430][P 2.0233] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… adhigamāya. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – ‘na cāyamāyasmā [V 1.0211] suvaṇṇapātiyāpi rūpiyacuṇṇaparipūrāya hetu sampajānamusā bhāseyyā’ti. Tamenaṃ passāmi aparena samayena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsantaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

167. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh, an obstacle to attainment. Here, bhikkhus, I know a certain individual, having encompassed their mind with my own mind thus: ‘This venerable one would not speak a deliberate falsehood even for the sake of a golden bowl filled with silver dust.’ At a later time, I see that same person, their mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, speaking a deliberate falsehood. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' First.

2. Rūpiyapātisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Silver Bowl

168. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – ‘na cāyamāyasmā rūpiyapātiyāpi suvaṇṇacuṇṇaparipūrāya hetu sampajānamusā bhāseyyā’ti. Tamenaṃ passāmi aparena samayena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsantaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

168. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh... Here, bhikkhus, I know a certain individual, having encompassed their mind with my own mind thus: ‘This venerable one would not speak a deliberate falsehood even for the sake of a silver bowl filled with gold dust.’ At a later time, I see that same person, their mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, speaking a deliberate falsehood. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' Second.

3-10. Suvaṇṇanikkhasuttādiaṭṭhakaṃ

3–10. The Octad Beginning with the Discourse on the Gold Coin

169. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “idhāhaṃ[P 2.0234], bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – ‘na cāyamāyasmā suvaṇṇanikkhassāpi [T 2.0275] hetu…pe… suvaṇṇanikkhasatassāpi hetu… siṅgīnikkhassāpi hetu… siṅgīnikkhasatassāpi hetu… pathaviyāpi jātarūpaparipūrāya hetu… āmisakiñcikkhahetupi… jīvitahetupi… janapadakalyāṇiyāpi hetu sampajānamusā bhāseyyā’ti. Tamenaṃ passāmi aparena samayena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsantaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dasamaṃ.

169. At Sāvatthī... 'Here, bhikkhus, I know a certain individual, having encompassed their mind with my own mind thus: ‘This venerable one would not speak a deliberate falsehood even for the sake of a gold coin... even for the sake of a hundred gold coins... even for the sake of a coin of refined gold... even for the sake of a hundred coins of refined gold... even for the sake of the earth filled with gold... even for the sake of a mere trifle of material things... even for the sake of his life... even for the sake of the most beautiful woman in the land.’ At a later time, I see that same person, their mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, speaking a deliberate falsehood. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' Tenth.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Dve [V 1.0212][M 1.0431] pāti dve suvaṇṇā ca, siṅgīhi apare duve;

Pathavī kiñcikkhajīvitaṃ, janapadakalyāṇiyā dasāti.

Two on bowls, two on gold coins, and two others on refined gold; The earth, a trifle, life, and the most beautiful woman in the land—these are the ten.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Mātugāmasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on a Woman

170. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0276] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… na [P 2.0235] tassa, bhikkhave, mātugāmo eko ekassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yassa lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko …pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

170. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh... Bhikkhus, a single woman does not seize and occupy a person’s mind in the way that gain, honor, and renown seize and occupy that person's mind. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' First.

2. Kalyāṇīsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Beautiful Woman

171. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… na tassa, bhikkhave, janapadakalyāṇī ekā ekassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yassa lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

171. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh... Bhikkhus, the single most beautiful woman in the land does not seize and occupy a person’s mind in the way that gain, honor, and renown seize and occupy that person's mind. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' Second.

3. Ekaputtakasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Only Son

172. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… saddhā, bhikkhave, upāsikā ekaputtakaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ evaṃ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya – ‘tādiso, tāta, bhavāhi yādiso citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako’ti. Esā, bhikkhave[T 2.0277], tulā etaṃ pamāṇaṃ mama sāvakānaṃ upāsakānaṃ, yadidaṃ citto [V 1.0213] ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako. Sace kho tvaṃ, tāta, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajasi; tādiso, tāta, bhavāhi yādisā sāriputtamoggallānāti. Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṃ pamāṇaṃ mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, yadidaṃ sāriputtamoggalānā[M 1.0432]. Mā ca kho tvaṃ, tāta, sekhaṃ appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇātūti. Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ [P 2.0236] sekhaṃ appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇāti, so tassa hoti antarāyāya. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

172. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh... A faithful female lay follower, bhikkhus, rightly urging her dear and beloved only son, might urge him thus: ‘Dear boy, be like Citta the householder and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.’ This, bhikkhus, is the balance and the measure for my male lay disciples, namely, Citta the householder and Hatthaka of Āḷavī. ‘But if, dear boy, you go forth from the household life into homelessness, then be like Sāriputta and Moggallāna.’ This, bhikkhus, is the balance and the measure for my bhikkhu disciples, namely, Sāriputta and Moggallāna. ‘And may gain, honor, and renown not befall you, dear boy, while you are still a trainee who has not attained the goal.’ For if, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown befall a bhikkhu who is a trainee and has not attained the goal, that becomes an obstacle for him. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' Third.

4. Ekadhītusuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Only Daughter

173. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… saddhā bhikkhave upāsikā ekaṃ dhītaraṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ evaṃ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya – ‘tādisā, ayye, bhavāhi yādisā khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā veḷukaṇḍakī (sī. chakkaṅguttarepi) ca nandamātā’ti. Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṃ pamāṇaṃ mama sāvikānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, yadidaṃ khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā ca nandamātā. Sace kho tvaṃ, ayye, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajasi; tādisā, ayye, bhavāhi yādisā khemā ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā cāti. Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṃ pamāṇaṃ mama sāvikānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ, yadidaṃ khemā [T 2.0278] ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā ca. Mā ca kho tvaṃ, ayye, sekhaṃ appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇātūti. Taṃ ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniṃ sekhaṃ appattamānasaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇāti, so tassā hoti antarāyāya. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Catutthaṃ.

173. At Sāvatthī... 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown are harsh... A faithful female lay follower, bhikkhus, rightly urging her dear and beloved only daughter, might urge her thus: ‘Dear, be like the female lay disciple Khujjuttarā and Nandamātā of Veḷukaṇḍakī.’ This, bhikkhus, is the balance and the measure for my female lay disciples, namely, the female lay disciple Khujjuttarā and Nandamātā of Veḷukaṇḍakī. ‘If you, dear, go forth from the household life into homelessness, then be like the bhikkhunīs Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā.’ This, bhikkhus, is the balance and the measure for my bhikkhunī disciples, namely, the bhikkhunīs Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā. ‘And may gain, honor, and renown not befall you, dear, while you are still a trainee who has not attained the goal.’ For if, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown befall a bhikkhunī who is a trainee and has not attained the goal, that becomes an obstacle for her. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.' Fourth.

5. Samaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

174. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “ye [P 2.0237] hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā lābhasakkārasilokassa assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmantā sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā [V 1.0214] sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā lābhasakkārasilokassa assādañca ādīnavañca [M 1.0433] nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti, te ca kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

174. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, those ascetics and brahmins who do not truly understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to gain, honor, and praise—these, bhikkhus, are not considered by me to be ascetics among ascetics, or brahmins among brahmins; nor do these venerable ones live having realized for themselves with direct knowledge and attained in this very life the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood. But those ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand as it actually is the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to gain, honor, and praise—these, bhikkhus, are considered by me to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins; and these venerable ones live having realized for themselves with direct knowledge and attained in this very life the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

175. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā lābhasakkārasilokassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti…pe… pajānanti…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

175. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, any ascetics or brahmins who do not truly understand as they really are the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to gain, honor, and praise… But those who do truly understand these things… these venerable ones live having realized for themselves with direct knowledge and attained in this very life the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” The sixth.

7. Tatiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

7. The Third Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

176. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā [T 2.0279] vā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, lābhasakkārasilokasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, lābhasakkārasilokanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, lābhasakkārasilokanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti …pe… pajānanti…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

176. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, those ascetics and brahmins who do not truly understand gain, honor, and praise as it actually is, who do not understand the origin of gain, honor, and praise, who do not understand the cessation of gain, honor, and praise, who do not understand the path leading to the cessation of gain, honor, and praise… But those who do truly understand these things… these venerable ones live having realized for themselves with direct knowledge and attained in this very life the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” The seventh.

8. Chavisuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Outer Skin

177. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasiloko[P 2.0238], bhikkhave, chaviṃ chindati, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindati, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindati, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindati, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindati, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ [V 1.0215] āhacca tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

177. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh. Gain, honor, and praise, bhikkhus, cut through the outer skin; having cut through the outer skin, they cut through the hide; having cut through the hide, they cut through the flesh; having cut through the flesh, they cut through the sinews; having cut through the sinews, they cut through the bone; having cut through the bone, they reach the bone marrow and remain. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.” The eighth.

9. Rajjusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Rope

178. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasiloko, bhikkhave, chaviṃ chindati, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindati, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindati, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindati, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindati, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati”.

178. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh. Gain, honor, and praise, bhikkhus, cut through the outer skin; having cut through the outer skin, they cut through the hide; having cut through the hide, they cut through the flesh; having cut through the flesh, they cut through the sinews; having cut through the sinews, they cut through the bone; having cut through the bone, they reach the bone marrow and remain.”

“Seyyathāpi[M 1.0434], bhikkhave, balavā puriso daḷhāya vāḷarajjuyā jaṅghaṃ veṭhetvā ghaṃseyya. Sā chaviṃ chindeyya, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindeyya, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindeyya, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindeyya, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindeyya, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭheyya. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko [T 2.0280] chaviṃ chindati, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindati, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindati, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindati, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindati, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃmiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Navamaṃ.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a strong man were to bind a leg with a strong horsehair rope and chafe it. It would cut through the outer skin; having cut through the outer skin, it would cut through the hide; having cut through the hide, it would cut through the flesh; having cut through the flesh, it would cut through the sinews; having cut through the sinews, it would cut through the bone; having cut through the bone, it would reach the bone marrow and remain. In the same way, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise cut through the outer skin; having cut through the outer skin, they cut through the hide; having cut through the hide, they cut through the flesh; having cut through the flesh, they cut through the sinews; having cut through the sinews, they cut through the bone; having cut through the bone, they reach the bone marrow and remain. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise… Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.” The ninth.

10. Bhikkhusuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Bhikkhu

179. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “yopi [P 2.0239] so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo tassapāhaṃ lābhasakkārasiloko antarāyāya vadāmī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kissa pana, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno lābhasakkārasiloko antarāyāyā”ti? “Yā hissa sā, ānanda, akuppā cetovimutti nāhaṃ tassā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ antarāyāya vadāmi. Ye ca khvassa, ānanda, appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā adhigatā tesāhamassa lābhasakkārasilokaṃ antarāyāya vadāmi. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, ānanda, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Tasmātihānanda, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘uppannaṃ [V 1.0216] lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahissāma, na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti. Evañhi vo, ānanda, sikkhitabba”nti. Dasamaṃ.

179. At Sāvatthī... “Even for that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, who is an arahant, one with taints destroyed, I declare that gain, honor, and praise are an obstacle.” When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “For what reason, Bhante, are gain, honor, and praise an obstacle for a bhikkhu with taints destroyed?” “Ānanda, I do not say that gain, honor, and praise are an obstacle to his unshakeable liberation of mind. But, Ānanda, for those pleasant dwellings in the here-and-now that have been attained by him dwelling heedfully, ardently, and with a mind dispatched to Nibbāna, for these I say gain, honor, and praise are an obstacle. So harsh, Ānanda, are gain, honor, and praise, so bitter, so cruel, an obstacle to the attainment of the unsurpassed security from the yokes. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train thus: ‘We will abandon arisen gain, honor, and praise, and arisen gain, honor, and praise will not remain, having taken over our minds.’ Thus, Ānanda, should you train yourselves.” The tenth.

Tatiyo vaggo.

The Third Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Mātugāmo [T 2.0281] ca kalyāṇī, putto ca ekadhītu ca;

Samaṇabrāhmaṇā tīṇi, chavi rajju ca bhikkhunāti.

A woman and a beautiful woman, a son and a single daughter; three on ascetics and brahmins, the skin, the rope, and the bhikkhu.

4. Catutthavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter

1. Bhindisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Splitting

180. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0282][M 1.0435] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasilokena [P 2.0240] abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto, bhikkhave, devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindi. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… sikkhitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

180. At Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and praise are harsh. Bhikkhus, Devadatta, his mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and praise, split the Saṅgha. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and praise... Thus should you train.” The first.

2. Kusalamūlasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Wholesome Roots

181. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtassa pariyādiṇṇacittassa, bhikkhave, devadattassa kusalamūlaṃ samucchedamagamā. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… sikkhitabba”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

181. Dwelling in Sāvatthī... 'Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown. Bhikkhus, for Devadatta, his mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, his wholesome roots were utterly cut off. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus should you train.' Second.

3. Kusaladhammasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Wholesome Qualities

182. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0217] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtassa pariyādiṇṇacittassa, bhikkhave, devadattassa kusalo dhammo samucchedamagamā. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… sikkhitabba”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

182. Dwelling in Sāvatthī... 'Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown. Bhikkhus, for Devadatta, his mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, his wholesome quality was utterly cut off. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus should you train.' Third.

4. Sukkadhammasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Bright Qualities

183. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtassa pariyādiṇṇacittassa, bhikkhave, devadattassa sukko dhammo samucchedamagamā. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… sikkhitabba”nti[T 2.0283]. Catutthaṃ.

183. Dwelling in Sāvatthī... 'Harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown. Bhikkhus, for Devadatta, his mind overcome and consumed by gain, honor, and renown, his bright quality was utterly cut off. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown... Thus should you train.' Fourth.

5. Acirapakkantasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on One Who Recently Departed

184. Ekaṃ [P 2.0241] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate acirapakkante devadatte. Tatra kho bhagavā devadattaṃ ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi [M 1.0436] – “attavadhāya, bhikkhave, devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi”.

184. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha on Gijjhakūṭa Peak, not long after Devadatta had departed. There the Blessed One, concerning Devadatta, addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown arose for Devadatta for his own destruction, for his ruin.'

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kadalī attavadhāya phalaṃ deti, parābhavāya phalaṃ deti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.

‘Just as, bhikkhus, a banana plant produces fruit for its own destruction, produces fruit for its ruin; even so, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown arose for Devadatta for his own destruction, for his ruin.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, veḷu attavadhāya phalaṃ deti, parābhavāya phalaṃ deti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.

‘Just as, bhikkhus, a bamboo plant produces fruit for its own destruction, produces fruit for its ruin; even so, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown arose for Devadatta for his own destruction, for his ruin.

“Seyyathāpi[V 1.0218], bhikkhave, naḷo attavadhāya phalaṃ deti, parābhavāya phalaṃ deti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.

‘Just as, bhikkhus, a reed produces fruit for its own destruction, produces fruit for its ruin; even so, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown arose for Devadatta for his own destruction, for his ruin.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, assatarī attavadhāya gabbhaṃ gaṇhāti, parābhavāya gabbhaṃ gaṇhāti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko [T 2.0284] udapādi. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti.

‘Just as, bhikkhus, a female mule conceives for her own destruction, conceives for her ruin; even so, bhikkhus, gain, honor, and renown arose for Devadatta for his own destruction, for his ruin. So harsh, indeed, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown. Thus indeed, bhikkhus, should you train.’

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Phalaṃ ve kadaliṃ hanti, phalaṃ veḷuṃ phalaṃ naḷaṃ;

Sakkāro kāpurisaṃ hanti, gabbho assatariṃ yathāti”. pañcamaṃ;

‘Fruit indeed destroys the banana, fruit the bamboo, and fruit the reed; honor destroys a base person, just as the womb destroys the female mule.’ Fifth.

6. Pañcarathasatasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Five Hundred Chariots

185. Rājagahe [P 2.0242] viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena devadattassa ajātasattukumāro pañcahi rathasatehi sāyaṃ pātaṃ [M 1.0437] upaṭṭhānaṃ gacchati, pañca ca thālipākasatāni bhattābhihāro abhiharīyati. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “devadattassa, bhante, ajātasattukumāro pañcahi rathasatehi sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gacchati, pañca ca thālipākasatāni bhattābhihāro abhiharīyatī”ti. “Mā, bhikkhave, devadattassa lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pihayittha. Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, devadattassa ajātasattukumāro pañcahi rathasatehi sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gamissati, pañca ca thālipākasatāni bhattābhihāro āharīyissati, hāniyeva, bhikkhave, devadattassa pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi”.

185. The Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. At that time, Prince Ajātasattu would attend on Devadatta in the morning and evening with five hundred chariots, and five hundred pots of cooked rice were brought as a meal offering. Then a number of bhikkhus went to the Blessed One, and after approaching and paying homage to him, they sat down to one side. Sitting there, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, Prince Ajātasattu attends on Devadatta in the morning and evening with five hundred chariots, and five hundred pots of cooked rice are brought as a meal offering.” “Bhikkhus, do not envy Devadatta’s gain, honor, and renown. For as long, bhikkhus, as Prince Ajātasattu attends on Devadatta in the morning and evening with five hundred chariots, and five hundred pots of cooked rice are brought as a meal offering, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected for Devadatta, not growth.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, caṇḍassa kukkurassa nāsāya pittaṃ bhindeyyuṃ[T 2.0285], evañhi so, bhikkhave[V 1.0219], kukkuro bhiyyosomattāya caṇḍataro assa; evameva, bhikkhave, yāvakīvañca devadattassa ajātasattukumāro pañcahi rathasatehi sāyaṃ pātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gamissati, pañca ca thālipākasatāni bhattābhihāro āharīyissati, hāniyeva, bhikkhave, devadattassa pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko…pe… evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, one were to break open a gall bladder on the nose of a fierce dog; that dog would thereby become even fiercer. In the same way, bhikkhus, for as long as Prince Ajātasattu attends on Devadatta in the morning and evening with five hundred chariots, and five hundred pots of cooked rice are brought as a meal offering, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected for Devadatta, not growth. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and renown… Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.” Sixth.

7. Mātusuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Mother

186. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Idhāhaṃ[P 2.0243], bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – ‘na cāyamāyasmā mātupi hetu sampajānamusā bhāseyyā’ti. Tamenaṃ passāmi aparena samayena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsantaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘uppannaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahissāma. Na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Sattamaṃ.

186. At Sāvatthī. … “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and fame are harsh, bitter, and rough, an obstacle to the attainment of the unexcelled security from bondage. Here, bhikkhus, I know a certain person, having encompassed their mind with my own, thus: ‘This venerable one would not speak a deliberate falsehood even for the sake of his mother.’ Then at a later time I see that same person—overcome by gain, honor, and fame, with his mind consumed by them—speaking a deliberate falsehood. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame—bitter and rough, an obstacle to the attainment of the unexcelled security from bondage. Therefore, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will abandon arisen gain, honor, and fame, and they, when arisen, will not stand consuming our minds.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.” Seventh.

8-13. Pitusuttādichakkaṃ

8–13. The Six Suttas Beginning with the Pitu Sutta

187. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0438] viharati…pe… “dāruṇo, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Idhāhaṃ[T 2.0286], bhikkhave, ekaccaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi – ‘na cāyamāyasmā pitupi hetu…pe… bhātupi hetu… bhaginiyāpi hetu… puttassapi hetu… dhītuyāpi hetu… pajāpatiyāpi hetu sampajānamusā bhāseyyā’ti. Tamenaṃ passāmi aparena samayena lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūtaṃ pariyādiṇṇacittaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsantaṃ. Evaṃ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘uppannaṃ [P 2.0244] lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahissāma, na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko [V 1.0220] cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Terasamaṃ.

187. At Sāvatthī. … “Bhikkhus, gain, honor, and fame are harsh, bitter, and rough, an obstacle to the attainment of the unexcelled security from bondage. Here, bhikkhus, I know a certain person, having encompassed their mind with my own, thus: ‘This venerable one would not speak a deliberate falsehood even for the sake of his father… nor for the sake of his brother… nor for the sake of his sister… nor for the sake of his son… nor for the sake of his daughter… nor for the sake of his wife.’ Then at a later time I see that same person—overcome by gain, honor, and fame, with his mind consumed by them—speaking a deliberate falsehood. So harsh, bhikkhus, are gain, honor, and fame—bitter and rough, an obstacle to the attainment of the unexcelled security from bondage. Therefore, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will abandon arisen gain, honor, and fame, and they, when arisen, will not stand consuming our minds.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.” Thirteenth.

Catuttho vaggo.

The Fourth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Bhindi mūlaṃ duve dhammā, pakkantaṃ ratha mātari;

Pitā bhātā ca bhaginī, putto dhītā pajāpatīti.

Bhindi, Mūla, the two Dhammas, Pakkanta, Ratha, Mātari; Pitā, Bhātā, and Bhaginī, Putta, Dhītā, and Pajāpati.

Lābhasakkārasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Gain and Honor is completed.

7. Rāhulasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Connected Discourses with Rāhula

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Cakkhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Eye

188. Evaṃ [T 2.0287][V 1.0221][M 1.0439] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

188. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then the Venerable Rāhula approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side.
