Seated to one side, the Venerable Rāhula said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, cakkhuṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ [P 2.0245] panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Sotaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe…. “Ghānaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe… “jivhā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti? “Aniccā, bhante”…pe… “kāyo nicco vā anicco vā”ti? “Anicco, bhante” [T 2.0288] …pe… “mano nicco vā anicco vā”ti? “Anicco, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Rāhula, is the eye permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is the ear permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is the nose permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is the tongue permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is the body permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is the mind permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, rāhula, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati [V 1.0222] …pe… sotasmimpi nibbindati… ghānasmimpi nibbindati… jivhāyapi nibbindati… kāyasmimpi nibbindati… manasmimpi nibbindati; nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Seeing thus, Rāhula, the well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye … with the ear … with the nose … with the tongue … with the body … with the mind. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. Upon liberation, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming back to any state of being.’” First.

2. Rūpasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Forms

189. Dutiyaṃ.

189. At Sāvatthī. … “What do you think, Rāhula, are forms permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Are sounds … odors … tastes … tactile objects … mental objects permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Seeing thus, Rāhula, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with forms … with sounds … with odors … with tastes … with tactile objects … with mental objects. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate … he understands.” Second.

Tatiyaṃ.

At Sāvatthī... “What do you think, Rāhula, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Seeing thus, Rāhula, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form… disenchanted with feeling… disenchanted with perception… disenchanted with volitional formations… disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. Upon liberation, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” Tenth.

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Cakkhu rūpañca viññāṇaṃ, samphasso vedanāya ca;

Saññā sañcetanā taṇhā, dhātu khandhena te dasāti.

The eye, form, and consciousness, contact and feeling; perception, volition, craving, elements, and with the aggregates—these are the ten.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Cakkhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Eye

198. Evaṃ [T 2.0293] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha [P 2.0250] kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ [M 1.0443] bhagavā etadavoca – “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, cakkhuṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? “Aniccaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Sotaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ… jivhā… kāyo… mano nicco vā anicco vā”ti? “Anicco, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti? “Dukkhaṃ, bhante”. “Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evaṃ passaṃ, rāhula, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati…pe… sotasmimpi nibbindati… ghānasmimpi nibbindati [V 1.0228]… jivhāyapi nibbindati… kāyasmimpi nibbindati… manasmimpi nibbindati; nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā [T 2.0294] jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Etena peyyālena dasa suttantā kātabbā. Paṭhamaṃ.

198. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Rāhula went to the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. To the Venerable Rāhula sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: “What do you think, Rāhula, is the eye permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed, it is not so, venerable sir.” “Is the ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… the mind permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it proper to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed, it is not so, venerable sir.” “Seeing thus, Rāhula, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye… with the ear… with the nose… with the tongue… with the body… with the mind. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” By this abbreviated text, ten discourses are to be composed. First.

2-10. Rūpādisuttanavakaṃ

2–10. The Set of Nine Discourses on Forms, etc.

199. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, rūpā [P 2.0251] niccā vā aniccā vā”ti? “Aniccā, bhante”…pe… saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā….

199. Dwelling in Sāvatthī… “What do you think, Rāhula, are forms permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… mental objects….

“Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… sotaviññāṇaṃ… ghānaviññāṇaṃ… jivhāviññāṇaṃ… kāyaviññāṇaṃ… manoviññāṇaṃ….

Eye-consciousness… ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… mind-consciousness….

“Cakkhusamphasso…pe… sotasamphasso… ghānasamphasso… jivhāsamphasso… kāyasamphasso… manosamphasso….

Eye-contact… ear-contact… nose-contact… tongue-contact… body-contact… mind-contact….

“Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… sotasamphassajā vedanā… ghānasamphassajā vedanā… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā… kāyasamphassajā vedanā… manosamphassajā vedanā….

Feeling born of eye-contact… feeling born of ear-contact… feeling born of nose-contact… feeling born of tongue-contact… feeling born of body-contact… feeling born of mind-contact….

“Rūpasaññā…pe… saddasaññā… gandhasaññā… rasasaññā… phoṭṭhabbasaññā… dhammasaññā….

Perception of forms… perception of sounds… perception of odors… perception of tastes… perception of tangibles… perception of mental objects….

“Rūpasañcetanā…pe… saddasañcetanā… gandhasañcetanā… rasasañcetanā… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā… dhammasañcetanā….

Volition regarding forms… volition regarding sounds… volition regarding odors… volition regarding tastes… volition regarding tangibles… volition regarding mental objects….

“Rūpataṇhā [V 1.0229][M 1.0444] …pe… saddataṇhā… gandhataṇhā… rasataṇhā… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā… dhammataṇhā….

Craving for forms… craving for sounds… craving for odors… craving for tastes… craving for tangibles… craving for mental objects….

“Pathavīdhātu…pe… āpodhātu… tejodhātu… vāyodhātu… ākāsadhātu [T 2.0295]… viññāṇadhātu….

The earth element… the water element… the fire element… the wind element… the space element… the consciousness element….

“Rūpaṃ [P 2.0252]…pe… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti? Aniccaṃ, bhante…pe… evaṃ passaṃ rāhula…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātīti. Dasamaṃ.

“Are form… feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Seeing thus, Rāhula… he understands: ‘There is nothing further for this state of being.’” Tenth.

11. Anusayasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Latent Tendencies

200. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, jānato kathaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā na hontī”ti? “Yaṃ kiñci, rāhula, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Evaṃ kho, rāhula, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā [T 2.0296] na hontī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

200. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Rāhula approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rāhula said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, for one who knows how, for one who sees how, do the latent tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit not occur in regard to this conscious body and all external signs?” “Whatever form, Rāhula—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—one sees all form as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—one sees all consciousness as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ It is for one who knows thus, Rāhula, for one who sees thus, that the latent tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit do not occur in regard to this conscious body and all external signs.” Eleventh.

12. Apagatasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on Having Departed

201. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0230][P 2.0253]. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, jānato kathaṃ passato imasmiṃ ca saviññāṇake kāye [M 1.0445] bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṃ mānasaṃ hoti vidhā samatikkantaṃ santaṃ suvimutta”nti? “Yaṃ kiñci, rāhula, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādā vimutto hoti”.

201. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Rāhula approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Rāhula said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how is it that for one who knows, for one who sees, the mind—in regard to this conscious body and all external signs—becomes devoid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit, has transcended the varieties of conceit, is peaceful, and well liberated?” “Whatever form, Rāhula—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—having seen all form as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self,’ one is liberated without clinging.”

“Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādā vimutto hoti. Evaṃ kho, rāhula, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṃ mānasaṃ hoti [T 2.0297] vidhā samatikkantaṃ santaṃ suvimutta”nti. Dvādasamaṃ.

“Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever formations… whatever consciousness—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—having seen all consciousness as it actually is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self,’ one is liberated without clinging. It is for one who knows thus, Rāhula, for one who sees thus, that the mind—in regard to this conscious body and all external signs—becomes devoid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit, has transcended the varieties of conceit, is peaceful, and well liberated.” Twelfth.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Cakkhu [P 2.0254] rūpañca viññāṇaṃ, samphasso vedanāya ca;

Saññā sañcetanā taṇhā, dhātu khandhena te dasa;

Anusayaṃ apagatañceva, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

The Eye, Form, and Consciousness, Contact and Feeling; Perception, Volition, Craving, Element, and with the Aggregate—these are ten; Latent Tendencies and Being Devoid as well. By these, the chapter is declared.

Rāhulasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Rāhula Saṃyutta is concluded.

8. Lakkhaṇasaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Lakkhaṇa Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Aṭṭhisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Skeleton

202. Evaṃ [T 2.0298][V 1.0231][M 1.0446] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno mahāmoggalāno (ka.) gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yenāyasmā lakkhaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etadavoca – “āyāmāvuso ehi āvuso (syā. kaṃ. ka.) lakkhaṇa, rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto aññatarasmiṃ padese sitaṃ pātvākāsi. Atha kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti? “Akālo kho, āvuso lakkhaṇa, etassa pañhassa. Bhagavato maṃ santike etaṃ pañhaṃ pucchā”ti.

202. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time the Venerable Lakkhaṇa and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna were dwelling on Gijjhakūṭa mountain. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having dressed, took his bowl and robes, approached the Venerable Lakkhaṇa and said to him, “Come, friend Lakkhaṇa, let us enter Rājagaha for alms.” “Very well, friend,” the Venerable Lakkhaṇa replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Then, as the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, he smiled at a certain spot. The Venerable Lakkhaṇa then said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, “What, friend Moggallāna, is the reason, what is the cause for smiling?” “It is not the time for this question, friend Lakkhaṇa. Ask me this question in the presence of the Blessed One.”

Atha [P 2.0255] kho āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno [T 2.0299] rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “idhāyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto aññatarasmiṃ padese sitaṃ pātvākāsi. Ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti?

Then the Venerable Lakkhaṇa and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having gone for alms in Rājagaha, after the meal and having returned from the alms-round, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Lakkhaṇa said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, “Here, as the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, he smiled at a certain spot. What, friend Moggallāna, is the reason, what is the cause for smiling?”

“Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā [M 1.0447][V 1.0232] anupatitvā phāsuḷantarikāhi vitudenti vitacchenti virājenti vitudenti (sī.), vitacchenti vibhajenti (pī. ka.). Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Evarūpopi nāma satto bhavissati! Evarūpopi nāma yakkho bhavissati! Evarūpopi nāma attabhāvapaṭilābho bhavissatī’”ti!!

“Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a skeleton-chain peta going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and hawks, pursuing it again and again, were pecking, carving, and tearing it apart from between its ribs. It was uttering a cry of distress. To me, friend, this thought occurred: ‘Oh, it is indeed wonderful! Oh, it is indeed marvelous! That a being of such a nature could exist! That a yakkha of such a nature could exist! That an acquisition of an individual existence of such a nature could exist!’”

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “cakkhubhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti; ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti, yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṃ vā karissati. Pubbeva me so, bhikkhave, satto diṭṭho ahosi, api cāhaṃ na byākāsiṃ. Ahañcetaṃ ahamevetaṃ (sī.) byākareyyaṃ, pare ca me pare me (sī.) na saddaheyyuṃ. Ye me na saddaheyyuṃ, tesaṃ taṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe goghātako [T 2.0300] ahosi. So tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesena [P 2.0256] evarūpaṃ attabhāvapaṭilābhaṃ paṭisaṃvedayatī”ti. (Sabbesaṃ suttantānaṃ eseva peyyālo). Paṭhamaṃ.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, the disciples indeed dwell as those who have become the eye; monks, the disciples indeed dwell as those who have become knowledge, in that a disciple will know, or see, or bear witness to such a thing. Monks, that being was seen by me even before, but I did not declare it. And if I were to declare it, others would not believe me. For those who would not believe me, that would be for their long-term harm and suffering. This being, monks, was a cattle-butcher right here in Rājagaha. As a result of that kamma, having been tormented in hell for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years, by the remaining result of that very kamma, he experiences the acquisition of an individual existence of such a nature.” (For all the suttas, this is the refrain.) First.

2. Pesisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Lump of Flesh

203. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ maṃsapesiṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti virājenti (sī. syā. kaṃ.), vibhajenti (pī. ka.). Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe goghātako ahosi…pe…. Dutiyaṃ.

203. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a lump-of-flesh peta going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and hawks, pursuing it again and again, were carving and tearing it apart. It was uttering a cry of distress… Monks, that being was a cattle-butcher right here in Rājagaha… Second.

3. Piṇḍasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Lump of Meat

204. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ maṃsapiṇḍaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti[V 1.0233]. Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe sākuṇiko ahosi…pe…. Tatiyaṃ.

204. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a lump of meat going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and falcons, having pursued it again and again, were slicing and tearing it apart. It was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a fowler right here in Rājagaha... The third.”

4. Nicchavisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Skinless Man

205. “Idhāhaṃ[M 1.0448], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ nicchaviṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe orabbhiko ahosi…pe…. Catutthaṃ.

205. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a skinless man going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and falcons, having pursued him again and again, were slicing and tearing him apart. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a sheep butcher right here in Rājagaha... The fourth.”

5. Asilomasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Man with Sword-Hairs

206. “Idhāhaṃ[T 2.0301][P 2.0257], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ asilomaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa te asī uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe sūkariko ahosi…pe…. Pañcamaṃ.

206. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with sword-hairs going through the sky. Those swords, having risen up again and again, fall back upon his own body. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a pig butcher right here in Rājagaha... The fifth.”

6. Sattisuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Man with Spear-Hairs

207. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ sattilomaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa tā sattiyo uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe māgaviko ahosi…pe…. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

207. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with spear-hairs going through the sky. Those spears, having risen up again and again, fall back upon his own body. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a deer hunter right here in Rājagaha... The sixth.”

7. Usulomasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Man with Arrow-Hairs

208. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ usulomaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa te usū uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ [V 1.0234] karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe kāraṇiko ahosi…pe…. Sattamaṃ.

208. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with arrow-hairs going through the sky. Those arrows, having risen up again and again, fall back upon his own body. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was an executioner right here in Rājagaha... The seventh.”

8. Sūcilomasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on the Man with Needle-Hairs

209. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ sūcilomaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa tā sūciyo uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso[M 1.0449], bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe sūto sārathiko (ka. vinayepi) ahosi…pe…. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

209. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with needle-hairs going through the sky. Those needles, having risen up again and again, fall back upon his own body. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a charioteer right here in Rājagaha... The eighth.”

9. Dutiyasūcilomasuttaṃ

9. The Second Sutta on the Man with Needle-Hairs

210. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ sūcilomaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa [P 2.0258] tā sūciyo sīse pavisitvā mukhato nikkhamanti; mukhe pavisitvā urato nikkhamanti; ure pavisitvā udarato nikkhamanti; udare pavisitvā ūrūhi nikkhamanti; ūrūsu pavisitvā [T 2.0302] jaṅghāhi nikkhamanti; jaṅghāsu pavisitvā pādehi nikkhamanti; so sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe sūcako ahosi…pe…. Navamaṃ.

210. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with needle-hairs going through the sky. Those needles entered his head and came out through his mouth; entered his mouth and came out through his chest; entered his chest and came out through his belly; entered his belly and came out through his thighs; entered his thighs and came out through his shins; entered his shins and came out through his feet. He was uttering a painful cry… Monks, that being was an informer right here in Rājagaha… The ninth.”

10. Kumbhaṇḍasuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on the Man with Pot-Sized Testicles

211. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ kumbhaṇḍaṃ purisaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. So gacchantopi teva aṇḍe khandhe āropetvā gacchati. Nisīdantopi tesveva aṇḍesu nisīdati. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe gāmakūṭako ahosi…pe…. Dasamaṃ.

211. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man with pot-sized testicles going through the sky. When he walks, he does so by placing those very testicles on his shoulder. When he sits, he sits on those very testicles. Vultures, crows, and falcons, flying after him again and again, pecked at him and tore him apart. He was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that being was a fraudulent village judge right here in Rājagaha... The tenth.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 1.0235] –

The summary verse for this is:

Aṭṭhi pesi ubho gāvaghātakā,

Piṇḍo sākuṇiyo nicchavorabbhi;

Asi sūkariko sattimāgavi,

Usu kāraṇiko sūci sārathi;

Yo ca sibbiyati sūcako hi so,

Aṇḍabhāri ahu gāmakūṭakoti.

The Bone and the Flesh petas, both were cattle-slayers;

The Lump-of-Flesh peta was a bird-hunter; the Skinless peta, a sheep-butcher;

The Sword-Haired peta was a pig-butcher; the Spear-Haired peta, a deer-hunter;

The Arrow-Haired peta was an executioner; the Needle-Haired peta, a charioteer;

And he who is sewn up was the informer;

The one who carried the burden of his testicles was the fraudulent village judge.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sasīsakasuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on Being Submerged with the Head

212. Evaṃ [T 2.0303][M 1.0450][P 2.0259] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ rājagahe veḷuvane. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ purisaṃ gūthakūpe sasīsakaṃ nimuggaṃ…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe pāradāriko ahosi…pe…. Paṭhamaṃ.

212. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha at the Bamboo Grove, Veḷuvana. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man submerged along with his head in a dung pit... Monks, that being was an adulterer right here in Rājagaha... The first.”

2. Gūthakhādasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Dung-Eater

213. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ purisaṃ gūthakūpe nimuggaṃ ubhohi hatthehi gūthaṃ khādantaṃ…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe duṭṭhabrāhmaṇo ahosi. So kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane bhikkhusaṅghaṃ bhattena nimantetvā doṇiyo doṇiyā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) gūthassa pūrāpetvā etadavoca – aho bhonto, yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjantu ceva harantu cāti…pe…. Dutiyaṃ.

213. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a man submerged in a dung pit, eating dung with both hands... Monks, this being was a wicked brahmin right here in Rājagaha. In the Dispensation of Kassapa, the Perfectly Enlightened One, he invited the community of monks for a meal, had troughs filled with dung, and said this: ‘Sirs, please eat as much as you like and also take some away!’... The second.”

3. Nicchavitthisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Skinless Woman

214. “Idhāhaṃ[V 1.0236], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ nicchaviṃ itthiṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti. Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… esā, bhikkhave, itthī imasmiṃyeva rājagahe aticārinī ahosi…pe…. Tatiyaṃ.

214. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a skinless woman going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and falcons, pursuing her again and again, were carving and tearing her apart. She was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that woman was an adulteress right here in Rājagaha... The third.”

4. Maṅgulitthisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Uncomely Woman

215. “Idhāhaṃ[P 2.0260], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ itthiṃ duggandhaṃ maṅguliṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi [T 2.0304] anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti. Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… esā, bhikkhave, itthī imasmiṃyeva rājagahe ikkhaṇikā ahosi…pe…. Catutthaṃ.

215. “Friend, as I was descending from Gijjhakūṭa mountain, I saw a foul-smelling, uncomely woman going through the sky. Vultures, crows, and falcons, pursuing her again and again, were carving and tearing her apart. She was uttering a painful cry... Monks, that woman was a spirit-medium right here in Rājagaha... The fourth.”

5. Okilinīsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Woman Covered in Embers

216. “Idhāhaṃ[M 1.0451], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ itthiṃ uppakkaṃ okiliniṃ okiriniṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… esā, bhikkhave, itthī kaliṅgassa rañño aggamahesī ahosi. Sā issāpakatā sapattiṃ aṅgārakaṭāhena okiri…pe…. Pañcamaṃ.

216. “Friend Lakkhaṇa, as I was descending from Vulture's Peak Mountain, I saw a woman going through the sky, severely burnt, covered with falling embers, and strewn with charcoal. She was crying out in agony… Monks, that woman was the chief queen of the King of Kaliṅga. Overcome by jealousy, she poured a pan of embers over a co-wife… Fifth.”

6. Asīsakasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Headless One

217. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ asīsakaṃ kabandhaṃ kavandhaṃ (sī. pī.) vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa ure akkhīni ceva honti mukhañca. Tamenaṃ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṃyeva rājagahe hāriko nāma coraghātako ahosi…pe…. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

217. “Friend Lakkhaṇa, as I was descending from Vulture's Peak Mountain, I saw a headless torso going through the sky. On its chest there were eyes and a mouth. Vultures, crows, and hawks, pursuing it again and again, were carving and tearing it apart. It was crying out in agony… Monks, this being was an executioner of thieves named Hārika right here in this Rājagaha… Sixth.”

7. Pāpabhikkhusuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Wicked Monk

218. “Idhāhaṃ[V 1.0237], āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ bhikkhuṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā sampajjalitā sajotibhūtā sañjotibhūtā (syā. kaṃ.), pattopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto, kāyabandhanampi [P 2.0261] ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ, kāyopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto. So sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti…pe… eso, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane pāpabhikkhu ahosi…pe…. Sattamaṃ.

218. “Friend, as I was descending from Vulture's Peak Mountain, I saw a monk-peta going through the sky. His outer robe was on fire, blazing, and aflame; his bowl was on fire, blazing, and aflame; his waistband was on fire, blazing, and aflame; and his body was on fire, blazing, and aflame. He was uttering a cry of distress… Monks, this monk was a wicked monk in the Dispensation of the Sammāsambuddha Kassapa… Seventh.”

8. Pāpabhikkhunīsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Wicked Nun

219. “Addasaṃ [T 2.0305] bhikkhuniṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tassā saṅghāṭipi ādittā…pe… pāpabhikkhunī ahosi…pe…. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

219. “I saw a nun-peta going through the sky. Her outer robe was on fire… She was a wicked nun… Eighth.”

9. Pāpasikkhamānasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Wicked Probationary Nun

220. “Addasaṃ [M 1.0452] sikkhamānaṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tassā saṅghāṭipi ādittā…pe… pāpasikkhamānā ahosi…pe…. Navamaṃ.

220. “I saw a probationary nun-peta going through the sky. Her outer robe was on fire… She was a wicked probationary nun… Ninth.”

10. Pāpasāmaṇerasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Wicked Male Novice

221. “Addasaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantaṃ. Tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā…pe… pāpasāmaṇero ahosi…pe…. Dasamaṃ.

221. “I saw a male novice-peta going through the sky. His outer robe was on fire… He was a wicked male novice… Tenth.”

11. Pāpasāmaṇerīsuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Wicked Female Novice

222. “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṃ sāmaṇeriṃ vehāsaṃ gacchantiṃ. Tassā saṅghāṭipi ādittā sampajjalitā sajotibhūtā, pattopi āditto sampajjalito [V 1.0238] sajotibhūto, kāyabandhanampi ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ, kāyopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto. Sā sudaṃ aṭṭassaraṃ karoti. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Evarūpopi nāma satto bhavissati! Evarūpopi nāma yakkho bhavissati! Evarūpopi nāma attabhāvapaṭilābho bhavissatī’”ti!!

222. “Friend, as I was descending from Vulture's Peak Mountain, I saw a female novice-peta going through the sky. Her outer robe was on fire, blazing, and aflame; her bowl was on fire, blazing, and aflame; her waistband was on fire, blazing, and aflame; and her body was on fire, blazing, and aflame. She was uttering a cry of distress. Then, friend, this thought occurred to me: ‘Sirs, it is truly amazing! Sirs, it is truly wonderful! That a being of such a nature could exist! That a yakkha of such a nature could exist! That the acquisition of an individual existence of such a nature could exist!’”

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “cakkhubhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti; ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti, yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṃ vā karissati. Pubbeva [P 2.0262] me sā, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī diṭṭhā ahosi. Api cāhaṃ na byākāsiṃ. Ahañcetaṃ byākareyyaṃ, pare ca me na saddaheyyuṃ. Ye me na saddaheyyuṃ, tesaṃ taṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya [T 2.0306] dukkhāya. Esā, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane pāpasāmaṇerī ahosi. Sā tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesena evarūpaṃ attabhāvapaṭilābhaṃ paṭisaṃvedayatī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Truly, monks, the disciples dwell as those who have become the eye; truly, monks, the disciples dwell as those who have become knowledge, inasmuch as a disciple might know, see, or bear witness to such a being. Monks, that female novice-peta was seen by me even before, but I did not declare it. If I were to declare it, others would not believe my words. For those who would not believe my words, that would be for their long-term harm and suffering. This female novice-peta, monks, was a wicked female novice in the Dispensation of the Sammāsambuddha Kassapa. Through the result of that kamma, for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years, she was tormented in hell. Then, through the residual result of that very kamma, she experiences the acquisition of such an individual existence.” Eleventh.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Kūpe [M 1.0453] nimuggo hi so pāradāriko;

Gūthakhādi ahu duṭṭhabrāhmaṇo.

Immersed in a cesspool was that adulterer; a filth-eater was the wicked brahmin.

Nicchavitthi aticārinī ahu;

Maṅgulitthi ahu ikkhaṇitthikā.

The skinless woman was an adulteress; the ill-favored woman was a sorceress.

Okilini sapattaṅgārokiri;

Sīsacchinno ahu coraghātako.

The one covered with embers had poured coals on a co-wife; the beheaded one was an executioner of thieves.

Bhikkhu [V 1.0239] bhikkhunī sikkhamānā;

Sāmaṇero atha sāmaṇerikā.

A monk, a nun, a probationary nun; a male novice, and then a female novice.

Kassapassa vinayasmiṃ pabbajjaṃ;

Pāpakammaṃ kariṃsu tāvadeti.

Having gone forth in the Dispensation of Kassapa, these many performed wicked deeds.

Lakkhaṇasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Lakkhaṇa Saṃyutta is concluded.

9. Opammasaṃyuttaṃ

9. The Connected Discourses on Similes

1. Kūṭasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Peak

223. Evaṃ [T 2.0307][V 1.0240][M 1.0454] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra [P 2.0263] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo sabbā tā kūṭaṅgamā kūṭasamosaraṇā kūṭasamugghātā sabbā tā samugghātaṃ gacchanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci akusalā dhammā sabbe te avijjāmūlakā avijjāsamosaraṇā avijjāsamugghātā, sabbe te samugghātaṃ gacchanti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘appamattā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

223. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks.” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Monks, just as in a peaked house, whatever rafters there are, they all lead to the peak, converge on the peak, and incline towards the peak. Even so, monks, whatever unwholesome qualities there are, they are all rooted in ignorance, converge on ignorance, and incline towards ignorance. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell heedfully.’ Thus, indeed, monks, should you train yourselves.” First.

2. Nakhasikhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Fingernail Tip

224. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsuṃ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ, yo vāyaṃ yo cāyaṃ (bahūsu) mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito ayaṃ vā yā cāyaṃ (syā. ka.) mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ yadidaṃ mahāpathavī. Appamattakoyaṃ bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito. Saṅkhampi na upeti upanidhimpi na upeti kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteyeva bahutarā sattā ye aññatra manussehi paccājāyanti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ [T 2.0308] – ‘appamattā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

224. Dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the Blessed One, having placed a little dust on the tip of his fingernail, addressed the monks: “What do you think, monks? Which is more: this little dust I have placed on the tip of my fingernail, or the great earth?” “Venerable sir, the great earth is far more. The little dust the Blessed One has placed on the tip of his fingernail is insignificant. When compared with the great earth, it does not amount to a calculation, nor to a comparison, nor even to a fraction.” “Just so, monks, few are the beings reborn among humans; far more numerous are those reborn elsewhere than among humans. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell heedfully.’ Thus should you train yourselves.”

3. Kulasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Families

225. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0241] viharati…pe… “seyyathāpi[P 2.0264], bhikkhave, yāni kānici kulāni bahutthikāni appapurisāni tāni suppadhaṃsiyāni honti corehi kumbhatthenakehi[M 1.0455]; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno mettācetovimutti abhāvitā abahulīkatā so suppadhaṃsiyo hoti amanussehi. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici kulāni appitthikāni bahupurisāni tāni duppadhaṃsiyāni honti corehi kumbhatthenakehi, evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno mettācetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā so duppadhaṃsiyo hoti amanussehi. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettā no cetovimutti bhāvitā bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

225. Dwelling at Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, just as any families with many women and few men are easily plundered by housebreakers; even so, bhikkhus, any bhikkhu whose liberation of mind by loving-kindness is undeveloped and uncultivated is easily overcome by non-human beings. Just as any families with few women and many men are hard to plunder by housebreakers; even so, any bhikkhu whose liberation of mind by loving-kindness is developed and cultivated is hard to overcome by non-human beings. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘Our liberation of mind by loving-kindness will be developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, made a basis, established, made familiar, and well undertaken.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.”

4. Okkhāsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Cauldrons

226. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “yo, bhikkhave, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ okkhāsataṃ dānaṃ dadeyya, yo majjhanhikasamayaṃ okkhāsataṃ dānaṃ dadeyya, yo sāyanhasamayaṃ okkhāsataṃ dānaṃ dadeyya, yo vā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ antamaso gadduhanamattampi mettacittaṃ bhāveyya, yo vā majjhanhikasamayaṃ antamaso gadduhanamattampi mettacittaṃ bhāveyya, yo [T 2.0309] vā sāyanhasamayaṃ antamaso gadduhanamattampi mettacittaṃ bhāveyya, idaṃ tato mahapphalataraṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettā no cetovimutti bhāvitā bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Catutthaṃ.

226. At Sāvatthī… “Bhikkhus, if someone were to give a gift of a hundred cauldrons in the morning, a gift of a hundred cauldrons at noon, and a gift of a hundred cauldrons in the evening; and if someone else were to develop a mind of loving-kindness in the morning, even for the time it takes to milk a cow, or were to develop a mind of loving-kindness at noon, even for the time it takes to milk a cow, or were to develop a mind of loving-kindness in the evening, even for the time it takes to milk a cow—this would be far more fruitful than that. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘Our liberation of mind through loving-kindness will be developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, made familiar, and well undertaken.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.”

5. Sattisuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Spear

227. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 2.0265] viharati…pe… “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, satti tiṇhaphalā. Atha puriso āgaccheyya – ‘ahaṃ imaṃ sattiṃ tiṇhaphalaṃ pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇissāmi paṭikoṭṭissāmi paṭivaṭṭessāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, bhabbo nu kho so puriso amuṃ sattiṃ tiṇhaphalaṃ pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇetuṃ paṭikoṭṭetuṃ paṭivaṭṭetu”nti? “No hetaṃ[V 1.0242], bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Asu hi, bhante, satti tiṇhaphalā na sukarā pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇetuṃ paṭikoṭṭetuṃ paṭivaṭṭetuṃ. Yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā”ti.

227. At Sāvatthī… “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a sharp-pointed spear. Then a man would come thinking, ‘I will bend, crush, or twist this sharp-pointed spear with my hand or fist.’ What do you think, bhikkhus, would that man be able to bend, crush, or twist that sharp-pointed spear with his hand or fist?” “No, venerable sir.” “For what reason?” “Because, venerable sir, that sharp-pointed spear is not easy to bend, crush, or twist with the hand or fist. That man would only partake of weariness and vexation.”

“Evameva [M 1.0456] kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno mettācetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, tassa ce amanusso cittaṃ khipitabbaṃ maññeyya; atha kho sveva amanusso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assa. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettā no cetovimutti bhāvitā bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā [T 2.0310] paricitā susamāraddhā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“So too, bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu for whom the liberation of mind through loving-kindness is developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, made familiar, and well undertaken, should a non-human being think of assailing his mind, that very non-human being would become a partaker of weariness and vexation. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘Our liberation of mind through loving-kindness will be developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, made familiar, and well undertaken.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.”

6. Dhanuggahasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Archer

228. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cattāro daḷhadhammā dhanuggahā [P 2.0266] susikkhitā katahatthā katūpāsanā catuddisā ṭhitā assu. Atha puriso āgaccheyya – ‘ahaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ daḷhadhammānaṃ dhanuggahānaṃ susikkhitānaṃ katahatthānaṃ katūpāsanānaṃ catuddisā kaṇḍe khitte appatiṭṭhite pathaviyaṃ gahetvā āharissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, ‘javano puriso paramena javena samannāgato’ti alaṃ vacanāyā”ti?

228. He was dwelling in Sāvatthī... 'Suppose, bhikkhus, there were four strong-bow archers—well-trained, with practiced hands, and accomplished—standing in the four directions. Then a man might come and say, ‘I will catch and bring back the arrows shot towards the four directions by these four strong-bow archers—well-trained, with practiced hands, and accomplished—before they fall to the ground.’ What do you think, bhikkhus? Is it fit to say, ‘This is a swift man, endowed with supreme speed’?'

“Ekassa cepi, bhante, daḷhadhammassa dhanuggahassa susikkhitassa katahatthassa katūpāsanassa kaṇḍaṃ khittaṃ appatiṭṭhitaṃ pathaviyaṃ gahetvā āhareyya – ‘javano puriso paramena javena samannāgato’ti alaṃ vacanāya, ko pana vādo catunnaṃ daḷhadhammānaṃ dhanuggahānaṃ susikkhitānaṃ katahatthānaṃ katūpāsanāna”nti?

‘Venerable Sir, even if he were to catch and bring back an arrow shot by a single strong-bow archer—well-trained, with practiced hands, and accomplished—before it fell to the ground, it is fit to say, ‘This is a swift man, endowed with supreme speed.’ What then is to be said of four strong-bow archers—well-trained, with practiced hands, and accomplished?’

“Yathā ca, bhikkhave, tassa purisassa javo, yathā ca candimasūriyānaṃ javo, tato sīghataro. Yathā ca, bhikkhave, tassa purisassa javo yathā ca candimasūriyānaṃ javo yathā ca yā devatā candimasūriyānaṃ purato dhāvanti tāsaṃ devatānaṃ javo, ( ) (tato sīghataro. yathā ca bhikkhave tassa purisassa javo, yathā ca candimasuriyānaṃ javo, yathā ca yā devatā candimasuriyānaṃ purato dhāvanti, tāsaṃ devatānaṃ javo,) (sī. syā. kaṃ.) tato sīghataraṃ āyusaṅkhārā [V 1.0243] khiyanti. Tasmātiha[T 2.0311], bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘appamattā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, as is the speed of that man, and as is the speed of the moon and sun—there is that which is swifter. Bhikkhus, as is the speed of that man, as is the speed of the moon and sun, and as is the speed of those deities who run before the moon and sun—the life-formations waste away even swifter than that. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘We will dwell heedfully.’ Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The Sixth.

7. Āṇisuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Peg

229. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0457] viharati…pe… “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, dasārahānaṃ ānako āṇako (sī.) nāma mudiṅgo ahosi. Tassa dasārahā ānake ghaṭite aññaṃ āṇiṃ odahiṃsu. Ahu [P 2.0267] kho so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṃ ānakassa mudiṅgassa porāṇaṃ pokkharaphalakaṃ antaradhāyi. Āṇisaṅghāṭova avasissi. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṃ, ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatappaṭisaṃyuttā, tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsissanti na sotaṃ odahissanti na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpessanti na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbaṃ maññissanti”.

229. He was dwelling in Sāvatthī... “Bhikkhus, formerly, the Dasārahās had a drum named Ānaka. When it was damaged, they inserted another peg. There came a time, bhikkhus, when the original drumhead-plank of the Ānaka drum disappeared, and only the collection of pegs remained. So too, bhikkhus, in a future time there will be bhikkhus who, when those suttantas spoken by the Tathāgata—deep, deep in meaning, supramundane, connected with emptiness—are being recited, will not want to listen, will not lend an ear, will not apply their minds to understanding, and will not consider those teachings fit to be learned and mastered.”

“Ye pana te suttantā kavikatā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā, tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissanti, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpessanti, te ca dhamme uggahetabbaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbaṃ maññissanti. Evametesaṃ, bhikkhave, suttantānaṃ tathāgatabhāsitānaṃ gambhīrānaṃ gambhīratthānaṃ lokuttarānaṃ suññatappaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ antaradhānaṃ bhavissati. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatappaṭisaṃyuttā, tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsissāma, sotaṃ odahissāma[T 2.0312], aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpessāma, te ca dhamme uggahetabbaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbaṃ maññissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“But as for those suttantas that are made by poets, poetic, with embellished words and phrases, external, spoken by disciples—when these are being recited, they will want to listen, they will lend an ear, they will apply their minds to understanding, and they will consider those teachings fit to be learned and mastered. In this way, bhikkhus, the disappearance of those suttantas spoken by the Tathāgata—deep, deep in meaning, supramundane, connected with emptiness—will come about. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘When those suttantas spoken by the Tathāgata—deep, deep in meaning, supramundane, connected with emptiness—are being recited, we will want to listen, we will lend an ear, we will apply our minds to understanding, and we will consider those teachings fit to be learned and mastered.’ Thus, bhikkhus, should you train.” The Seventh.

8. Kaliṅgarasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Block of Wood

230. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

230. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Gabled Hall. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” they replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Kaliṅgarūpadhānā[V 1.0244], bhikkhave, etarahi licchavī viharanti [P 2.0268] appamattā ātāpino upāsanasmiṃ. Tesaṃ rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto na labhati otāraṃ na labhati ārammaṇaṃ. Bhavissanti, bhikkhave[M 1.0458], anāgatamaddhānaṃ licchavī sukhumālā sukumālā (sī.), sukhumā (ka.) mudutalunahatthapādā mudutalāhatthapādā (syā. kaṃ.) te mudukāsu seyyāsu tūlabimbohanāsu tūlabimbohanāsu (syā. kaṃ. pī.), tūlabimbohanādīsu (sī.), tūlabibbohanādīsu (ka.) yāvasūriyuggamanā seyyaṃ kappissanti. Tesaṃ rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto lacchati otāraṃ lacchati ārammaṇaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, at present the Licchavis dwell using wooden blocks as pillows, diligent and ardent in their training. King Ajātasattu of Magadha, the son of the Videhan queen, does not gain an opening, does not gain a foothold against them. But in the future, bhikkhus, the Licchavis will be delicate, with soft and tender hands and feet. They will sleep on soft beds with cotton pillows until sunrise. Then King Ajātasattu of Magadha, the son of the Videhan queen, will gain an opening, will gain a foothold against them.

“Kaliṅgarūpadhānā, bhikkhave, etarahi bhikkhū viharanti appamattā ātāpino padhānasmiṃ. Tesaṃ māro pāpimā na labhati otāraṃ na labhati ārammaṇaṃ. Bhavissanti, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ bhikkhū sukhumā mudutalunahatthapādā. Te mudukāsu seyyāsu tūlabimbohanāsu yāvasūriyuggamanā seyyaṃ kappissanti. Tesaṃ māro pāpimā lacchati otāraṃ lacchati ārammaṇaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ [T 2.0313] sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘kaliṅgarūpadhānā viharissāma appamattā ātāpino padhānasmi’nti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, at present the bhikkhus dwell using wooden blocks as pillows, diligent and ardent in striving. Māra the Evil One gains no opening, gains no foothold against them. But in the future, bhikkhus, there will be bhikkhus who are delicate, with soft and tender hands and feet. They will sleep on soft beds with cotton pillows until sunrise. Then Māra the Evil One will gain an opening, will gain a foothold against them. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell using wooden blocks as pillows, diligent and ardent in striving.’ That is how you should train yourselves.” The Eighth.

9. Nāgasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Bull Elephant

231. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro navo bhikkhu ativelaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamati. Tamenaṃ bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “māyasmā ativelaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamī”ti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi vuccamāno evamāha – “ime hi nāma therā bhikkhū kulāni upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññissanti, kimaṅgaṃ kimaṅga (sī.) panāha”nti?

231. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time a certain junior bhikkhu was visiting families at an improper time. The bhikkhus said to him: “Venerable, do not visit families at an improper time.” But when he was told this by the bhikkhus, that bhikkhu said: “These elder bhikkhus must think it is allowable to visit families, so what about me?”

Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ [P 2.0269] nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, aññataro navo bhikkhu ativelaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamati. Tamenaṃ bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – ‘māyasmā ativelaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamī’ti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi vuccamāno evamāha – ‘ime hi nāma therā bhikkhū kulāni upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññissanti, kimaṅgaṃ panāha’”nti.

Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, here a certain junior bhikkhu visits families at an improper time. The bhikkhus told him: ‘Venerable, do not visit families at an improper time.’ But when told this by the bhikkhus, that bhikkhu replied: ‘These elder bhikkhus must think it is allowable to visit families, so what about me?’”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ[V 1.0245][M 1.0459], bhikkhave, araññāyatane mahāsarasī. Taṃ nāgā upanissāya viharanti. Te taṃ sarasiṃ ogāhetvā soṇḍāya bhisamuḷālaṃ abbuhetvā abbhūhetvā (ka.), abbāhitvā (mahāva. 278) suvikkhālitaṃ vikkhāletvā akaddamaṃ saṅkhāditvā saṅkharitvā (pī. ka.) ajjhoharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ vaṇṇāya ceva hoti balāya ca, na ca tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tesaṃyeva [T 2.0314] kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānāgānaṃ anusikkhamānā taruṇā bhiṅkacchāpā taṃ sarasiṃ ogāhetvā soṇḍāya bhisamuḷālaṃ abbuhetvā na suvikkhālitaṃ vikkhāletvā sakaddamaṃ asaṅkhāditvā ajjhoharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ neva vaṇṇāya hoti na balāya. Tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.

“Once in the past, bhikkhus, in a forest wilderness there was a great lake. Bull elephants lived in dependence on it. They would enter that lake, pull up lotus stalks and roots with their trunks, and having washed them well, making them free of mud, and having chewed them, they would swallow them. For them, this was for the sake of both beauty and strength, and on account of that, they did not meet with death or suffering comparable to death. But then, bhikkhus, young elephant calves, imitating those great bull elephants, would enter that lake, pull up lotus stalks and roots with their trunks, and without washing them well and without chewing them, they would swallow them along with the mud. For them, this was for the sake of neither beauty nor strength, and on account of that, they met with death or suffering comparable to death.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idha therā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisanti. Te tattha dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Tesaṃ gihī pasannākāraṃ karonti. Te taṃ lābhaṃ agadhitā amucchitā anajjhopannā anajjhāpannā (sabbattha) ma. ni. 1 pāsarāsisuttavaṇṇanā oloketabbā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti. Tesaṃ taṃ vaṇṇāya ceva hoti balāya ca, na ca tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tesaṃyeva kho pana, bhikkhave, therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anusikkhamānā navā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisanti. Te tattha dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Tesaṃ gihī pasannākāraṃ [P 2.0270] karonti. Te taṃ lābhaṃ gadhitā mucchitā ajjhopannā anādīnavadassāvino anissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti. Tesaṃ taṃ neva vaṇṇāya hoti na balāya, te tatonidānaṃ maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘agadhitā amucchitā anajjhopannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā taṃ lābhaṃ paribhuñjissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti[T 2.0315]. Navamaṃ.

“Just so, bhikkhus, here the elder bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, take their bowls and robes and enter a village or town for alms. There they speak the Dhamma. The householders show their confidence. They partake of that gain ungreedy, uninfatuated, unentangled, seeing the danger, and with the wisdom of escape. For them, this is for the sake of both beauty and strength, and on account of that, they do not meet with death or with suffering comparable to death. But then, bhikkhus, the junior bhikkhus, imitating those elder bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, take their bowls and robes and enter a village or town for alms. There they speak the Dhamma. The householders show their confidence. They partake of that gain while being greedy, infatuated, entangled, not seeing the danger, and without the wisdom of escape. For them, this is for the sake of neither beauty nor strength, and on account of that, they meet with death or with suffering comparable to death. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will partake of that gain ungreedy, uninfatuated, unentangled, seeing the danger, and with the wisdom of escape.’ That is how you should train yourselves.”

10. Biḷārasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Cat

232. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ativelaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati. Tamenaṃ bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “māyasmā ativelaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjī”ti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi vuccamāno na viramati. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[M 1.0460]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, aññataro bhikkhu ativelaṃ [V 1.0246] kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjati. Tamenaṃ bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – ‘māyasmā ativelaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjī’ti. So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi vuccamāno na viramatī”ti.

232. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was frequenting families for too long a time. The bhikkhus said to him: “Venerable, do not frequent families for too long a time.” But that bhikkhu, though spoken to by the bhikkhus, did not desist. Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, a certain bhikkhu is frequenting families for too long a time. The bhikkhus said to him: ‘Venerable, do not frequent families for too long a time.’ But that bhikkhu, though spoken to by the bhikkhus, does not desist.”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, biḷāro sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīre ṭhito ahosi mudumūsiṃ maggayamāno – ‘yadāyaṃ mudumūsi gocarāya pakkamissati, tattheva naṃ gahetvā khādissāmī’ti. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mudumūsi gocarāya pakkāmi. Tamenaṃ biḷāro gahetvā sahasā saṅkhāditvā saṅkharitvā (pī. ka.), maṃsaṃ khāditvā (syā. kaṃ.), asaṃkhāditvā (katthaci) ajjhohari. Tassa so mudumūsi antampi khādi, antaguṇampi khādi. So tatonidānaṃ [P 2.0271] maraṇampi nigacchi maraṇamattampi dukkhaṃ.

“Once in the past, bhikkhus, a cat stood by a junction of drains and a refuse heap, seeking a tender mouse, thinking: ‘When this tender mouse comes out to forage, I will catch it right there and eat it.’ Then, bhikkhus, that tender mouse came out to forage. The cat, having caught it, swiftly crunched it up and swallowed it. That tender mouse bit the cat's large intestine and its small intestine. On account of that, the cat met with death or suffering comparable to death.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisati arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya arakkhitena cittena, anupaṭṭhitāya [T 2.0316] satiyā, asaṃvutehi indriyehi. So tattha passati mātugāmaṃ dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā. Tassa mātugāmaṃ disvā dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. So rāgānuddhaṃsena cittena maraṇaṃ vā nigacchati maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Maraṇañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye yo sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati. Maraṇamattañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ yadidaṃ aññataraṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Yathārūpāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyati. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘rakkhiteneva kāyena rakkhitāya vācāya rakkhitena cittena, upaṭṭhitāya satiyā, saṃvutehi indriyehi gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dasamaṃ.

“In the same way, bhikkhus, here a certain bhikkhu, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms with an unguarded body, unguarded speech, and an unguarded mind, with mindfulness unestablished and faculties unrestrained. There he sees a woman improperly dressed or improperly covered. Upon seeing the woman improperly dressed or improperly covered, lust destroys his mind. With his mind destroyed by lust, he meets with death or suffering comparable to death. Bhikkhus, this is death in the discipline of the Noble One: when one renounces the training and reverts to the lower life. And bhikkhus, this is suffering comparable to death: when one commits some defiled offense from which rehabilitation is recognized. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will enter a village or town for alms with a guarded body, guarded speech, and a guarded mind, with mindfulness established and faculties restrained.’ Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.”

11. Siṅgālasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Jackal

233. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ jarasiṅgālassa vassamānassā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Eso kho, bhikkhave, jarasiṅgālo ukkaṇḍakena nāma rogajātena phuṭṭho. So yena [M 1.0461] yena icchati tena tena gacchati; yattha yattha icchati tattha tattha tiṭṭhati; yattha yattha icchati tattha tattha nisīdati; yattha yattha icchati [P 2.0272] tattha tattha nipajjati; sītakopi naṃ vāto upavāyati. Sādhu khvassa, bhikkhave, yaṃ idhekacco sakyaputtiyapaṭiñño evarūpampi attabhāvapaṭilābhaṃ paṭisaṃvediyetha. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave[V 1.0247], evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ [T 2.0317] – ‘appamattā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Ekādasamaṃ.

233. At Sāvatthī…. “Bhikkhus, did you hear the old jackal howling at dawn?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, that old jackal is afflicted by a disease called Ukkaṇḍaka. He goes wherever he wishes; he stands wherever he wishes; he sits wherever he wishes; he lies down wherever he wishes; the cold wind also blows upon him. It would be good, bhikkhus, if a certain one here who professes to be a son of the Sakyans were to experience the attainment of even such an existence. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell heedfully.’ Thus indeed, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.”

12. Dutiyasiṅgālasuttaṃ

12. The Second Discourse on the Jackal

234. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… “assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ jarasiṅgālassa vassamānassā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Siyā kho, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ jarasiṅgāle yā kāci kataññutā kataveditā, na tveva idhekacce sakyaputtiyapaṭiññe siyā yā kāci kataññutā kataveditā. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘kataññuno bhavissāma katavedino; na ca no na ca noti idaṃ sī. pī. potthakesu natthi amhesu appakampi kataṃ nassissatī’ti mā nassissatīti (sī. pī.), vinassissatīti (syā. kaṃ.). Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dvādasamaṃ.

234. At Sāvatthī…. “Bhikkhus, did you hear the old jackal howling at dawn?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, there might be some gratitude and thankfulness in that old jackal, but there might not be any gratitude or thankfulness in a certain one here who professes to be a son of the Sakyans. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will be grateful and thankful; and not even a small deed done for us will be lost.’ Thus indeed, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.”

Opammasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Similes is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Kūṭaṃ nakhasikhaṃ kulaṃ, okkhā satti dhanuggaho;

Āṇi kaliṅgaro nāgo, biḷāro dve siṅgālakāti.

The Peak, the Fingernail, the Family, the Torch, the Spear, the Archer; the Linchpin, the Log, the Elephant, the Cat, and the two Jackals.

10. Bhikkhusaṃyuttaṃ

10. The Connected Discourses with Bhikkhus

1. Kolitasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse concerning Kolita

235. Evaṃ [T 2.0318][V 1.0248][P 2.0273][M 1.0462] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosuṃ.

235. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna.

Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, āvuso, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘ariyo tuṇhībhāvo, ariyo tuṇhībhāvoti vuccati. Katamo nu kho ariyo tuṇhībhāvo’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati ariyo tuṇhībhāvo’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihariṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato vitakkasahagatā saññā manasikārā samudācaranti”.

The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this: “Here, friends, while I was in seclusion, withdrawn, this thought arose in my mind: ‘The noble silence, the noble silence, it is said. Now what is the noble silence?’ Then, friends, it occurred to me: ‘Here, with the stilling of applied thought and sustained thought, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and is born of concentration, with rapture and pleasure. This is called the noble silence.’ So, friends, with the stilling of applied thought and sustained thought, I entered and dwelled in the second jhāna... As I was dwelling in this state, friends, perceptions and instances of attention accompanied by applied thought arose in me.”

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna, mā, brāhmaṇa, ariyaṃ tuṇhībhāvaṃ pamādo, ariye tuṇhībhāve cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, ariye tuṇhībhāve cittaṃ ekodibhāvaṃ karohi, ariye tuṇhībhāve cittaṃ [T 2.0319] samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Yañhi [V 1.0249] taṃ, āvuso[P 2.0274], sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārā anuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’ti, mamaṃ taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārā anuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by means of spiritual power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna, brahmin, do not be heedless of the noble silence! Establish your mind in the noble silence, make your mind one-pointed in the noble silence, concentrate your mind in the noble silence.’ So, friends, on a later occasion, with the stilling of applied thought and sustained thought... I am dwelling in the second jhāna. Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say: ‘A disciple assisted by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, should say this: ‘A disciple assisted by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge.’”

2. Upatissasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Upatissa

236. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0463] viharati. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

236. At Sāvatthī. There the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus, saying: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Idha mayhaṃ, āvuso, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘atthi nu kho taṃ kiñci lokasmiṃ yassa me vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘natthi kho taṃ kiñci lokasmiṃ yassa me vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’”ti.

“Here, friends, while I was in seclusion, withdrawn, this reflection arose in my mind: ‘Is there anything at all in the world whose alteration and change would cause sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair to arise in me?’ Then, friends, it occurred to me: ‘There is nothing at all in the world whose alteration and change would cause sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair to arise in me.’”

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “satthupi kho te, āvuso sāriputta, vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti? “Satthupi kho me, āvuso, vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, api ca me evamassa – ‘mahesakkho vata, bho, satthā [T 2.0320] antarahito mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo. Sace hi bhagavā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Tathā [P 2.0275] hi panāyasmato sāriputtassa dīgharattaṃ ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā susamūhatā. Tasmā āyasmato sāriputtassa satthupi vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, even regarding the Teacher, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair not arise in you due to his alteration and change?” “Friend, even regarding the Teacher, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would not arise in me due to his alteration and change. But it would occur to me thus: ‘Alas, the Teacher—of great majesty, great psychic power, and great might—has passed away! Indeed, if the Blessed One were to remain for a long, long time, that would be for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.’ For a long time the underlying tendencies of I-making, mine-making, and conceit have been thoroughly uprooted in the Venerable Sāriputta. Therefore, for the Venerable Sāriputta, even regarding the Teacher, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would not arise due to his alteration and change.”

3. Ghaṭasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Jar

237. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno [V 1.0250] rājagahe viharanti veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe ekavihāre. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ [M 1.0464] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca –

237. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. At that time the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna were dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground, in a single dwelling. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta rose from his solitude and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. After concluding their courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:

“Vippasannāni kho te, āvuso moggallāna, indriyāni; parisuddho mukhavaṇṇo pariyodāto santena nūnāyasmā mahāmoggallāno ajja vihārena vihāsī”ti. “Oḷārikena khvāhaṃ, āvuso, ajja vihārena vihāsiṃ. Api ca, me ahosi dhammī kathā”ti. “Kena saddhiṃ panāyasmato mahāmoggallānassa ahosi dhammī kathā”ti? “Bhagavatā [T 2.0321] kho me, āvuso, saddhiṃ ahosi dhammī kathā”ti. “Dūre kho, āvuso, bhagavā etarahi sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Kiṃ nu kho, āyasmā, mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṃ iddhiyā upasaṅkami; udāhu bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ iddhiyā upasaṅkamī”ti? “Na [P 2.0276] khvāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavantaṃ iddhiyā upasaṅkamiṃ; napi maṃ bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkami. Api ca, me yāvatā bhagavā ettāvatā dibbacakkhu visujjhi dibbā ca sotadhātu. Bhagavatopi yāvatāhaṃ ettāvatā dibbacakkhu visujjhi dibbā ca sotadhātū”ti. “Yathākathaṃ panāyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhagavatā saddhiṃ ahosi dhammī kathā”ti?

“Friend Moggallāna, your faculties are clear; your complexion is pure and bright. Surely the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna has spent the day in a peaceful abiding.” “Friend, I have been dwelling with a coarse abiding today. However, I had a Dhamma talk.” “With whom did the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna have a Dhamma talk?” “I had a Dhamma talk with the Blessed One, friend.” “But friend, the Blessed One is now far away, dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Did the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna approach the Blessed One by psychic power, or did the Blessed One approach the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna by psychic power?” “I did not approach the Blessed One by psychic power, friend, nor did the Blessed One approach me by psychic power. However, my divine eye and divine ear element are purified for the range extending to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One’s divine eye and divine ear element are purified for the range extending to me.” “But of what nature was the Dhamma talk between the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and the Blessed One?”

“Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘āraddhavīriyo āraddhavīriyoti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, āraddhavīriyo hotī’ti? Evaṃ vutte, maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā etadavoca – ‘idha, moggallāna, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati – kāmaṃ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhī ca avasissatu, sarīre upasussatu maṃsalohitaṃ, yaṃ taṃ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṃ na taṃ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṃ bhavissatīti. Evaṃ kho, moggallāna, āraddhavīriyo hotī’ti. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, bhagavatā saddhiṃ ahosi dhammī kathā”ti.

“Here, friend, I said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, it is said, “one with aroused energy, one with aroused energy.” To what extent, venerable sir, is one with aroused energy?’ When this was said, friend, the Blessed One said this to me: ‘Here, Moggallāna, a bhikkhu dwells with aroused energy, resolved: “Let only skin, sinews, and bones remain, and let the flesh and blood dry up in my body; there will be no stopping of my energy until I have attained what can be attained by human strength, human energy, and human effort.” It is in this way, Moggallāna, that one has aroused energy.’ This, friend, was the Dhamma talk I had with the Blessed One.”

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, himavato pabbatarājassa parittā pāsāṇasakkharā [T 2.0322] yāvadeva upanikkhepanamattāya[V 1.0251]; evameva kho mayaṃ āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa yāvadeva upanikkhepanamattāya. Āyasmā hi mahāmoggallāno mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti.

“Just as, friend, compared to the Himalayas, the king of mountains, a few small pebbles would be for the sake of comparison only; so too, compared to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, are we for the sake of comparison only. For the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna is of great psychic power and great might; if he so wished, he could remain for an aeon.”

“Seyyathāpi[M 1.0465], āvuso, mahatiyā loṇaghaṭāya parittā loṇasakkharāya yāvadeva upanikkhepanamattāya; evameva kho mayaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa yāvadeva upanikkhepanamattāya. Āyasmā [P 2.0277] hi sāriputto bhagavatā anekapariyāyena thomito vaṇṇito pasattho –

“Just as, friend, compared to a great salt pot, a few small salt crystals would be for the sake of comparison only; so too, compared to the Venerable Sāriputta, are we for the sake of comparison only. For the Venerable Sāriputta has been praised, extolled, and commended by the Blessed One in many ways:

“Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena ca;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā”ti.

‘Sāriputta is supreme in wisdom, virtue, and peacefulness; any bhikkhu who has gone to the far shore would be, at most, his equal.’”

Itiha te ubho mahānāgā aññamaññassa subhāsitaṃ sulapitaṃ samanumodiṃsūti. Tatiyaṃ.

Thus those two great beings rejoiced in each other’s well-spoken words.

4. Navasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the New Monk

238. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro navo bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto vihāraṃ pavisitvā appossukko tuṇhībhūto saṅkasāyati, na bhikkhūnaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ karoti cīvarakārasamaye. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha[T 2.0323], bhante, aññataro navo bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto vihāraṃ pavisitvā appossukko tuṇhībhūto saṅkasāyati, na bhikkhūnaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ karoti cīvarakārasamaye”ti.
