238. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Now at that time, a certain new monk, having returned from the alms-round after the meal, entered the monastery and remained unconcerned and silent. At the time of making robes, he did not perform service for the monks. Then a number of monks approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, a certain new monk, having returned from the alms-round after the meal, entered the monastery and remained unconcerned and silent. At the time of making robes, he does not perform service for the monks.”

Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena taṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantehi ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso, āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “satthā taṃ, āvuso, āmantetī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho so bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi[V 1.0252]. Ekamantaṃ [P 2.0278] nisinnaṃ kho taṃ bhikkhuṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto vihāraṃ pavisitvā appossukko tuṇhībhūto saṅkasāyasi, na bhikkhūnaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ karosi cīvarakārasamaye”ti? “Ahampi kho, bhante, sakaṃ kiccaṃ karomī”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: “Come, bhikkhu, by my word call that monk, saying, ‘The Teacher calls you, friend.’” “Yes, venerable sir,” that monk replied to the Blessed One, and he approached that other monk. Having approached, he said this to that monk: “The Teacher calls you, friend.” “Yes, friend,” that monk replied to the other, and he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to that monk sitting to one side: “Is it true, bhikkhu, that after returning from the alms-round after the meal and entering the monastery, you remain unconcerned and silent, and do not perform service for the monks at the time of making robes?” “I too, venerable sir, am doing my own duty.”

Atha [M 1.0466] kho bhagavā tassa bhikkhuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya bhikkhū āmantesi – “mā kho tumhe, bhikkhave, etassa bhikkhuno ujjhāyittha. Eso kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā [T 2.0324] sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the mental reflection of that monk, addressed the monks: “Monks, do not find fault with this monk. This monk, monks, is an obtainer at will, without trouble, and without difficulty of the four jhānas, which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant dwellings in this very life. And that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness—this he has realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, and having attained it, he dwells therein.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Nayidaṃ sithilamārabbha, nayidaṃ appena thāmasā;

Nibbānaṃ adhigantabbaṃ, sabbadukkhappamocanaṃ.

“Not with slack endeavor, not with little strength, is Nibbāna to be attained, the release from all suffering.”

“Ayañca daharo bhikkhu, ayamuttamapuriso;

Dhāreti antimaṃ dehaṃ, jetvā māraṃ savāhini”nti. catutthaṃ;

“And this monk is young, yet he is a supreme person; having conquered Māra along with his army, he bears his final body.” The fourth.

5. Sujātasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Sujāta

239. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha kho āyasmā sujāto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sujātaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “ubhayenevāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kulaputto sobhati – yañca [P 2.0279] abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato, yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjanti tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

239. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sujāta approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sujāta coming from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, this clansman is beautiful in both ways: he is handsome, attractive, inspiring confidence, possessing supreme beauty of complexion; and he dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.” The Blessed One said this… The Teacher said:

“Sobhati [V 1.0253] vatāyaṃ bhikkhu, ujubhūtena cetasā;

Vippayutto visaṃyutto, anupādāya nibbuto;

Dhāreti antimaṃ dehaṃ, jetvā māraṃ savāhini”nti. pañcamaṃ;

“Truly shines this bhikkhu, with a mind that has become straight; disassociated, unfettered, extinguished without grasping; he bears his final body, having conquered Māra with his army.”

6. Lakuṇḍakabhaddiyasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya

240. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0325][M 1.0467] viharati. Atha kho āyasmā lakuṇḍakabhaddiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ lakuṇḍakabhaddiyaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ āgacchantaṃ dubbaṇṇaṃ duddasikaṃ okoṭimakaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paribhūtarūpa”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Eso kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, na ca sā samāpatti sulabharūpā yā tena bhikkhunā asamāpannapubbā. Yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

240. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya coming from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, do you see that bhikkhu coming who is ugly, unpleasant to behold, dwarfish, and of a form despised by the bhikkhus?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is of great psychic power and great majesty. There is no meditative attainment that has not been previously attained by him. He dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.” The Blessed One said this… The Teacher said:

“Haṃsā koñcā mayūrā ca, hatthayo pasadā migā;

Sabbe sīhassa bhāyanti, natthi kāyasmiṃ tulyatā.

“Geese, herons, and peacocks, elephants and spotted deer—all fear the lion; there is no equality in body.”

“Evameva manussesu, daharo cepi paññavā;

So hi tattha mahā hoti, neva bālo sarīravā”ti. chaṭṭhaṃ;

“Even so among humans, though one be young, if he is wise, he is indeed great among them; but the fool with a large body is not.”

7. Visākhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Visākha

241. Evaṃ [P 2.0280] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā visākho pañcālaputto upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti, poriyā vācāya vissaṭṭhāya [T 2.0326] anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā pariyāpannāya anissitāya.

241. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. At that time, in the attendance hall, the Venerable Visākha Pañcālaputta was instructing, causing to undertake, inciting, and gladdening the monks with a Dhamma talk, with speech that was urbane, clear, faultless, that conveyed the meaning, was pertinent, and unattached.

Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [V 1.0254] paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ko nu kho, bhikkhave, upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti poriyā vācāya vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā pariyāpannāya anissitāyā”ti? “Āyasmā, bhante, visākho [M 1.0468] pañcālaputto upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti, poriyā vācāya vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā pariyāpannāya anissitāyā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, in the evening, having risen from seclusion, approached the attendance hall. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Seated, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Who now, monks, in the attendance hall, is instructing, causing to undertake, inciting, and gladdening the monks with a Dhamma talk, with speech that is urbane, clear, faultless, that conveys the meaning, is pertinent, and unattached?' 'Venerable sir, it is the Venerable Visākha Pañcālaputta who, in the attendance hall, is instructing, causing to undertake, inciting, and gladdening the monks with a Dhamma talk, with speech that is urbane, clear, faultless, that conveys the meaning, is pertinent, and unattached.'

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ visākhaṃ pañcālaputtaṃ āmantesi – “sādhu sādhu, visākha, sādhu kho tvaṃ, visākha, bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi…pe… atthassa viññāpaniyā pariyāpannāya anissitāyā”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Visākha Pañcālaputta: 'Good, good, Visākha! It is good, Visākha, that you instruct the monks with a Dhamma talk that conveys the meaning, is included within the scope of the truths, and is unattached.'

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Nābhāsamānaṃ jānanti, missaṃ bālehi paṇḍitaṃ;

Bhāsamānañca jānanti, desentaṃ amataṃ padaṃ.

They do not know the wise one who does not speak, when he is mixed with fools. But they know him when he speaks, teaching the deathless state.

“Bhāsaye jotaye dhammaṃ, paggaṇhe isinaṃ dhajaṃ;

Subhāsitadhajā isayo, dhammo hi isinaṃ dhajo”ti. sattamaṃ;

Let one speak and illuminate the Dhamma, let him raise the banner of the seers. The seers have the well-spoken as their banner; for the Dhamma is indeed the banner of the seers.

8. Nandasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Nanda

242. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 2.0327][P 2.0281] viharati. Atha kho āyasmā nando bhagavato mātucchāputto ākoṭitapaccākoṭitāni cīvarāni pārupitvā akkhīni añjetvā acchaṃ pattaṃ gahetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ nandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “na kho te taṃ, nanda, patirūpaṃ kulaputtassa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitassa, yaṃ tvaṃ ākoṭitapaccākoṭitāni cīvarāni pārupeyyāsi, akkhīni ca añjeyyāsi, acchañca pattaṃ dhāreyyāsi. Etaṃ kho te, nanda, patirūpaṃ kulaputtassa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitassa, yaṃ tvaṃ āraññiko [V 1.0255] ca assasi, piṇḍapātiko ca paṃsukuliko ca kāmesu ca anapekkho vihareyyāsī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

242. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Nanda, the son of the Blessed One's maternal aunt, having put on robes that were pressed and re-pressed, having anointed his eyes, and taking a clear bowl, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said to the Venerable Nanda as he was sitting to one side: 'It is not proper for you, Nanda, a clansman who has gone forth in faith from the household life into homelessness, that you should wear robes that are pressed and re-pressed, anoint your eyes, and carry a clear bowl. This is proper for you, Nanda, a clansman who has gone forth in faith from the household life into homelessness: that you should be a forest-dweller, an alms-food-eater, a rag-robe-wearer, and should dwell unconcerned with sensual pleasures.' The Blessed One said this... the Teacher...

“Kadāhaṃ nandaṃ passeyyaṃ, āraññaṃ paṃsukūlikaṃ;

Aññātuñchena yāpentaṃ, kāmesu anapekkhina”nti.

When shall I see Nanda, a forest-dweller, a rag-robe-wearer, sustaining himself on mixed alms, unconcerned with sensual pleasures?

Atha [M 1.0469] kho āyasmā nando aparena samayena āraññiko ca piṇḍapātiko ca paṃsukūliko ca kāmesu ca anapekkho vihāsīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

Then, at a later time, the Venerable Nanda lived as a forest-dweller, an alms-food-eater, a rag-robe-wearer, and unconcerned with sensual pleasures. The eighth.

9. Tissasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Tissa

243. Sāvatthiyaṃ viharati. Atha [P 2.0282] kho āyasmā tisso bhagavato pitucchāputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[T 2.0328]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi dukkhī dummano assūni pavattayamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ tissaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho tvaṃ, tissa, ekamantaṃ nisinno dukkhī dummano assūni pavattayamāno”ti? “Tathā hi pana maṃ, bhante, bhikkhū samantā vācāsannitodakena vācāya sannitodakena (ka.) sañjambharimakaṃsū”ti sañjabbharimakaṃsūti (?). “Tathāhi pana tvaṃ, tissa, vattā no ca vacanakkhamo; na kho te taṃ, tissa, patirūpaṃ kulaputtassa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitassa, yaṃ tvaṃ vattā no ca vacanakkhamo. Etaṃ kho te, tissa, patirūpaṃ kulaputtassa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitassa – ‘yaṃ tvaṃ vattā ca assa vacanakkhamo cā’”ti.

243. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Tissa, the son of the Blessed One's paternal aunt, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side, distressed and dejected, shedding tears. Then the Blessed One said to the Venerable Tissa: "Why, Tissa, are you sitting to one side, distressed and dejected, shedding tears?" "Because, venerable sir, the monks on all sides have incessantly pierced me with words like spear-thrusts." "Indeed, Tissa, you are one who speaks, but you are not one who can endure speech. It is not fitting for you, Tissa, a clansman who has gone forth out of faith from the household life into homelessness, that you are one who speaks but are not one who can endure speech. This is fitting for you, Tissa, a clansman who has gone forth out of faith from the household life into homelessness: that you should be one who speaks and also one who can endure speech."

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Kiṃ nu kujjhasi mā kujjhi, akkodho tissa te varaṃ;

Kodhamānamakkhavinayatthañhi, tissa brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti. navamaṃ;

Why are you angry? Do not be angry, Tissa; non-anger is superior for you. Indeed, Tissa, the holy life is lived for the purpose of subduing anger, conceit, and denigration.

10. Theranāmakasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Elder

244. Ekaṃ [V 1.0256] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu theranāmako ekavihārī ceva hoti ekavihārassa ca vaṇṇavādī. So eko gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisati eko paṭikkamati eko raho nisīdati eko caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[T 2.0329]; [P 2.0283] upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho [M 1.0470] te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, aññataro bhikkhu theranāmako ekavihārī ekavihārassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

244. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time, a certain monk named Thera was a solitary dweller and also one who spoke in praise of solitary dwelling. He would enter a village for alms alone, return alone, sit in seclusion alone, and undertake walking meditation alone. Then a number of monks approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, here a certain monk named Thera is a solitary dweller and also one who speaks in praise of solitary dwelling."

Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena theraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso thera, āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā thero tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “satthā taṃ, āvuso thera, āmantetī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā thero tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ theraṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, thera, ekavihārī ekavihārassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, thera, ekavihārī ekavihārassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, bhante, eko gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisāmi eko paṭikkamāmi eko raho nisīdāmi eko caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhāmi. Evaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, ekavihārī ekavihārassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: "Come, monk, with my word call the monk Thera, saying: ‘Friend Thera, the Teacher calls you.’" "Very well, venerable sir," that monk replied to the Blessed One, and he approached the Venerable Thera and said to him: "Friend Thera, the Teacher calls you." "Very well, friend," the Venerable Thera replied to that monk. Then he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. To the Venerable Thera, sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: "Is it true, Thera, as is said, that you are a solitary dweller and one who speaks in praise of solitary dwelling?" "Indeed, venerable sir." "But in what way, Thera, are you a solitary dweller and one who speaks in praise of solitary dwelling?" "Here, venerable sir, I enter a village for alms alone, I return alone, I sit in seclusion alone, and I undertake walking meditation alone. In this way, venerable sir, I am a solitary dweller and one who speaks in praise of solitary dwelling."

“Attheso, thera, ekavihāro neso natthīti vadāmi. Api ca, thera, yathā ekavihāro vitthārena paripuṇṇo hoti taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho…pe…. “Kathañca[T 2.0330], thera, ekavihāro vitthārena paripuṇṇo hoti. Idha, thera, yaṃ atītaṃ taṃ pahīnaṃ, yaṃ anāgataṃ taṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, paccuppannesu ca attabhāvapaṭilābhesu chandarāgo suppaṭivinīto. Evaṃ kho, thera, ekavihāro vitthārena paripuṇṇo hotī”ti.

“Thera, there is one who dwells alone; I do not say that there is not. However, Thera, listen and pay careful attention as to how dwelling alone is fulfilled in detail; I will speak.” “Very well, venerable sir.” … “And how, Thera, is dwelling alone fulfilled in detail? Here, Thera, what is past has been abandoned, what is future has been relinquished, and desire and lust for present acquisitions of individual existence are well-subdued. In this way, Thera, dwelling alone is fulfilled in detail.”

Idamavoca [P 2.0284] bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Sabbābhibhuṃ [V 1.0257] sabbaviduṃ sumedhaṃ,

Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalittaṃ;

Sabbañjahaṃ taṇhākkhaye vimuttaṃ,

Tamahaṃ naraṃ ekavihārīti brūmī”ti. dasamaṃ;

“The one who has overcome all, the all-knower, the wise, unstained by all phenomena, who has abandoned all, liberated in the destruction of craving—that person I call one who dwells alone.”

11. Mahākappinasuttaṃ

11. The Mahākappina Sutta

245. Sāvatthiyaṃ [M 1.0471] viharati. Atha kho āyasmā mahākappino yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahākappinaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha no tumhe bhikkhave, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ āgacchantaṃ odātakaṃ tanukaṃ tuṅganāsika”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Eso kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo. Na ca sā samāpatti sulabharūpā yā tena bhikkhunā asamāpannapubbā. Yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ [T 2.0331] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.

245. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Mahākappina approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw the Venerable Mahākappina coming from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, do you see that bhikkhu coming, who is fair, slender, and has a prominent nose?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “This bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is of great psychic power and great might. And there is no easily obtainable attainment that has not been previously attained by that bhikkhu. For the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness—that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life—he dwells having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life and having attained it.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse.

“The khattiya is best among people who are concerned with lineage; one endowed with knowledge and conduct is best among gods and humans.”

“Divā tapati ādicco, rattimābhāti candimā;

Sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo;

Atha sabbamahorattiṃ atha sabbamahorattaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), buddho tapati tejasā”ti. ekādasamaṃ;

“The sun shines by day, the moon illumines the night; the khattiya shines in armor, the brahmin shines in jhāna; but the Buddha shines with splendor all day and night.”

12. Sahāyakasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Companions

246. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 2.0285] viharati. Atha kho dve bhikkhū sahāyakā āyasmato mahākappinassa saddhivihārino yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasā kho bhagavā te bhikkhū dūratova [V 1.0258] āgacchante. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, ete bhikkhū sahāyake āgacchante kappinassa saddhivihārino”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Ete kho te bhikkhū mahiddhikā mahānubhāvā. Na ca sā samāpatti sulabharūpā, yā tehi bhikkhūhi asamāpannapubbā. Yassa catthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā [T 2.0332] upasampajja viharantī”ti.

246. He was dwelling at Sāvatthī. Then two bhikkhus who were companions and co-residents of the Venerable Mahākappina approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw those bhikkhus coming from afar. Having seen them, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, do you see those companion bhikkhus coming, the co-residents of Kappina?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “These bhikkhus are of great psychic power and great might. And there is no easily obtainable attainment that has not been previously attained by those bhikkhus. For the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness—that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life—they dwell having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life and having attained it.”

Idamavoca [M 1.0472] bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Sahāyā vatime bhikkhū, cirarattaṃ sametikā;

Sameti nesaṃ saddhammo, dhamme buddhappavedite.

“Indeed, these bhikkhus are companions, for a long time united. Their good Dhamma is in harmony with the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha.”

“Suvinītā kappinena, dhamme ariyappavedite;

Dhārenti antimaṃ dehaṃ, jetvā māraṃ savāhini”nti. dvādasamaṃ;

“Well-trained by Kappina in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble One, they bear their final body, having conquered Māra with his army.”

Bhikkhusaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Bhikkhus is complete.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Kolito upatisso ca, ghaṭo cāpi pavuccati;

Navo [P 2.0286] sujāto bhaddi ca, visākho nando tisso ca;

Theranāmo ca kappino, sahāyena ca dvādasāti.

Kolita and Upatissa, and Ghaṭa is also spoken of; Nava, Sujāta, and Bhaddiya, Visākha, Nanda, and Tissa; the one named Thera, and Kappina, and with the Companion, make twelve.

Nidānavaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on Causation, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Nidānābhisamayadhātu, anamataggena kassapaṃ;

Sakkārarāhulalakkhaṇo, opamma-bhikkhunā vaggo.

Nidāna, Abhisamaya, Dhātu, Anamatagga, and Kassapa; Sakkāra, Rāhula, Lakkhaṇa, Opamma, and Bhikkhu.

Dutiyo tena pavuccatīti.

Thus it is called the second.

Nidānavaggasaṃyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Connected Discourses of the Nidāna Vagga is finished.
